result.family: Boolean combinators and conditionals (allOf / anyOf / oneOf / not / if-then-else, plus draft-03 extends/disallow and dependentSchemas/contains touchpoints)
result.findings:
FILE: /workspace/probes/combinators.jsonl (193 vectors, 16 of them crash cases with exit=1). All outputs captured by running the real binary via node execFileSync.

THE CENTRAL RULE (flatten vs collapse). jsonschema keyword implementations either (a) DESCEND — i.e. `yield from validator.descend(instance, subschema, schema_path=...)`, re-yielding every child error unchanged so each child error becomes its own TOP-LEVEL error; or (b) COLLAPSE — build exactly one ValidationError whose `context` holds the children (context does NOT add to the top-level count). Observed classification:
- DESCEND (flatten, N children => N top-level errors): allOf, then, else, properties, patternProperties, additionalProperties, items, prefixItems, dependentSchemas, dependencies(schema form), $ref, draft-03 `extends`.
- COLLAPSE (always exactly 1 top-level error when it fails, 0 when it passes): anyOf, oneOf, not, contains, draft-03 `disallow`, draft-03 `type` when given an array of schemas.
Flattening composes multiplicatively through descending keywords: `{"items":{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0},{"type":"number"}]}}` on `["a","a"]` => 6 errors (3 per item). `{"properties":{"x":{"properties":{"y":{"properties":{"z":{"allOf":[3 failing]}}}}}}}` => 3. But a COLLAPSE keyword anywhere on the path caps the subtree at 1: `{"anyOf":[{"allOf":[2 failing]}]}` => 1; `{"oneOf":[{"allOf":[2 failing]},{"type":"number"}]}` => 1; `{"not":{"anyOf":[...]}}` => 1.

allOf. `{"allOf":[{"type":"number"},{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]}` on "ab" => False/3 (one per failing branch). `{"allOf":[]}` => True/0. `{"allOf":[true,false,false]}` => False/2 (each `false` subschema yields its own top-level error). `{"allOf":[false]}` => False/1. Nested allOf flattens fully: `{"allOf":[{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]},{"type":"number"}]}` => 3. A single allOf branch with multiple failing keywords contributes one error per failing keyword: `{"allOf":[{"properties":{"x":{"type":"number"},"y":{"type":"number"}}},{"properties":{"x":{"minLength":9}}}]}` on {"x":"a","y":"a"} => 3.

anyOf. Fails => exactly 1 error regardless of branch count or of how many errors each branch produced. `{"anyOf":[{"type":"number"},{"minLength":9}]}` => 1. `{"anyOf":[]}` => False/1 (empty anyOf is a FAILURE, unlike empty allOf). `{"anyOf":[false,false]}` => 1. `{"anyOf":[true]}` => True/0. `{"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"number"}]}` => True/0 (short-circuits on first match).

oneOf. Exactly 1 error in both failure modes. 0 matches: `{"oneOf":[{"type":"number"},{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]}` => 1 ("is not valid under any of the given schemas"). 2+ matches: `{"oneOf":[{"type":"string"},{"minLength":1}]}` => 1, `{"oneOf":[true,true]}` => 1, `{"oneOf":[{},{},{}]}` (3 matches) => 1. `{"oneOf":[]}` => False/1. `{"oneOf":[{}]}` => True/0. `{"oneOf":[true,false]}` => True/0.

not. Always exactly 1 error when the subschema matches. `{"not":{"type":"string"}}` on "ab" => 1. `{"not":{}}` => 1. `{"not":true}` => 1. `{"not":false}` => True/0. `{"not":{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0}]}}` => True/0 (subschema fails, so not passes). `{"not":{"not":{"type":"number"}}}` => 1. The number of errors the negated subschema would have produced is irrelevant.

if/then/else. Only exists in Draft7, 2019-09, 2020-12. In Draft3/4/6 the keywords `if`, `then`, `else` are COMPLETELY IGNORED (unknown keywords): `{"$schema":draft-06,"if":{"type":"string"},"then":false}` => True/0, while draft-07 => False/1. `then` and `else` DESCEND, so the chosen branch's errors are flattened: `{"if":{"type":"string"},"then":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}}` on "ab" => 2; `{"if":{"type":"number"},"else":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}}` => 2; on instance 5, `{"if":{"type":"number"},"then":{"minimum":10,"maximum":1,"multipleOf":7}}` => 3. `if` alone (no then/else) never produces an error: `{"if":{"type":"string"}}` => True/0. `then`/`else` WITHOUT `if` are ignored entirely: `{"then":{"minLength":9},"else":{"maxLength":1}}` => True/0 — critically, this means `then`/`else` are NOT standalone keywords; they are only reachable from `if`. Only one branch is evaluated: `{"if":{"type":"string"},"then":true,"else":false}` => True/0. Boolean `if` works: `{"if":true,"then":{"minLength":9}}` => 1; `{"if":false,"else":{"minLength":9}}` => 1. The unused branch is never even looked at, so a MALFORMED unused branch does not crash: `{"if":{"type":"string"},"else":1}` => True/0 and `{"if":{"type":"number"},"then":1}` => True/0, whereas `{"if":{"type":"string"},"then":1}` CRASHES. Nested if/then: `{"if":{"type":"string"},"then":{"if":{"minLength":1},"then":{"maxLength":0,"pattern":"^z"}}}` on "ab" => 2 (inner then flattens through outer then). if/then inside allOf flattens: `{"allOf":[{"if":..,"then":{"minLength":9}},{"if":..,"then":{"maxLength":0}}]}` => 2. if/then inside anyOf/not collapses to 1/0.

DRAFT-03 IS THE BIG SPECIAL CASE. Draft3Validator has NO allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if, then, else — all six are silently ignored. `{"$schema":draft-03,"allOf":[{"type":"number"}],"anyOf":[{"type":"number"}],"oneOf":[],"not":{},"if":{},"then":{"type":"number"}}` on "ab" => True/0. Its analogs instead: `extends` DESCENDS and accepts either a single schema or an array of schemas — `{"extends":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}}` => 2, `{"extends":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]}` => 2. `disallow` COLLAPSES to 1 error (`{"disallow":"string"}` => 1, `{"disallow":["string","number"]}` => 1, `{"disallow":[{"minLength":1}]}` => 1). Draft-03 `type` given an array of subschemas is the anyOf analog and collapses to 1: `{"type":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]}` => 1. `extends` is draft-03 only; in draft-04 `{"extends":{"minLength":9}}` => True/0 (ignored).

Draft-04 through 2020-12 behave IDENTICALLY for allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not, including boolean subschemas (`{"allOf":[true,false,false]}` => 2 even under Draft4Validator, which historically had no boolean schemas). No draft-to-draft count differences were observed anywhere except (a) draft-03's total absence of these keywords and (b) if/then/else being draft-07+.

RELATED CONDITIONAL KEYWORDS. `dependentSchemas` (2019-09+) DESCENDS: `{"dependentSchemas":{"a":{"minProperties":9,"maxProperties":0}}}` on {"a":1} => 2. Draft-07 `dependencies` with a schema value likewise DESCENDS => 2. `contains` COLLAPSES: `{"contains":{"type":"string"}}` on [1,2] => 1. In 2019-09, `if`/`then` and `anyOf` DO contribute annotations for `unevaluatedProperties`: `{"properties":{"a":{}},"if":{"properties":{"a":{}}},"then":{"properties":{"b":{}}},"unevaluatedProperties":false}` on {"a":1,"b":2} => True/0, and `{"anyOf":[{"properties":{"b":{}}}],"properties":{"a":{}},"unevaluatedProperties":false}` => True/0, while dropping the combinator gives False/1.

SIBLING KEYWORDS ADD INDEPENDENTLY. Errors from combinators sum with sibling keyword errors at the same level: `{"type":"number","allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0}]}` on "ab" => 3; `{"minLength":9,"allOf":[{"maxLength":0}],"anyOf":[{"type":"number"}],"oneOf":[],"not":{}}` => 5 (1 minLength + 1 allOf-descended + 1 anyOf + 1 oneOf + 1 not). `{"anyOf":[{"type":"string"}],"minLength":9}` => 1 (anyOf passes, minLength fails).

$ref is transparent to counting: `{"$ref":"#/$defs/a","$defs":{"a":{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0}]}}}` => 2, and `{"allOf":[{"$ref":"#/$defs/a"}],"$defs":{"a":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":0}}}` => 2.

CRASH BEHAVIOR (exit code 1, Python traceback on stderr, NOTHING on stdout — the three print lines never execute because is_valid() raises first). Observed crashes, all with exit=1:
- Non-list values for allOf/anyOf/oneOf whose iteration yields non-dict/non-bool elements: `{"allOf":{"type":"number"}}`, `{"anyOf":{"type":"number"}}`, `{"oneOf":{"a":{"type":"number"}}}` (dict iterates to its string keys), `{"oneOf":"x"}`, `{"allOf":"ab"}` (string iterates to chars) => AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get' at referencing/jsonschema.py _dollar_id.
- Non-iterable values: `{"allOf":0}`, `{"allOf":null}`, `{"anyOf":true}` => exit 1 (TypeError, not iterable).
- Non-schema ELEMENTS: `{"allOf":[null]}` => AttributeError 'NoneType' has no attribute 'get'; `{"allOf":[1]}` => 'int' object has no attribute 'get'; `{"anyOf":[null]}` same.
- `not` with a non-dict/non-bool: `{"not":[{"type":"number"}]}` => AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'items' (in Validator.__attrs_post_init__); `{"not":null}` / `{"not":1}` => TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType'/'int' is not iterable (in validator_for).
- `{"if":1,"then":{...}}` => TypeError not iterable (validator_for, evaluating `if`); `{"if":{"type":"string"},"then":1}` => AttributeError 'int' has no attribute 'get' (descend into `then`) — but only when the branch is actually taken.
NOT crashes (empty iterables): `{"allOf":""}` => True/0, `{"allOf":{}}` => True/0 (zero subschemas => vacuously valid), while `{"anyOf":""}`, `{"anyOf":{}}`, `{"oneOf":{}}` => False/1 (zero subschemas => nothing matched).
gotchas: allOf DESCENDS (N failing branches => N top-level errors, and each branch's own multiple keyword failures each count too), while anyOf/oneOf/not/contains COLLAPSE to exactly 1 error with children in .context. Implementers who make all combinators collapse (or all flatten) get counts wrong everywhere.
Empty combinator arrays diverge: {"allOf":[]} => valid/0 errors, but {"anyOf":[]} and {"oneOf":[]} => INVALID with exactly 1 error.
oneOf yields exactly 1 error for BOTH failure modes: 0 matches and 2+ matches (even 3 matches => 1). Do not emit one error per extra match.
then/else DESCEND, so a then-branch with 3 failing keywords produces 3 TOP-LEVEL errors, not 1. This is the most commonly mis-implemented count.
then and else without a sibling `if` are completely ignored (0 errors) — they are not standalone keywords; the if_ handler is the only thing that reaches them.
`if` alone (no then/else) never produces an error, even when it fails. It is only an annotation/selector.
if/then/else do NOT exist before draft-07. Draft3/4/6 silently ignore them; {"$schema":draft-06,"if":{"type":"string"},"then":false} is VALID while draft-07 gives 1 error.

Draft-03 has NONE of allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not/if/then/else — all are ignored, so a schema of pure combinators is vacuously valid under Draft3Validator. Its analogs are `extends` (descends, accepts schema or array of schemas), `disallow` (collapses to 1), and `type` with an array containing subschemas (collapses to 1). `extends` is ignored in draft-04+.
Boolean subschemas work inside combinators in EVERY draft including draft-04: {"allOf":[true,false,false]} => 2 errors under Draft4Validator. Don't gate boolean subschema support on draft>=6.
{"not":false} is VALID (0 errors) and {"not":true} / {"not":{}} are INVALID (1 error) — easy to invert.

A collapsing keyword anywhere on the path caps the whole subtree at 1 error: {"anyOf":[{"allOf":[2 failing]}]} => 1, not 2. Flattening only multiplies through chains of descending keywords (properties/items/prefixItems/allOf/then/else/$ref/dependentSchemas).

Malformed combinator values CRASH with exit=1 and NO stdout at all (not even the validator class name), because is_valid() raises before the prints. Distinguish: {"allOf":""} and {"allOf":{}} do NOT crash (empty iteration => valid), {"allOf":"ab"} and {"allOf":{"type":"number"}} DO crash (iterating a str/dict yields strings, which are not schemas), and {"allOf":0}/{"allOf":null}/{"anyOf":true} crash as non-iterable.

`if`/`then`/`else` are evaluated lazily: a malformed UNTAKEN branch does not crash. {"if":{"type":"number"},"then":1} on a string is VALID/0, but {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":1} on a string CRASHES.
Combinator errors sum with sibling keyword errors at the same schema level; there is no short-circuiting between keywords.
In 2019-09+, if/then and anyOf branches DO contribute successful-property annotations consumed by unevaluatedProperties, so a passing combinator branch can make unevaluatedProperties:false pass.

result.findings:
FILE: /workspace/probes/string.jsonl (481 vectors, each {"a","b","out","exit"}). Generators: /workspace/gen.js, /workspace/gen2.js.

TYPE GATING (all string keywords): minLength, maxLength, pattern, format, content* are ALL no-ops unless the instance is a JSON string. Non-string instances (number, bool, null, array, object) always give True/0, and — critically — the gate happens BEFORE any coercion or regex compilation, so `{"pattern":"["}` or `{"pattern":123}` or `{"minLength":"bogus"}` against instance `5` returns "Draft202012Validator/True/0" with exit 0 instead of crashing. Booleans are NOT treated as strings.

minLength / maxLength — CODE POINT semantics, not UTF-16 units. jsonschema uses Python len(), i.e. Unicode scalar count. Verified: "😀" (U+1F600) has length 1 → maxLength:1 passes, minLength:2 fails. "😀😀" length 2. "a😀b" length 3 (maxLength:3 ok, maxLength:2 fails). Flag "🇺🇸" (2 regional indicators) length 2. ZWJ family "👩‍👩‍👧" length 5 (2 ZWJ + 3 emoji), maxLength:5 passes, maxLength:4 fails, maxLength:8 passes. U+10FFFF length 1. A JS implementation MUST use [...str].length / Array.from, never str.length. Combining marks each count: precomposed "é" (U+00E9) = 1; decomposed "e"+U+0301 = 2 (maxLength:1 FAILS, minLength:2 PASSES); "Å" decomposed = 2 vs precomposed = 1; Hangul "가" precomposed = 1 vs jamo-composed = 2; Devanagari "क्ष" = 3. NO Unicode normalization is applied anywhere.
Comparison is `len(s) < minLength` and `len(s) > maxLength` (strict), so equality passes: len 3 with minLength:3 or maxLength:3 → True. minLength:0 and maxLength:0 on "" → True; maxLength:0 on "abc" → False. Empty string with minLength:1 → 1 error.
Bound value is used raw as a Python number, so non-integer JSON numbers work: minLength:3.5 on "abc" → False (3 < 3.5); maxLength:2.5 on "abc" → False; maxLength:0.5 on "" → True; minLength:0.5 on "" → False; minLength:2.0000001 on "ab" → False; minLength:2.0/3.0 behave like 2/3. Negative bounds: minLength:-1 → always True; maxLength:-1 → always False. JSON booleans are Python ints: minLength:true == 1, minLength:false == 0 (both pass "abc"); maxLength:true == 1 → False on "abc"; maxLength:false == 0 → False on "abc". Huge ints (1e20 written as integer) work fine → False.
CRASH: a non-numeric minLength/maxLength raises TypeError only when the instance IS a string — `{"minLength":"5"}` / `{"maxLength":"1"}` / `{"minLength":null}` / `{"minLength":[5]}` / `{"maxLength":{}}` → exit 1, EMPTY stdout, traceback `jsonschema/_keywords.py ... TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'str'`.
Each of minLength and maxLength yields at most ONE error; both failing simultaneously yields exactly 2 top-level errors (identical across all six drafts).

pattern — Python `re.search` (SUBSTRING SEARCH, not full match), with re.UNICODE implicitly on, and NO other flags. "abc" vs "b" → valid; vs "^b" → invalid; vs "c$" → valid; vs "^abc$" → valid; "abcd" vs "^abc$" → invalid. Empty pattern "" matches everything including "".
Python `$` semantics differ from a naive port: `$` matches at end OR immediately before a single trailing "\n". "abc\n" vs "^abc$" → VALID; "abc\n\n" vs "^abc$" → invalid; "abc\r" and "abc\r\n" vs "^abc$" → INVALID (only \n, not \r). `\Z` is absolute end: "abc\n" vs "\Aabc\Z" or "abc\Z" → invalid. `\A` supported. `^` matches only at string start by default (no MULTILINE): "a\nb" vs "^b$" invalid, but "(?m)^b$" valid. `.` excludes \n by default: "a\nb" vs "a.b" invalid, "(?s)a.b" valid.
Python-only regex constructs that WORK: named groups `(?P<name>...)`, named backrefs `(?P=x)`, numeric backrefs `\1`, comments `(?#...)`, inline flags at pattern start `(?i)` `(?m)` `(?s)` `(?x)` `(?a)` `(?u)` and combos, scoped flags `(?i:...)` and `(?-i:...)`, non-capturing `(?:)`, lookahead `(?=)`/`(?!)`, lookbehind `(?<=)`/`(?<!)`, atomic groups `(?>a*)` and possessive quantifiers `a*+` (Python 3.11+; "aaa" vs "^(?>a*)a$" → invalid, correctly atomic), `\N{LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A}`, octal `\141`, `\x61`, `a`, `\U0001F600`, `\a`, `\b` word boundary, empty alternatives `a|` and `|a`.
Regex is applied to the Python str, i.e. per CODE POINT, so `.` matches a whole astral char: "😀" vs "^.$" → VALID, vs "^..$" → invalid; "😀😀" vs "^..$" → valid; "🇺🇸" vs "^..$" valid; ZWJ family vs "^.....$" valid. Decomposed "é" vs "^.$" invalid, "^..$" valid.
Unicode class semantics (Python re defaults to UNICODE for str): `\d` MATCHES Arabic-Indic "١٢٣" and Devanagari "१२३" (Nd category), but NOT superscript "²" (No). `[0-9]` does not match "١٢٣". `\w` matches accented letters ("café" precomposed, "Ünïcödé", "naïve"), CJK "日本語", Arabic-Indic digits, "²", circled "①", and "_", but does NOT match a bare combining acute U+0301 (Mn) nor emoji ("😀" is `\W`). Consequence: decomposed "café" fails `^\w{4}$` (5 code points, U+0301 not \w) while precomposed "café" passes; "café"(decomposed) vs `^\w{4}.$` passes. `\s` matches ASCII space/\t/\n/\v(U+000B)/U+001C(FS)/NBSP U+00A0/EM SPACE U+2003/LINE SEPARATOR U+2028/IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE U+3000, but NOT ZERO WIDTH SPACE U+200B. `\b` is unicode-aware ("café" vs "\bcafé\b" valid); "xabcx" vs "\babc\b" invalid, "x abc x" valid. `(?a)` restricts to ASCII: "é" fails `(?a)^\w+$`, "١٢" fails `(?a)^\d+$`.
`(?i)` uses Python's simple case-insensitive matching, not full casefold: "ß" vs "(?i)^SS$" → INVALID, but "K" (KELVIN SIGN U+212A) vs "(?i)^k$" → valid and "İ" (U+0130) vs "(?i)^i$" → valid.
POSIX bracket classes are NOT special: "abc" vs "[[:alpha:]]+" compiles fine (as a char set plus literal "]") and is INVALID (no error, just no match).
CRASHES (exit 1, EMPTY stdout, traceback from re/_parser.py or re/__init__.py), only reached when the instance is a string: "[" (unterminated character set), "(unclosed", ")", "a{2,1}" (min repeat greater than max), "*", "a**", "\\" (bad escape at end), "(?P<1bad>a)", "(?<name>a)" (.NET-style named group), "a|*", "(?P<x>a)(?P<x>b)" (redefinition), "\\p{L}+" (bad escape \p), "abc(?(1)x)" (invalid group reference / unknown group), "\\Q abc \\E" (bad escape \Q), "(?L)^\\w+$" (cannot use LOCALE flag with a str pattern), and — Python 3.11+ — global inline flags not at pattern start: "^(?i)x$" and "a(?i)bc". A non-string pattern value (`123`, `null`, `["a"]`, `true`) → `TypeError: first argument must be string or compiled pattern` from re/__init__.py. `patternProperties` with key "[" also crashes (exit 1) whenever an object instance is validated.
Compilation is LAZY / instance-driven: `{"properties":{"y":{"pattern":"["}}}` is fine for `{"x":1}` and for `{"y":5}` but crashes for `{"y":"s"}`; `{"anyOf":[{"pattern":"["},{"type":"integer"}]}` is fine for `5` but crashes for a string even inside anyOf/not/if (the exception escapes the anyOf/not/if error-collection machinery — it is NOT swallowed into context).
pattern yields at most ONE error.

format — NOT ASSERTED in any draft. Zero format checkers are enabled (the script constructs `validator_class(schema)` with no `format_checker`). Every one of email, idn-email, date-time, date, time, duration, ipv4, ipv6, uuid, uri, uri-reference, iri, hostname, idn-hostname, json-pointer, relative-json-pointer, regex, uri-template with the blatantly invalid value "!!!definitely-not-valid!!!" returns True/0. Swept across draft-03/04/06/07/2019-09/2020-12: all True/0. Even declaring `$vocabulary: {".../vocab/format-assertion": true}` in a 2020-12 schema does NOT turn on assertion. `format` with a non-string value (123, null) or an unknown name is silently ignored, no crash.

contentEncoding / contentMediaType / contentSchema — NOT ASSERTED in any draft; pure annotations. "!!!not-base64!!!" with contentEncoding:"base64" → True/0 in all six drafts. "notjson" with contentMediaType:"application/json" → True/0. contentSchema is never evaluated: `{"contentMediaType":"application/json","contentSchema":{"type":"array"}}` against the string "{\"a\":1}" → True/0, and even `contentSchema:false` → True/0. Malformed values (contentEncoding:12345, contentMediaType:[]) do not crash. Also true in draft-07 where content* first appeared.

ERROR COUNTING. Sibling string keywords each contribute independently and additively at top level: `{"type":"string","minLength":5,"maxLength":2,"pattern":"^z$"}` on "abc" → 3; with `type:"number"` instead → 4 (type + 3); `{"minLength":5,"maxLength":2,"pattern":"^z$","enum":["q"]}` → 4; adding `format`/`contentEncoding` adds nothing → still 3. Annotations ($comment/title/description/default/examples) and unknown keywords contribute 0.
Descending applicators surface each child error at TOP level: properties (2 failing props → 2), nested properties (→ 2 for two failures at depth 2), additionalProperties (2), items (2 items × 1 = 2; 3 items × 2 failing keywords = 6), draft-07 tuple `items:[...]` (2), prefixItems (2), propertyNames (1 per failing key: 2 keys → 2), allOf (2 branches × their failures → 2 and 3), $ref (2), if/then and if/else (then's errors bubble up individually: `{"if":{"minLength":1},"then":{"minLength":5,"maxLength":0}}` → 2).
Collapsing applicators yield exactly 1 top-level error regardless of sub-failures: anyOf → 1 (even with 4 sub-failures), oneOf → 1 (both when zero and when multiple branches match), not → 1, contains → 1. dependentSchemas with an absent key → 0.
Draft differences: NONE observed for this family — minLength/maxLength/pattern behave and count identically in Draft3/4/6/7/201909/202012; format and content* are ignored in all. Draft-03-only `type:[{schema},{schema}]` still yields 1 error. Line 1 of stdout is the only thing that varies by $schema.
Crash output shape: on any exception, stdout is COMPLETELY EMPTY (is_valid runs before the first print, so no partial lines) and exit code is 1; the traceback ends with `[PYI-xxxx:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13' due to unhandled exception!` on stderr.
gotchas: minLength/maxLength count Unicode CODE POINTS (Python len), not UTF-16 units. In JS you MUST use [...s].length / Array.from(s).length. '\u{1F600}' is length 1, not 2; a ZWJ family emoji is 5, a flag is 2.
No Unicode normalization: precomposed 'é' (U+00E9) has length 1 but decomposed 'e'+U+0301 has length 2, and they are NOT equal for pattern matching either.
pattern uses re.search (substring SEARCH), so 'b' matches 'abc'. Do NOT use fullmatch/anchoring. In JS use new RegExp(p, 'u'?) + .test(), but see the flag caveats below.

Python '$' matches before a SINGLE trailing '
': 'abc
' is VALID against '^abc$'. But 'abc

', 'abc', and 'abc
' are INVALID. JS '$' without /m matches only at absolute end — you must emulate Python. '\Z' is the true absolute-end anchor and is Python-only syntax.

Python re is UNICODE by default: \d matches Arabic-Indic ١٢٣ and Devanagari १२३; \w matches accented letters, CJK, and Nd/No digits like ² and ①. JS \d/\w are ASCII-only even with /u — you must translate to Unicode property escapes.
\w does NOT match combining marks (Mn) and does NOT match emoji. Decomposed 'café' fails ^\w{4}$ while precomposed 'café' passes.
\s matches NBSP, EM SPACE, U+2028, U+3000, \v, and U+001C, but NOT U+200B (ZWSP).

format is NEVER asserted — in ANY draft, for ANY format name, even with $vocabulary format-assertion:true. Always True / 0 errors. Same for contentEncoding, contentMediaType, and contentSchema (contentSchema:false is still ignored).

All string keywords are silently skipped for non-string instances, and the skip happens BEFORE regex compilation or numeric comparison — so an invalid regex or a string-valued minLength does NOT crash when the instance is a number/null/array/object/boolean. JSON booleans are not strings here.

Invalid regex, non-string pattern values, and non-numeric minLength/maxLength cause a hard crash: exit 1 with COMPLETELY EMPTY stdout (not 3 lines). The crash escapes anyOf/oneOf/not/if — it is never captured as a sub-error.
Regex compilation is lazy and instance-driven: {'properties':{'y':{'pattern':'['}}} is fine until a STRING actually reaches that subschema.

Python-specific regex syntax must be supported or emulated: (?P<name>...), (?P=name), (?#comment), inline (?i)(?m)(?s)(?x)(?a)(?u) at pattern START only (mid-pattern global flags CRASH in Python 3.11+), (?-i:...), \A, \Z, \N{NAME}, octal \141, \U0001F600, atomic (?>...) and possessive a*+. Conversely \p{L} and \Q...\E CRASH, and (?<name>...) (.NET style) CRASHES.
[[:alpha:]] is NOT a POSIX class — Python parses it as a character set, so it compiles but usually fails to match; do not special-case it.
(?i) uses simple case-insensitive matching, not full casefolding: 'ß' does NOT match (?i)^SS$, but KELVIN SIGN K matches (?i)k and İ matches (?i)i.

Bounds comparison is strict (< / >) against the raw JSON number, so fractional bounds matter (minLength:3.5 fails a length-3 string) and JSON booleans coerce to 1/0 (maxLength:true rejects 'abc', maxLength:false rejects everything non-empty).

Error counting: minLength and maxLength each contribute one error and both can fire at once (2). if/then/else, allOf, $ref, properties, items, prefixItems, additionalProperties, and propertyNames bubble child errors up as SEPARATE top-level errors; anyOf, oneOf, not, and contains always collapse to exactly 1.
Behavior is IDENTICAL across draft-03/04/06/07/2019-09/2020-12 for this whole family — only line 1 (the validator class name) changes.

result.findings:
FILE: /workspace/probes/validator-selection.jsonl (315 lines, JSONL). Each line is {"a": <instance JSON text>, "b": <schema JSON text>, "out": <exact stdout incl. trailing \n>, "exit": <int>} plus, when non-empty, "stderr": <exact stderr> and, for CLI-shape probes, "argv": [...] (the raw argv actually passed; for those the a/b fields are the effective parsed values or null when the run never got that far).

=== 1. $schema -> validator class mapping (validator_for) ===
Exactly six URIs are recognized, and ONLY these exact spellings (each additionally accepted with a single trailing '#'):
  http://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema  -> Draft3Validator
  http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema  -> Draft4Validator
  http://json-schema.org/draft-06/schema  -> Draft6Validator
  http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema  -> Draft7Validator
  https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema -> Draft201909Validator
  https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema -> Draft202012Validator
SCHEME IS NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. Drafts 03/04/06/07 are registered under http ONLY: 'https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#' is UNKNOWN -> warning + Draft202012Validator. 2019-09/2020-12 are registered under https ONLY: 'http://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' is UNKNOWN -> warning + Draft202012Validator. Trailing '#' is optional and irrelevant for all six (both '...2020-12/schema' and '...2020-12/schema#' work).

Unknown $schema string => one line on STDERR, exactly:
  "test13.py:15: DeprecationWarning: The metaschema specified by $schema was not found. Using the latest draft to validate, but this will raise an error in the future.\n"
and then Draft202012Validator is used. Exit stays 0, stdout unaffected. Tested-unknown values that all fall back with that warning: 'http://json-schema.org/schema#' and 'https://json-schema.org/schema#' and 'http://json-schema.org/schema' (the "latest" alias is NOT registered), draft-00/01/02/05, all hyper-schema URIs (http://json-schema.org/hyper-schema#, .../draft-07/hyper-schema#, .../draft-04/hyper-schema#, https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/hyper-schema, .../2020-12/hyper-schema), vocabulary meta URIs (https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/meta/core, .../meta/applicator, .../2019-09/meta/core), a nonexistent draft (2021-12), 'urn:foo', 'foo', '', '   ', '#'.

=== 2. URI normalization: it is urlsplit(uri).geturl(), and the result is a CACHED (hashed) lookup key ===
Observed normalization behavior, which matters a lot:
- Scheme is case-folded to lowercase: 'HTTP://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#' and 'HtTp://...' -> Draft7Validator. But 'HTTPS://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' -> ALSO Draft202012Validator, though that is the fallback: it emits the DeprecationWarning (host case matters, see next). Careful: 'HTTPS://JSON-SCHEMA.ORG/draft/2020-12/schema' warns; scheme-only uppercasing of a 2020-12 URI ('HTTPS://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema') ALSO warns in my probe -- see the vector; do not assume symmetry, use the recorded vectors.
- Host case is NOT normalized: 'http://JSON-SCHEMA.ORG/draft-07/schema#' and 'http://Json-Schema.org/...' -> unknown/warn. Path case is NOT normalized: '/DRAFT-07/schema#' and '/draft-07/Schema#' -> unknown/warn.
- An EMPTY query is dropped by geturl(): 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema?' -> Draft7Validator (no warning!). Same for 'https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema?' -> Draft202012Validator with NO warning. A non-empty query is kept: '...schema?x=1' -> warn.
- An empty fragment is dropped, a non-empty one is kept: '...schema#' == '...schema'; but '...schema##' (fragment '#'), '...schema#?' , '...schema#foo', '...schema#/definitions/foo' all -> warn. Same for 2019-09/2020-12 with '##'.
- TAB, CR and LF are stripped from ANYWHERE in the string before parsing: '\thttp://...', '\nhttp://...', '\rhttp://...', 'http\t://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#', 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/sch\nema#' ALL resolve to Draft7Validator.
- LEADING spaces are stripped, TRAILING spaces are NOT: ' http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#' and '  http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema' -> Draft7Validator; 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema# ' and 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema ' and 'https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema ' -> warn/fallback. (So the underlying urlsplit does lstrip only, not strip.)
- No path normalization: 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/../draft-07/schema#' -> warn. No default-port removal: 'http://json-schema.org:80/draft-07/schema#' -> warn. Missing scheme/authority variants ('//json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#', 'json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#', 'http:/json-schema.org/...', 'http:///json-schema.org/...', 'http://json-schema.org//draft-07/schema#') -> warn.

=== 3. Non-string $schema values: three distinct outcomes ===
The lookup key goes into a functools-cached normalize() that first HASHES the argument, then calls urlsplit, whose _coerce_args treats FALSY non-str as ''.
- $schema: null, false, "" (and "   ", which lstrips to "") => NO crash: normalizes to '' -> not found -> DeprecationWarning + Draft202012Validator, exit 0, "Draft202012Validator/True/0".
- $schema: any truthy number or true (1, -1, 1.5, true) => UNCAUGHT AttributeError: "'int'/'float'/'bool' object has no attribute 'decode'" (urllib/parse.py _decode_args). exit 1, full Python traceback on stderr, no stdout.
- $schema: {} , [] , {"a":1} , ["http://..."] , {"$ref":"x"} => UNCAUGHT TypeError: "unhashable type: 'dict'" / "'list'" raised inside jsonschema/_utils.py normalize (the lru_cache hashing the key). exit 1, traceback, no stdout. NOTE: 0 also crashes? No -- {"$schema":0} FALLS BACK with the warning (0 is falsy), while {"$schema":1} and {"$schema":-1} crash. That asymmetry is real and recorded.
All crash tracebacks end with the PyInstaller line "[PYI-NNNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13' due to unhandled exception!" (the PYI number varies run to run, so do not diff on it).

=== 4. Whole-schema (the --b document) types ===
- true  -> Draft202012Validator / True / 0 for every instance type tested (1, "s", [1], {"k":1}, null, true, 1.5).
- false -> Draft202012Validator / False / 1 for every instance type.
- {}    -> Draft202012Validator / True / 0.
- null  -> crash in validator_for: TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable (the `"$schema" not in schema` membership test). exit 1.
- number (1, 0, 1.5, -1) -> crash in validator_for: TypeError: argument of type 'int'/'float' is not iterable. exit 1.
- string ("hello", "") and array ([], [1,2], ["a"]) -> validator_for SURVIVES (membership `in` works on str/list) and returns Draft202012Validator, then the crash happens LATER while constructing the validator/resource: AttributeError: 'str'/'list' object has no attribute 'get' in referencing/jsonschema.py:_dollar_id. exit 1, no stdout. So the failure point differs by type even though the observable result (exit 1, empty stdout) is the same.

=== 5. $schema is root-only; $id is irrelevant to dispatch ===
A $schema nested inside properties/items/additionalProperties/definitions/allOf does NOT change the chosen validator class (still Draft202012Validator or whatever the root said), and does not suppress or add a warning. Examples: {"properties":{"a":{"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema#","type":"string"}}} with {"a":1} -> Draft202012Validator/False/1. {"$schema":draft-07, "properties":{"a":{"$schema":2020-12,...}}} -> Draft7Validator. A root with only "$id" or only "id" -> Draft202012Validator/True/0, no warning. $id alongside a valid $schema does not disturb dispatch.

=== 6. Top-level error counting (line 3) ===
Confirmed: is_valid (line 2) and len(list(iter_errors)) (line 3) are consistent -- False iff count>0.
- Sibling keywords each yield their own top-level error: {"type":"string","minimum":5,"maxLength":2} on 1 -> 2 (type + minimum; maxLength is inapplicable to a number).
- properties: one top-level error per failing property, at any depth (they are yielded via descend, not nested): 2 failing props -> 2; 3 -> 3; a single failing grandchild -> 1; two failing grandchildren under one child -> 2.
- items (schema form): one top-level error per failing element: [1,2] -> 2, [1,2,3] -> 3.
- allOf: sub-errors DO surface individually -> {"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"boolean"}]} on 1 -> 2.
- anyOf / oneOf / not / if-then: exactly 1 top-level error each (children live in .context).
- $ref: 1 error.
- type as a list: 1 error.
- Combined: {"$schema":X,"properties":{a:string,b:string},"type":"array"} on {"a":1,"b":2} -> 3 in EVERY draft (2 property errors + 1 type error), including under an unknown $schema (which then warns and uses 2020-12).

=== 7. Cross-draft semantics reachable only through correct dispatch ===
- exclusiveMinimum:5 (no minimum) on 3: draft3 True/0, draft4 True/0 (numeric form ignored), draft6/7/2019/2020 False/1.
- minimum:5 + exclusiveMinimum:true on 3: False/1 in ALL six drafts (draft3/4 honour the boolean modifier; 6+ ignore the boolean exclusiveMinimum but minimum:5 alone already fails).
- items as an ARRAY on [1,"a"]: draft3/4/6/7/2019 -> False/1. Draft 2020-12 -> UNCAUGHT AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' (jsonschema/_keywords.py items -> validators.descend -> referencing in_subresource -> _dollar_id), exit 1, traceback. 2020-12 assumes items is a schema and blows up on the list.
- prefixItems on [1,"a"]: ignored (True/0) in draft3/4/6/7/2019; only 2020-12 -> False/1.
- $ref with sibling keywords ({"$ref":"#/definitions/x","definitions":{...},"maximum":1} on 5): draft3/4/6/7 -> 1 error ($ref replaces siblings); 2019-09/2020-12 -> 2 errors (siblings apply).
- const:2 on 1: draft3/4 True/0 (unknown keyword); draft6+ False/1.
- contains on [1]: draft3/4 True/0; draft6+ False/1.
- dependencies:{"a":["b"]} on {"a":1}: draft3/4/6/7 False/1; 2019-09 and 2020-12 True/0 (dependencies removed).
- required:["b"] array form: draft3 ignores it (only 1 error from properties); draft4+ -> 2.
- required:true inside a property subschema: 1 error in every draft (draft3 honours it as "must be present" and it IS present, so only the type error).
- type:"integer" on 1.0: draft3/4 False/1 (float rejected); draft6+ True/0 (1.0 is an integer by value).
- type:"any": VALID (True/0) only in draft3. In draft4/6/7/2019/2020 it raises UNCAUGHT jsonschema.exceptions.UnknownType: "Unknown type 'any' for validator with schema: ..." -> exit 1, traceback that includes the pretty-printed schema and "While checking instance:". Note this crash happens inside is_valid (line 18 of the script), i.e. AFTER the class name would have been computed but BEFORE anything is printed, so stdout is empty.
- $defs vs definitions: both are just plain objects, $ref by JSON pointer works into either in every draft (False/1 each).

=== 8. JSON parsing of the args (before any jsonschema work) ===
--a is json.loads'd first (script line 11), then --b (line 12). Bad JSON -> uncaught json.decoder.JSONDecodeError, exit 1, no stdout. Exact messages observed: '' or 'nan' or "'1'" -> "Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)"; '{' -> "Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 2 (char 1)"; '01' -> "Extra data: line 1 column 2 (char 1)". Python's json ACCEPTS 'NaN' and 'Infinity' (both -> Draft202012Validator/True/0 against {}), and tolerates leading/trailing whitespace ('1 ', ' 1'). Because --a is parsed before --b, an invalid --a masks an invalid --b.

=== 9. CLI / argparse (prog name is "test13_executable") ===
- Both --a and --b are required=True, type=str. '--a=VAL' and '--a VAL' are both accepted; order is free ('--b {} --a 1' works).
- Repeated options: LAST WINS. '--a 1 --a "x" --b {"type":"string"}' -> True (uses "x"); '--a 1 --b {} --b false' -> False/1 (uses false).
- Missing args, exit 2, stdout empty, stderr exactly:
    "usage: test13_executable [-h] --a A --b B\ntest13_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --a, --b\n"
  (with "--a" or "--b" alone when only one is missing).
- Unknown option / stray positional, exit 2, stderr "usage: ...\ntest13_executable: error: unrecognized arguments: --c 1\n" (or "5", or "extra", or "--"). IMPORTANT: the required-arguments check fires BEFORE the unrecognized check, so '-a 1 -b {}' reports "the following arguments are required: --a, --b" (NOT "unrecognized"), and '-a 1 --b {}' reports "required: --a". Single-dash '-a'/'-b' are NOT accepted (only '--a'/'--b' were registered).
- Uppercase '--A 1 --B {}' -> required-args error (case sensitive).
- '-h' and '--help' print to STDOUT, exit 0, exactly:
    "usage: test13_executable [-h] --a A --b B\n\noptions:\n  -h, --help  show this help message and exit\n  --a A       instance (JSON string)\n  --b B       schema (JSON string)\n"
  ("options:" -- Python 3.10+ wording, not "optional arguments:"). Help wins even when placed after valid --a/--b, and even when --a/--b are absent.
- Prefix abbreviation IS enabled: '--h', '--he', '--hel' all print help (exit 0). '--hell' is not a prefix -> exit 2 required-args error.
- Missing value: '--a --b {}' -> exit 2, "test13_executable: error: argument --a: expected one argument". Same for '--a 1 --b'. A value that looks like an option is rejected the same way: '--a -x' and '--a --1' -> "expected one argument". BUT a negative NUMBER is accepted as a value: '--a -5 --b {}' -> parses -5 fine (argparse's negative-number heuristic, since no option string looks like a negative number). '--a=--b --b={}' is accepted by argparse (the '=' form takes anything) and then fails in json.loads with exit 1.
- Empty-string values: '--a "" --b {}' and '--a= --b=' -> exit 1 JSONDecodeError (argparse accepts them).
- '--' separator: '-- --a 1 --b {}' -> everything after '--' becomes positionals, so exit 2 "required: --a, --b". '--a 1 -- --b {}' -> exit 2 "required: --b". '--a 1 --b {} --' -> exit 2 "unrecognized arguments: --". Bare '--', '-', '-x' with no other args -> exit 2 required-args error.

=== 10. Exit codes summary ===
0 = normal (3 lines of stdout; a DeprecationWarning may also be on stderr). 1 = uncaught Python exception (traceback on stderr, stdout EMPTY -- nothing is printed partially, since all three prints come after validation). 2 = argparse usage error (usage+error on stderr, stdout empty, except -h/--help which is exit 0 with help on stdout).
gotchas: Scheme is NOT interchangeable per draft: drafts 03/04/06/07 are only registered under http://, and 2019-09/2020-12 only under https://. 'https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#' and 'http://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' both fall back to Draft202012Validator WITH the deprecation warning.

The trailing '#' is optional for all six URIs, but an empty QUERY is also dropped: 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema?' resolves to Draft7Validator with no warning. '...schema##' and '...schema#?' do NOT resolve.

Normalization is urlsplit(uri).geturl(): scheme lowercased, tab/CR/LF removed from anywhere in the string, LEADING whitespace stripped but TRAILING whitespace NOT. Host and path case are preserved, so 'http://JSON-SCHEMA.ORG/draft-07/schema#' is unknown.

$schema: null, false, "" and 0 quietly FALL BACK (warning + 2020-12) because they are falsy and coerce to ''. $schema: 1, -1, 1.5, true CRASH with AttributeError ('no attribute decode'), and $schema: {} or [] CRASH with TypeError: unhashable type. Same 'wrong type' category, three different outcomes.
There is no 'latest' alias: 'http://json-schema.org/schema#' is UNKNOWN and warns. Hyper-schema and per-vocabulary meta URIs (.../meta/core etc.) are also unknown.

A whole-schema of null or a number crashes inside validator_for (TypeError: argument of type X is not iterable), but a whole-schema that is a string or an array survives validator_for (prints nothing anyway) and crashes later in referencing._dollar_id with AttributeError: 'str'/'list' object has no attribute 'get'. All are exit 1 with empty stdout.
$schema is honoured ONLY at the document root. A $schema inside properties/items/definitions/allOf changes nothing and produces no warning.

items given as an ARRAY under $schema 2020-12 is not merely ignored -- it CRASHES (AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'), exit 1. Under 2019-09 and earlier it works as tuple validation.
type:"any" is valid only in draft-03; in draft-04 and later it raises UnknownType and the process exits 1 with EMPTY stdout (the crash is inside is_valid, before any print).

Error counting: properties/items yield one top-level error per failing child at any nesting depth, and allOf yields one per failing branch, but anyOf/oneOf/not/if-then always yield exactly 1 (children are in .context).
$ref with sibling keywords yields 1 error in drafts 3/4/6/7 ($ref replaces siblings) but 2 in 2019-09/2020-12.
argparse reports missing REQUIRED arguments before unrecognized ones, so '-a 1 -b {}' produces 'the following arguments are required: --a, --b', not an 'unrecognized arguments' message.
Prefix abbreviation is on: '--h', '--he', '--hel' all trigger help (exit 0, help on stdout). Help wins even when --a/--b are also present.
Repeated --a/--b: last occurrence wins, no error.
'--a -5' is accepted (argparse negative-number heuristic) but '--a -x' errors with 'expected one argument'; '--a=--b' is accepted by argparse and only fails later in json.loads.
The help/usage text says 'options:' (Python 3.10+), the prog name is 'test13_executable', and help goes to stdout with exit 0 while usage errors go to stderr with exit 2.
Crash tracebacks end with a PyInstaller line '[PYI-<random>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13' ...' whose number changes every run -- never diff on it.
--a is json.loads'd before --b, so a malformed instance masks a malformed schema; Python's json accepts NaN/Infinity and surrounding whitespace but rejects 'nan', "'1'", and '01'.

result.family: Numeric keywords (multipleOf, divisibleBy, maximum, minimum, exclusiveMaximum, exclusiveMinimum)
result.findings:
DELIVERABLE: /workspace/probes/numeric.jsonl (796 lines, all valid JSONL, generated by /workspace/probes/gen_numeric.js and /workspace/probes/gen_numeric2.js which shell out to the real binary via execFileSync and capture stdout+exit code; stderr discarded). Each line = {"a","b","out","exit"}.

KEYWORD-TO-DRAFT MAP (verified by sweeping every case over draft-03/04/06/07/2019-09/2020-12 plus a bare no-$schema schema, which always behaves exactly as 2020-12):
* multipleOf: absent in Draft3 (completely ignored, never even type-checks its own value: {"multipleOf":"3"}, {"multipleOf":null}, {"multipleOf":0} are all silently ignored under draft-03 and yield True/0). Present in Draft4, 6, 7, 2019-09, 2020-12 with identical behavior.
* divisibleBy: present ONLY in Draft3. Under draft-04 and later it is an unknown keyword => ignored (True/0), even divisibleBy:0. Under draft-03 it behaves exactly like multipleOf does in draft4+ (same code path: 10/divisibleBy 3 => False/1; 10/divisibleBy 2.5 => True/0 since 10/2.5=4.0; divisibleBy:0 and divisibleBy:false => ZeroDivisionError crash; divisibleBy:"3" and divisibleBy:null => TypeError crash; divisibleBy:true => 5%1==0 => True/0). A schema carrying BOTH keys yields 3 errors under draft-03 for {"minimum":10,"maximum":3,"divisibleBy":3} vs 2 under draft4+, and 3 under draft4+ for {"minimum":10,"maximum":3,"multipleOf":3} vs 2 under draft-03.
* maximum / minimum: present in ALL six drafts. Plain numeric comparison; each violation is exactly ONE top-level error.
* exclusiveMaximum / exclusiveMinimum: in Draft3 and Draft4 they are NOT standalone keywords — they exist only as boolean-ish modifiers read from inside the maximum/minimum validators via schema.get("exclusiveMaximum", False). Consequently, in draft-03/04, a schema containing exclusiveMaximum/exclusiveMinimum WITHOUT the corresponding maximum/minimum is a total no-op: {"exclusiveMaximum":5}, {"exclusiveMaximum":true}, {"exclusiveMinimum":6,"exclusiveMaximum":4}, even {"exclusiveMaximum":"3"}, {"exclusiveMaximum":null}, {"exclusiveMaximum":[1]} all give True/0 with NO crash. In Draft6/7/2019-09/2020-12 they are first-class standalone keywords and the boolean-modifier reading is gone entirely (maximum ignores exclusiveMaximum).

DRAFT3/4 MODIFIER SEMANTICS (exact): maximum yields an error when `instance >= maximum` if bool(schema.get("exclusiveMaximum", False)) is truthy, else when `instance > maximum`. Symmetric for minimum/exclusiveMinimum (instance <= minimum vs instance < minimum). Truthiness is Python truthiness of whatever JSON value sits there, so a NUMBER works as a flag: {"maximum":10,"exclusiveMaximum":3} => truthy => test 5>=10 => passes (True/0); {"maximum":3,"exclusiveMaximum":0} => 0 is falsy => test 5>3 => False/1 (only 1 error, because exclusiveMaximum itself is not a keyword); {"maximum":3,"exclusiveMaximum":"no"} => truthy string => 5>=3 => False/1 (no crash in draft-04, since the value is only tested for truthiness, never compared). The modifier NEVER produces its own separate error in draft3/4, so at most 1 error per maximum and 1 per minimum.

DRAFT6+ STANDALONE SEMANTICS (exact): maximum errors iff instance > maximum; minimum iff instance < minimum; exclusiveMaximum iff instance >= exclusiveMaximum; exclusiveMinimum iff instance <= exclusiveMinimum. Each keyword independently yields one error, so maximum and exclusiveMaximum CAN both fire and give 2 errors. Booleans in the value slot do NOT crash and are not ignored — they are compared as Python numbers True==1 / False==0: {"exclusiveMaximum":true} on 5 => 5>=1 => False/1; {"exclusiveMaximum":false} on 5 => 5>=0 => False/1; {"exclusiveMinimum":true} on 5 => 5<=1 false => True/0; {"exclusiveMinimum":true} on 0 => 0<=1 => False/1; {"maximum":true} on 5 => 5>1 => False/1; {"minimum":true} on 0.5 => 0.5<1 => False/1. Boolean exclusiveMaximum:false with maximum:5 on instance 5 => draft3/4 True/0 but draft6+ False/1 (the exclusiveMaximum:false keyword itself fires). {"maximum":5,"minimum":5,"exclusiveMaximum":true,"exclusiveMinimum":true} on 5 => draft3/4 = 2 errors, draft6+ = 1 error.

MULTIPLEOF IMPLEMENTATION (reverse-engineered exactly from tracebacks + results; jsonschema/_keywords.py lines 170-190): if the instance is not of type "number" (booleans are excluded from "number" — verified: true/false/"abc"/null/[]/{} with multipleOf 3 or multipleOf 0 all give True/0 with NO crash, so the ZeroDivision cases require a numeric instance), then return. If the SCHEMA value dB is a Python float (i.e. the JSON literal had a '.' or an exponent, e.g. 3.0, 1e-308, 0.0): quotient = instance / dB (line 172 — ZeroDivisionError "float division by zero" when dB is 0.0 or -0.0), then failed = int(quotient) != quotient, and on OverflowError from int(quotient) it falls back to failed = (Fraction(instance) % Fraction(dB)) != 0 (line 186). Otherwise (dB is an int or bool) failed = instance % dB (line 188 — ZeroDivisionError "integer modulo by zero" when dB is 0 or false).
Observed float consequences: no decimal/epsilon fuzzing at all, pure IEEE-754 double division. 4.5/1.5 => True/0. 0.0075 multipleOf 0.0001 => TRUE/0 (the double quotient rounds exactly to 75.0, so this famous "imprecision" case actually PASSES here). 1.1 multipleOf 0.1 => True/0 (quotient rounds to 11.0). 4.5 multipleOf 0.1 => True/0. 1 multipleOf 0.0001 => True/0. BUT 0.3 multipleOf 0.1 => False/1 (2.9999999999999996), 3.3 multipleOf 1.1 => False/1, 2.4 multipleOf 0.8 => False/1, 1 multipleOf 0.3 => False/1, 0.00751 multipleOf 0.0001 => False/1, 4.5 multipleOf 1.5000000000000002 => False/1. An implementer MUST reproduce double-precision division bit-for-bit; a "close enough" epsilon comparison gets 0.3/0.1 wrong and an exact-decimal comparison gets 0.0075/0.0001 wrong.
Overflow / Fraction fallback: 1e308 multipleOf 1e-308 => quotient overflows to inf, int(inf) raises OverflowError, Fraction path runs => False/1 (exit 0, no crash). 1e308 multipleOf 1e-310 and 1e-200 => False/1. 1e308 multipleOf 1.0 / 0.5 / 2 (int) => True/0. Big integers work natively: 123456789012345678901234567890 multipleOf 3 => True/0; multipleOf 7 => False/1; multipleOf 1.5 (float path) => True/0.
Infinity: JSON "1e400" parses to Python inf. With an INT multipleOf it is fine: 1e400 multipleOf 2 => inf % 2 == nan (truthy) => False/1; multipleOf 3 => False/1. With a FLOAT multipleOf it CRASHES: inf/2.0 = inf, int(inf) raises OverflowError, then Fraction(inf) raises OverflowError "cannot convert Infinity to integer ratio" which is NOT caught => exit 1, empty stdout. 1e400 multipleOf 1e400 and 1e400 multipleOf 1e-400 also crash. 1e-400 underflows to 0.0, so 1e-400 multipleOf 1e-400 crashes with ZeroDivisionError. But maximum/minimum/exclusive* handle inf fine: 1e400 maximum 5 => False/1; 1e400 minimum 5 => True/0; 1e400 exclusiveMaximum 5 => False/1; 1e400 maximum 1e400 => True/0; 1e400 exclusiveMaximum 1e400 => False/1; 1e-400 minimum 0 => True/0 but exclusiveMinimum 0 => False/1 (it is exactly 0.0).
Negative multipleOf uses Python modulo semantics (result has the sign of the divisor): 10 multipleOf -5 => 10 % -5 == 0 => True/0; 10 multipleOf -3 => 10 % -3 == -2 => False/1; 10 multipleOf -4 => False/1; 10.0 multipleOf -2.5 => quotient -4.0 => True/0. multipleOf -0.0 crashes (ZeroDivisionError).
Zero and negative-zero INSTANCES: 0, -0, 0.0, -0.0 with multipleOf 3 => all True/0. -0.0 minimum 0 => True/0, -0.0 maximum 0 => True/0 (Python -0.0 == 0), but -0.0 exclusiveMinimum 0 => False/1 and -0 exclusiveMaximum 0 => False/1.
multipleOf:true => 5 % 1 == 0 => True/0 in every draft (bool is not a float, takes the int path). multipleOf:false => crash.

CRASH CATALOGUE (78 of 796 vectors, always exit code 1 with a Python traceback on stderr and COMPLETELY EMPTY stdout — none of the three lines get printed, because the exception fires before any print). Which line the traceback names (validators.py:500 is_valid at test13.py:18 vs validators.py:384 iter_errors at test13.py:19) depends on whether an earlier keyword already short-circuited is_valid, and that in turn depends on JSON key insertion order — e.g. under draft-07 {"maximum":3,"exclusiveMaximum":"no"} crashes at line 19 while {"exclusiveMaximum":"no","maximum":3} crashes at line 18. Black-box output is identical either way (empty stdout, exit 1). Crashing inputs, all requiring a numeric (non-boolean) instance:
- multipleOf: 0 / 0.0 / -0.0 / false (ZeroDivisionError) and "3" / null / [3] (TypeError) — draft-04 and later only; draft-03 ignores all of them.
- divisibleBy: 0 / false / "3" / null — draft-03 only; ignored elsewhere.
- maximum or minimum with a non-comparable value ("3", null, [3]) — crashes in ALL SIX drafts.
- exclusiveMaximum / exclusiveMinimum with a non-comparable value ("3", "no", null, [1]) — crashes in draft-06/07/2019-09/2020-12 only; harmless in draft-03/04 where only truthiness is consulted.
- multipleOf with a float value and an infinite instance (1e400) — OverflowError from Fraction.
- The crash propagates from nested subschemas too: {"a":5} against {"properties":{"a":{"multipleOf":0}}} => exit 1, empty stdout.

ERROR-COUNT / BUBBLING RULES: every failing numeric keyword contributes exactly one top-level error and they accumulate. {"minimum":10,"maximum":3} on 5 => 2 in all drafts. {"type":"number","maximum":1,"minimum":9,"multipleOf":4} on 5 => 3 (2 under draft-03 where multipleOf is unknown). {"exclusiveMinimum":6,"exclusiveMaximum":4} on 5 => 2 in draft6+, 0 in draft3/4. Non-number instances (including booleans) short-circuit every numeric keyword: true against {"minimum":10,"maximum":3} => True/0 in all drafts. Descended errors from properties/items/prefixItems each appear at top level: {"a":5,"b":7} vs two failing maximum subschemas => 2; [1,2,3] vs {"items":{"minimum":10,"maximum":0}} => 6; [5,5,5] vs {"items":{"maximum":1,"minimum":9}} => 6; nested properties two levels deep with maximum+minimum failing => 2; three properties each failing one keyword => 3. Combinators collapse: anyOf => 1, oneOf => 1, not => 1, if/then => 1 (the then failure surfaces as a single error), contains => 1; allOf does NOT collapse — {"allOf":[{"maximum":1},{"minimum":10}]} => 2 and {"allOf":[{"maximum":1,"minimum":10}]} => 2. $ref to a subschema with one failing keyword => 1. Mixing: {"anyOf":[...],"maximum":2} on 5 => 2.

TYPE-KEYWORD INTERACTION worth noting for counts: 5.0 against {"type":"integer","multipleOf":2} yields 1 error under draft-03 (type fails, multipleOf unknown), 2 under draft-04 (5.0 is not an integer in draft3/4 AND multipleOf fails), and 1 under draft-06+ (5.0 counts as an integer, only multipleOf fails).

CLI note discovered while probing: instances whose JSON text begins with '-' (e.g. -1e400 passed as a bare argv token) make argparse reject the argument with "expected one argument", exit code 2 and a usage message on stderr. Vectors in the file therefore encode negative instances with a leading space (e.g. " -5", " -0.0"), which json.loads accepts identically.
gotchas: multipleOf does not exist in draft-03 at all — it is silently ignored there, including multipleOf:0 which would crash in every other draft. Conversely divisibleBy exists ONLY in draft-03 and is ignored (never crashes) in draft-04+.

In draft-03/draft-04, exclusiveMaximum/exclusiveMinimum are NOT keywords. A schema with only {"exclusiveMaximum":5} validates everything (True/0). They are read solely as a truthiness flag from inside maximum/minimum, so a numeric or string value acts as 'true' ({"maximum":10,"exclusiveMaximum":3} on 5 PASSES because it becomes 5>=10) and 0 acts as 'false'. They never emit their own error, so draft3/4 can never exceed 1 error from maximum plus 1 from minimum.

In draft-06+, booleans in a numeric keyword slot are compared as numbers, not ignored and not an error: exclusiveMaximum:true means 'instance >= 1' and exclusiveMaximum:false means 'instance >= 0'. So {"maximum":5,"exclusiveMaximum":false} on 5 is True/0 in draft3/4 but False/1 in draft6+.

multipleOf uses two entirely different code paths chosen by the Python type of the schema value: float => `instance / dB` then `int(q) != q`; int/bool => `instance % dB`. multipleOf:2 and multipleOf:2.0 are NOT interchangeable — with instance 1e400 the int form gives False/1 and the float form crashes with OverflowError. A JS reimplementation must track whether the JSON literal was written with a decimal point/exponent.

No epsilon or decimal fuzzing: it is raw IEEE-754 double division. 0.0075 multipleOf 0.0001 PASSES (quotient rounds to exactly 75.0) and 1.1 multipleOf 0.1 PASSES, while 0.3 multipleOf 0.1, 3.3 multipleOf 1.1 and 2.4 multipleOf 0.8 FAIL. Any 'smart' tolerance or exact-rational rewrite will diverge in one direction or the other.

On OverflowError from int(quotient) (huge instance / tiny float divisor, e.g. 1e308 multipleOf 1e-308) it silently falls back to exact Fraction arithmetic and returns a normal 1-error result — but if the instance is infinite (JSON 1e400) Fraction() itself raises OverflowError and the whole program crashes.

Negative multipleOf follows Python modulo sign rules: 10 multipleOf -5 is valid (10 % -5 == 0) but 10 multipleOf -3 is invalid (10 % -3 == -2). JS `%` gives 10 % -3 === 1, also truthy, so this particular case happens to agree, but the sign convention differs in general — compute with Python semantics.

Booleans are never 'numbers': true/false skip every numeric keyword entirely, so even {"multipleOf":0} against true returns True/0 instead of crashing. Only a real number instance reaches the division.

maximum/minimum with a non-comparable value ("3", null, array) crashes in ALL six drafts, but exclusiveMaximum/exclusiveMinimum with the same bad value crashes only in draft-06+ and is harmless in draft-03/04.

On any crash the program prints NOTHING to stdout (all three prints come after the failing statement) and exits 1. Whether the traceback points at is_valid (line 18) or iter_errors (line 19) depends on JSON key order, because is_valid short-circuits on the first error — but stdout is empty either way.

Error counts add up per keyword and descended errors from properties/items/prefixItems each surface at top level (e.g. [1,2,3] vs {"items":{"minimum":10,"maximum":0}} = 6). allOf also does NOT collapse (2 errors), whereas anyOf/oneOf/not/if-then/contains each collapse to exactly 1.
JSON 1e400 becomes +Infinity and 1e-400 becomes 0.0 before any keyword runs; that is why 1e-400 multipleOf 1e-400 dies with ZeroDivisionError and 1e-400 exclusiveMinimum 0 reports a violation.
-0.0 and -0 compare equal to 0, so minimum:0/maximum:0 accept them, but exclusiveMinimum:0 and exclusiveMaximum:0 reject them.
Passing an instance whose text starts with '-' as a bare argv token makes argparse fail with exit code 2 (not 1) and no validator output; the vector file uses a leading space to work around this.

result.findings:
FILE: /workspace/probes/type-and-scalars.jsonl (911 deduped vectors, all re-run and captured live; duplicates across batches were byte-identical => behavior is deterministic).

== `type`: basic matrix (identical in ALL drafts 3/4/6/7/2019-09/2020-12 unless noted) ==
Per JSON value kind, `{"type":T}` yields exactly 0 errors on match and exactly 1 error on mismatch. Never more than 1 error, no matter how many names are listed or how many fail.
- "null" matches only JSON null.
- "boolean" matches only true/false. 1 and 0 do NOT match "boolean".
- "object" matches only {}. "array" matches only [].
- "string" matches only JSON strings (1.0 -> not a string).
- "number" matches ints and floats, NOT booleans (true/false fail "number" in every draft).
- "integer" matches Python ints always; booleans NEVER match "integer" in any draft (bool is excluded despite being an int subclass).

== integer vs number for float instances: THE draft split ==
Draft3 and Draft4: "integer" means "the JSON literal was an int" (Python int). A JSON literal with a decimal point or an exponent parses to float and FAILS "integer":
  1.0, 2.0, 0.0, -0.0, 1e2, 1E2, 1.0e1, 1e308 -> "integer" FALSE / 1 error under draft-03 and draft-04.
Draft6, Draft7, 2019-09, 2020-12: "integer" additionally accepts floats whose value is integral (float.is_integer()):
  1.0, 2.0, 0.0, -0.0, 1e2, 1E2, 1.0e1, 1e308 -> "integer" TRUE / 0 errors.
  1.5 -> false in every draft. 1e-400 underflows to 0.0 -> "integer" TRUE in draft6+ (0 errors), and TRUE for "number".
  1e400 overflows to float inf -> "integer" FALSE in EVERY draft (inf.is_integer() is false), but "number" TRUE in every draft.
- `-0` (JSON literal without a dot) parses as Python int 0 -> "integer" TRUE in all drafts including 3/4. `-0.0` is a float -> false in 3/4, true in 6+.
- Arbitrary-precision ints: 10000000000000000000000000000001 is "integer" TRUE and "number" TRUE in every draft (bignum, no precision loss).
- NaN (Python json accepts the literals NaN / Infinity / -Infinity): NaN is "number" TRUE, "integer" FALSE, in every draft. Infinity is "number" TRUE, "integer" FALSE.

== `type` as an array ==
- Union semantics: valid if ANY listed name matches -> 0 errors; else exactly 1 error (one error listing all names, never one per name).
- Empty array `"type": []` -> ALWAYS invalid, exactly 1 error, every draft (including draft3).
- Duplicates `["integer","integer"]` behave like a single name.
- Evaluation SHORT-CIRCUITS left-to-right: `{"type":["string","foo"]}` on "s" -> valid, 0 errors, NO crash (never reaches the bogus name); `{"type":["foo","string"]}` on "s" -> CRASH exit 1. Same with `["number","any"]` on 1 -> valid in every draft, but `["any"]` alone crashes in draft4+.

== Unknown / malformed `type` values: crash semantics ==
Any type name that is not a known checker name raises jsonschema.exceptions.UnknownType. Effect: traceback on stderr, EMPTY stdout (nothing is printed at all — the exception happens inside is_valid on line 18, before any print), exit code 1.
- "foo", "Integer", "INTEGER", "!string" -> crash in every draft. Type names are case-sensitive and there is no normalization.
- "any" -> VALID (matches everything) ONLY under draft-03; crash under no-$schema/draft-04/06/07/2019-09/2020-12.
- The implementation calls ensure_list(types) which is `[x] if isinstance(x,str) else x` — it does NOT wrap non-strings. Consequences, all verified:
  * `"type": 1`, `"type": null`, `"type": true`, `"type": false` -> crash exit 1 (iterating a non-iterable), every draft.
  * `"type": {}` -> NO crash: iterating an empty dict gives no names, so `any(...)` is False -> exactly 1 error, instance always invalid. Every draft (including draft3).
  * `"type": {"string":1}` -> iterates the dict's KEYS, so this behaves like `type:["string"]`: instance "s" is VALID (0 errors). `{"string":1,"integer":2}` behaves like ["string","integer"]. `{"type":"string"}` as the value of type -> key "type" is not a type name -> crash.
  * `"type": [1]`, `[null]`, `[[]]` -> crash (unhashable/unknown type lookup).
- A crash anywhere in the schema tree propagates: `{"properties":{"x":{"type":"foo"}}}` crashes only if key x is present (crash on {"x":1}, clean 0 errors on {"y":1}). `{"items":{"type":"foo"}}` on [1] crashes. `{"not":{"type":"foo"}}` crashes (not does not swallow it). `{"anyOf":[{"type":"integer"},{"type":"foo"}]}` on 1 does NOT crash (anyOf short-circuits on first success) but `{"oneOf":[...]}` with the same branches DOES crash (oneOf evaluates all branches).
- Keyword ordering inside the schema object does not matter for crashing: both `{"enum":[1],"type":"foo"}` and `{"type":"foo","enum":[1]}` crash.

== draft-03 only: subschemas inside `type`, and `disallow` ==
- draft-03 allows objects inside the `type` array; each object is a subschema. Instance passes if any listed name matches OR any listed subschema validates.
  `{"$schema":draft3,"type":["integer",{"minLength":5}]}` -> "aaaaa" valid (0), "a" invalid (1 error).
  `{"type":[{"type":"string","minLength":5}]}` on 1 or "a" -> exactly 1 top-level error. Sub-errors from the failing subschemas live in error.context and do NOT add to the count: `type:[{"type":"string"},{"type":"boolean"},{"type":"null"}]` on 1 -> still exactly 1 error.
  Under all non-draft3 drafts, an object inside the `type` array crashes (exit 1).
- `disallow` is a draft-03-only keyword; it is silently IGNORED under draft-04/07/no-$schema (0 errors).
  Semantics: one error PER disallowed entry that matches. `disallow:["integer","number"]` on 1 -> 2 errors. `["number","integer","string","boolean"]` on 1 -> 2 errors. `["integer","number","any"]` on 1 -> 3 errors. `disallow:"integer"` on 1 -> 1 error, on "s" -> 0.
  `disallow:"any"` -> always 1 error. `disallow:[]` -> 0 errors. `disallow:{}` -> 0 errors (dict key iteration, empty). `disallow:[{"type":"integer"}]` (subschema) on 1 -> 1 error; `[{"type":"integer","minimum":5}]` on 1 -> 0 errors (subschema doesn't match). `[{"type":"integer"},{"minimum":0}]` -> 2 errors.
  `disallow:{"type":"integer"}` -> crash (iterates key "type"). `disallow:1`, `disallow:null`, `disallow:true`, `disallow:[[]]` -> crash. `disallow:["any","foo"]` -> crash (it yields the "any" error then hits "foo"), while `["string","any"]` -> 1 error (no bogus name).
  `type` and `disallow` are independent keywords: `{"type":"string","disallow":"integer"}` on 1 -> 2 errors.
- draft-03 `type:"any"` combined with other keywords does not suppress them: `{"type":"any","enum":[2]}` on 1 -> 1 error.

== `enum` (all drafts, including draft-03) ==
- 0 errors if any member is "equal", otherwise exactly 1 error. Never more than 1 error regardless of enum length.
- `enum: []` -> always exactly 1 error, every draft (no special "empty enum" diagnostic, just a normal failure).
- Equality is Python `==` with a boolean-vs-number guard: `true`/`false` are NEVER equal to 1/0 and vice-versa, at any nesting depth. 1 vs [true] -> 1 error; true vs [1] -> 1 error; 0 vs [false] -> 1 error; false vs [0] -> 1 error; [1] vs [[true]] -> 1 error; {"a":1} vs [{"a":true}] -> 1 error; {"a":0} vs [{"a":false}] -> 1 error.
- Numeric identity IS loose across int/float: 1 matches [1.0], 1.0 matches [1], 0 matches [0.0], -0 and -0.0 match [0], 1e20 matches [100000000000000000000] and vice versa. 1.0000000001 does not match [1].
- Strings are never equal to numbers: 1 vs ["1"] -> 1 error. null only equals null (null vs [0] -> 1 error).
- Objects compare by content, KEY ORDER IRRELEVANT: {"b":1,"a":2} matches [{"a":2,"b":1}]. Subset/superset are not equal.
- Arrays compare element-wise, ORDER MATTERS: [1,2] does not match [[2,1]]. Deep nesting works: [[1,{"a":1}]] matches [[[1,{"a":1}]]].
- Cross-kind: [] does not match [{}]; {} does not match [[]]; "" does not match [[]]; "ab" does not match [["a","b"]].
- Malformed `enum`: `enum: 1`, `enum: null`, `enum: true` -> CRASH exit 1 (not iterable). `enum: "abc"` does NOT crash — it iterates the string's characters, so instance "a" is VALID (0 errors) and "abc" or 1 gives 1 error. `enum: {"a":1}` iterates the dict's keys, so "a" is VALID and 1 gives 1 error.

== `const` ==
- Supported in draft-06, draft-07, 2019-09, 2020-12 and the default (no-$schema => 2020-12). SILENTLY IGNORED in draft-03 and draft-04: `{"$schema":draft3,"const":1}` and `{"$schema":draft4,"const":1}` on instance 2 -> True / 0 errors.
- Where supported: 0 or exactly 1 error, using the exact same equality function as enum. 1 vs const true -> 1 error; true vs const 1 -> 1 error; 0 vs const false -> 1 error; 1 vs const 1.0 -> 0; 1.0 vs const 1 -> 0; 0 vs const -0 -> 0; 0.0 vs const 0 -> 0; null vs const null -> 0; {"b":1,"a":2} vs const {"a":2,"b":1} -> 0; [1,true] vs const [true,1] -> 1 error; {"a":[1,{"b":1}]} vs const {"a":[1,{"b":true}]} -> 1 error; NaN vs const 1 -> 1 error.
- `const: null` is a real constraint (instance 1 -> 1 error), it is not treated as "absent".

== Error counting (top level) ==
- Every failing keyword in the same schema object contributes exactly one top-level error, independently: `{"type":"string","enum":[1],"const":2,"minimum":9}` on 4 -> 4 errors. `{"enum":[1,2],"type":"string"}` on 4 -> 2. `{"enum":[1],"const":2,"type":"string"}` on 4 -> 3. `{"type":"integer","minimum":5,"enum":["x"],"const":"y"}` on 1 -> 3. `{"type":["integer","number"],"enum":[1],"const":2}` on "x" -> 3.
- `properties`/`items` descend and each descended error is top-level: {"x":1,"y":2} vs properties x,y both type:string -> 2. [1,2,3] vs items type:string -> 3; items {"type":"string","enum":[9]} -> 6 (3 items x 2 keywords). Nested two levels {"x":{"z":1}} with z requiring type+enum -> 2.
- A failing `type` on the container does NOT stop `items` from running: `{"type":"string","items":{"type":"string"}}` on [1,2] -> 3 errors.
- Duplicate JSON keys in the schema: last one wins (Python json.loads). `{"const":1,"const":2}` on 1 -> 1 error; `{"type":"integer","type":"string"}` on 1 -> 1 error.
- Unknown keywords and wrong-case keywords are ignored: `{"Type":"string"}`, `{"typo":"string"}`, `{}` -> 0 errors. `true` -> 0 errors, `false` -> 1 error.

== Cross-draft summary ==
2019-09 and 2020-12 were indistinguishable for every probe in this family. draft-06 and draft-07 were indistinguishable too. The only real splits are: (a) integer-vs-float for "integer" (3/4 strict, 6+ lenient), (b) "any" and subschemas-inside-type and `disallow` are draft-03-only (crash/ignored elsewhere), (c) `const` is ignored in 3/4.
gotchas: `type`, `enum`, and `const` each yield AT MOST ONE top-level error, no matter how many names/members are listed or how many fail. Do not emit one error per union member.
Booleans are never numbers: true/false fail type "integer" AND type "number" in every draft. Equally, in enum/const true != 1 and false != 0 at any nesting depth — but 1 == 1.0 and -0 == 0 == 0.0.

The integer/float split: 1.0, 2.0, 1e2, 1E2, 0.0, -0.0, 1e308 are type "integer" TRUE in draft6/7/2019-09/2020-12 but FALSE in draft-03 and draft-04. Note `-0` (no decimal point) is an int literal so it is "integer" TRUE even in draft3/4.

1e400 parses to float infinity: type "number" TRUE but type "integer" FALSE in EVERY draft. 1e-400 underflows to 0.0 so it is "integer" TRUE in draft6+. Python json also accepts the bare literals NaN/Infinity: NaN is "number" TRUE, "integer" FALSE.

An unknown type name raises UnknownType: the program prints NOTHING to stdout and exits 1. But evaluation SHORT-CIRCUITS, so `{"type":["string","foo"]}` on a string is silently valid while `{"type":["foo","string"]}` on the same string crashes. Order matters. Likewise anyOf hides the crash if an earlier branch succeeds, but oneOf does not.

ensure_list does not wrap non-strings. `"type": {}` gives exactly 1 error (empty key iteration, always invalid, no crash), `"type": {"string":1}` behaves like `["string"]` (valid for strings!), and `"type": 1/null/true/false/[1]/[[]]` crash with exit 1. The same trick applies to `enum`: `enum:"abc"` iterates characters (so "a" is valid, "abc" is not), `enum:{"a":1}` iterates keys, while `enum:1/null/true` crash.
`type: []` and `enum: []` are always invalid with exactly 1 error — they are not no-ops.

`const` is silently IGNORED under draft-03 and draft-04 (always 0 errors); `disallow` and `type:"any"` and object-subschemas inside the `type` array are draft-03 ONLY — under other drafts `"any"` and inline subschemas crash with UnknownType and `disallow` is ignored.

draft-03 `disallow` emits ONE ERROR PER MATCHING ENTRY (disallow:["integer","number"] on 1 -> 2 errors; with "any" appended -> 3), unlike `type` which emits at most one. draft-03 `type` with failing subschemas still emits exactly 1 top-level error (sub-errors go to error.context).

Object equality in enum/const ignores key order but is exact on key set (subset/superset fail); array equality is order-sensitive; strings are never equal to arrays/numbers ( "ab" != ["a","b"], "" != [] ).

Errors from `properties`/`items` bubble up as separate top-level errors and multiply: items {"type":"string","enum":[9]} over a 3-element array gives 6. A failing container-level `type` does not stop `items`/`properties` from also running.

Harness artifact, not library behavior: an instance argument like `-1e400`, `-1e5`, or `-Infinity` is rejected by argparse (exit code 2, empty stdout) because it looks like a flag, while `-1`, `-1.5`, `-0`, `-0.0` are accepted.
