All 726 vectors were produced by actually executing /workspace/dataset/test13_executable and capturing stdout/exit verbatim; file is /workspace/probes/draft201909-202012.jsonl (fields a,b,out,exit; out is the exact 3-line stdout, empty string on crash).

=== KEYWORD x DRAFT SUPPORT MATRIX (observed) ===
definitions / $defs: neither is a validation keyword in any draft; both are just plain JSON-pointer targets, so "$ref":"#/definitions/P" AND "$ref":"#/$defs/P" both resolve in draft3,4,6,7,2019-09,2020-12 alike (all give False/1 for {"definitions":{"P":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/P"} on 1).
dependencies: honored in draft3/4/6/7 (both array form and schema form; draft3 ignores the schema form's "required" because draft3 has no "required" keyword — {"dependencies":{"a":{"required":["b"]}}} on {"a":1} is True/0 under draft3 but False/1 under 4/6/7). COMPLETELY IGNORED in 2019-09 and 2020-12 (True/0), even when malformed ("dependencies":5 → True/0).
dependentRequired / dependentSchemas: ignored in draft3/4/6/7; honored only in 2019-09 and 2020-12.
items array form ("tuple"): honored draft3,4,6,7,2019-09. In 2020-12 an ARRAY-valued "items" is a HARD CRASH: AttributeError 'list' object has no attribute 'get' (referencing/jsonschema.py _dollar_id), exit 1, empty stdout — but only when the instance is actually an array; with a non-array instance the keyword never descends and you get normal output (e.g. 1 vs {"items":[{"type":"string"}]} → Draft202012Validator/True/0).
additionalItems: honored draft3..2019-09 (only meaningful alongside array-form items). Silently ignored in 2020-12 (e.g. {"prefixItems":[{"type":"integer"}],"additionalItems":{"type":"string"}} on [1,2] → True/0 in every draft, since prefixItems does not enable additionalItems anywhere).
prefixItems: ignored in draft3,4,6,7 AND in 2019-09 (True/0). Honored ONLY in 2020-12. Non-array prefixItems: {} → True/0 everywhere; {"type":"string"} → 2020-12 crash exit 1 (iterating dict keys as schemas); prefixItems:[] → valid, evaluates nothing.
$dynamicRef/$dynamicAnchor: ignored in draft3..2019-09 (True/0, even for an unresolvable "#NOPE"). Honored ONLY in 2020-12. In 2020-12 $dynamicRef also resolves to a plain $anchor and to absolute-URI+fragment forms ("http://ex/t#N"). In 2020-12 an unresolvable $dynamicRef ("#NOPE") crashes exit 1. $dynamicAnchor also registers as an ordinary anchor in 2020-12 ("$ref":"#N" to a $dynamicAnchor resolves), while in 2019-09 the same "$ref":"#N" crashes exit 1 (anchor unknown).
$recursiveRef/$recursiveAnchor: honored ONLY in 2019-09 (working recursive-tree probe validates correctly). IGNORED in 2020-12 (True/0). A self-referential {"$recursiveAnchor":true,"$recursiveRef":"#"} under 2019-09 → RecursionError exit 1; the same under 2020-12 → True/0.
$ref siblings: draft7 ignores all sibling keywords when $ref is present ({"$ref":R,"maximum":0} → 1 error only from R); 2019-09/2020-12 evaluate $ref AND siblings (2 top-level errors). Self $ref "#" at root → RecursionError exit 1. Unresolvable "#/$defs/NOPE" → exit 1 crash in all modern drafts.
$anchor: honored in both 2019-09 and 2020-12; a syntactically invalid $anchor ("bad anchor!") does not crash if never referenced.
contains: ignored in draft3/4; honored draft6,7,2019-09,2020-12. minContains/maxContains: ignored in draft3,4,6,7; honored only in 2019-09/2020-12. Both are ignored entirely if "contains" is absent.
exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum: boolean modifier form in draft3/4, numeric standalone in draft6+ (unchanged for 2019-09/2020-12); the wrong form is simply ignored.
$vocabulary: totally ignored in every draft and at every position ($vocabulary:{} / "nope" / disabling applicator vocab all have zero effect and never crash).
Annotations title, description, default, examples, $comment, deprecated, readOnly, writeOnly: all ignored in all drafts (True/0), including nested inside properties.
Unknown keywords (e.g. fooBarBaz) ignored everywhere.

=== ERROR COUNTING ===
Every keyword's errors that come from descending (properties, patternProperties, additionalProperties, items, prefixItems, allOf, $ref, dependentSchemas, then/else, contains-count) appear as separate TOP-LEVEL errors; anyOf/oneOf/not/if aggregate into a single top-level error with sub-errors in .context.
- properties: one error per failing property (3 bad props = 3 errors). Nested property failures bubble to top level individually (one per leaf failure), e.g. {"a":{"b":{"c":1}}} with 3-deep properties → 1 error.
- additionalProperties:false → exactly ONE aggregated error no matter how many extra keys.
- required:["b","c"] → one error per missing key (2). dependentRequired:{"a":["b","c"]} → 2 errors (one per missing dependency). Two dependent keys each missing one → 2 errors. dependentRequired:{"a":"b"} (string) does not crash: the string is iterated per character.
- dependentSchemas: descended errors surface at top level (2 failing dependencies → 2 errors); dependentSchemas:{"a":false} → 1 error.
- 2020-12 items (schema form) → one error per failing item (5 bad items = 5). 2020-12 items:false → exactly ONE aggregated error regardless of how many items exceed prefixItems (["...x5"] → 1). 2019-09 items:false → one error PER item (5 items = 5 errors). This is the single biggest counting difference between the two modern drafts.
- 2019-09 additionalItems:false → ONE aggregated error; additionalItems:{schema} → one error per extra failing item.
- contains: always exactly 1 top-level error when it fails (sub-errors are not surfaced); the same single error covers min/maxContains violations.
- unevaluatedProperties: ALWAYS exactly ONE top-level error, no matter how many keys are unevaluated and no matter whether unevaluatedProperties is false or a schema (4 unevaluated failing keys → 1 error). Same for unevaluatedItems: always exactly ONE error.

=== unevaluatedProperties / unevaluatedItems SEMANTICS (2019-09 and 2020-12 only) ===
Both are silently ignored in draft3/4/6/7. Applied only to objects (unevaluatedProperties) / arrays (unevaluatedItems); ignored for other instance types, so {"unevaluatedProperties":false,"unevaluatedItems":false} on "s" or 5 is True/0, and on {"a":1,"b":2} only the properties one fires (1 error). Empty object/array → always valid. Value true → always valid.
CRUCIAL: jsonschema does NOT implement real annotation collection. The set of "evaluated" keys/indexes is computed by a LOCAL, purely structural walk of the SAME schema object that carries the unevaluated* keyword (recursing into that object's $ref, $recursiveRef, allOf/anyOf/oneOf branches, if/then/else, dependentSchemas). Consequences:
 - A sibling of the PARENT is invisible: {"allOf":[{"unevaluatedProperties":false}],"properties":{"a":{}}} on {"a":1} → 1 error (the outer properties annotation is not seen). Likewise {"allOf":[{"properties":{"a":{}}},{"unevaluatedProperties":false}]} → 1 error (sister allOf branch invisible), and {"$ref":"#/$defs/R","$defs":{"R":{"unevaluatedProperties":false}},"properties":{"a":{}}} → 1 error.
 - Move both into the same schema object and it works: {"$defs":{"X":{"unevaluatedProperties":false,"properties":{"a":{}}}},"allOf":[{"$ref":"#/$defs/X"}]} → True/0.
Contribution rules, in the schema object carrying unevaluated* (and recursively):
 - properties: every instance key that appears in "properties" counts as evaluated REGARDLESS of whether that subschema passed ({"properties":{"a":{"type":"string"}},"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1} → 1 error, not 2). Same for properties:{"a":false}.
 - patternProperties: matching keys count as evaluated regardless of validity.
 - additionalProperties: counts ONLY when its value is boolean true. additionalProperties:{} , {"type":"integer"}, {"minimum":0} and false all contribute NOTHING ({"additionalProperties":{"type":"integer"},"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1} → 1 error even though the additionalProperties schema passes). Same rule for a nested unevaluatedProperties: only literal true contributes to an outer unevaluated*.
 - propertyNames contributes nothing.
 - allOf / anyOf / oneOf: a branch contributes its evaluated keys ONLY IF that branch VALIDATES SUCCESSFULLY. Failing branches contribute nothing ({"allOf":[{"properties":{"a":{"type":"string"}}}],"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1} → 2 errors: the type error plus the unevaluated error). Successful branches contribute even when the enclosing keyword still fails overall — e.g. oneOf with two matching branches yields the oneOf error but no unevaluated error if the matching branches covered every key ({"oneOf":[{"properties":{"a":{}}},{"properties":{"a":{}}}],"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1,"b":2,"c":3} → 2 errors; on {"a":1} with second branch {} → 1 error).
 - $ref: contributes UNCONDITIONALLY (no validity check) — {"$ref":"#/$defs/R","$defs":{"R":{"properties":{"a":{"type":"string"}}}},"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1} → 1 error only. Note the asymmetry with allOf. $ref chains and $ref-with-siblings inside the target both contribute.
 - dependentSchemas: contributes unconditionally for every dependency key present in the instance (validity of the dependent schema irrelevant); dependencies whose key is absent contribute nothing.
 - if/then/else: "if" contributes its own evaluated keys only when "if" VALIDATES. If "if" validates, "then" contributes unconditionally (even if "then" then fails); if "if" fails, "else" contributes unconditionally. A failing "if" contributes nothing. "then"/"else" without an "if" are ignored entirely and contribute nothing.
 - not: NEVER contributes, whether it passes or fails.
 - contains: matched indexes count as evaluated for unevaluatedItems in BOTH 2019-09 and 2020-12 (jsonschema does not follow the 2019-09 spec here). [2] + contains:{const:2} + unevaluatedItems:false → True/0; [1,2] → 1 error; [2,2] → True/0; contains:{type:"integer"} on [1,2,3] → True/0. BUT if the contains keyword itself fails (including via maxContains/minContains bounds) nothing is marked evaluated: [1,2] with contains:{const:1},maxContains:0 → 2 errors.
 - items/prefixItems/additionalItems for unevaluatedItems: 2019-09 — object-form "items" marks ALL indexes evaluated; array-form "items" marks indexes 0..len(items)-1 (excess left unevaluated); the PRESENCE of "additionalItems" together with array-form "items" marks ALL indexes evaluated regardless of the additionalItems value (true, false or a schema); "additionalItems" without array "items" contributes nothing. 2020-12 — prefixItems marks its indexes evaluated (even failing ones), "items" (schema form) marks everything, "items":false also marks everything so {"prefixItems":[{},{}],"items":false,"unevaluatedItems":false} on [1,2] is True/0.
 - unevaluated* nest correctly through properties/prefixItems into child objects/arrays (each level computes independently).

=== CRASHES (exit 1, Python traceback on stderr, EMPTY stdout) ===
1. 2020-12 + array-form "items" + array instance → AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' (referencing). Also triggered by {"items":[...],"additionalItems":...} under 2020-12.
2. 2020-12 + non-array, non-empty object "prefixItems" (e.g. {"type":"string"}) with an array instance.
3. 2019-09 + "unevaluatedItems" together with a BOOLEAN "items" (true or false) and an array instance → TypeError: object of type 'bool' has no len() in _legacy_keywords.find_evaluated_item_indexes_by_schema. (items:{} and items:[...] are fine.)
4. minContains/maxContains with a non-number value ("0", "2") and a "contains" present, array instance → TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'str'.
5. Unresolvable $ref ("#/$defs/NOPE"); unresolvable $dynamicRef ("#NOPE") under 2020-12 only; "$ref":"#N" pointing at a $dynamicAnchor under 2019-09.
6. Self-recursive refs: {"$ref":"#"} at root, {"$recursiveAnchor":true,"$recursiveRef":"#"} under 2019-09, {"$dynamicAnchor":"X","$dynamicRef":"#X"} at root under 2020-12 → RecursionError.
Negative bounds do NOT crash: minContains:-1 → passes; maxContains:-1 → 1 error.
gotchas: 2020-12 CRASHES (exit 1, empty stdout, AttributeError from referencing) on array-form `items` when the instance is an array — it is not merely ignored. Non-array instances are fine because the keyword never descends.

`dependencies` (both array and schema form) is COMPLETELY IGNORED in 2019-09 and 2020-12 — implementers usually keep it as an alias for dependentRequired/dependentSchemas. It is not even type-checked (`"dependencies":5` → True/0).

`prefixItems` is NOT supported in 2019-09 (silently ignored, contributes nothing to unevaluatedItems). `$recursiveRef`/`$recursiveAnchor` are supported ONLY in 2019-09 and silently ignored in 2020-12. `$dynamicRef`/`$dynamicAnchor` are supported ONLY in 2020-12 and silently ignored in 2019-09 (an unresolvable `$dynamicRef` is a no-op in 2019-09 but a crash in 2020-12).
unevaluatedProperties and unevaluatedItems each emit EXACTLY ONE top-level error no matter how many keys/indexes are unevaluated or invalid — never one per key.

jsonschema does not do real annotation collection: unevaluated* only inspects the schema object it sits in (recursing into that object's $ref/allOf/anyOf/oneOf/if-then-else/dependentSchemas). Sibling-of-parent and sister-allOf-branch annotations are INVISIBLE, so `{"allOf":[{"unevaluatedProperties":false}],"properties":{"a":{}}}` reports 'a' as unevaluated (spec-noncompliant, but must be replicated).

Validity gating is inconsistent per keyword: adjacent `properties`/`patternProperties` mark keys evaluated even when the subschema FAILS; `$ref` and `dependentSchemas` contribute unconditionally; but allOf/anyOf/oneOf branches contribute only if the branch is_valid; `not` never contributes; `if` contributes only when it validates, while `then`/`else` contribute unconditionally once selected.

`additionalProperties` contributes evaluated keys ONLY when it is literal boolean `true`. `additionalProperties: {}` or `{"type":"integer"}` contributes NOTHING even though they accept everything. Same rule for a nested `unevaluatedProperties`. By contrast, in 2019-09 the mere PRESENCE of `additionalItems` alongside array-form `items` marks every index evaluated regardless of its value (true/false/schema).

`contains` marks matched indexes as evaluated for unevaluatedItems in BOTH 2019-09 and 2020-12 (not just 2020-12) — but only when the contains keyword itself passes; a min/maxContains violation suppresses all of that evaluation and yields 2 errors.

Error-count asymmetry for `items: false`: 2019-09 yields one error PER item (N errors), 2020-12 yields exactly ONE aggregated error. 2019-09 `additionalItems: false` also yields one aggregated error, while `additionalItems: {schema}` yields one error per failing extra item.

`minContains: 0` makes `contains` pass unconditionally (even `contains: false`, even on an empty array) in 2019-09/2020-12 only; minContains/maxContains are ignored without `contains` and ignored entirely in draft6/7. A non-numeric minContains/maxContains crashes with TypeError.
2019-09 crashes with `TypeError: object of type 'bool' has no len()` when `unevaluatedItems` is combined with a BOOLEAN `items` (true or false) on an array instance — an easy-to-miss legacy-path bug.
In 2019-09/2020-12, `$ref` no longer suppresses sibling keywords (unlike draft7), so `{"$ref":R,"maximum":0}` can produce 2 top-level errors where draft7 produces 1.

`$vocabulary` is inert everywhere; `deprecated`/`readOnly`/`writeOnly`/`title`/`description`/`default`/`examples`/`$comment` are inert everywhere; unknown keywords are inert. None of them affect unevaluated* evaluation either.

result.family: Object keywords across drafts (properties, patternProperties, additionalProperties, required, dependencies/dependentRequired/dependentSchemas, propertyNames, min/maxProperties, unevaluatedProperties, draft3 extends)
result.findings:
ALL object keywords are no-ops when the instance is not a JSON object (array, null, string, number) — verified with a schema stacking properties+patternProperties+additionalProperties:false+required+minProperties+propertyNames against [1] and null: True/0 in every draft.

PROPERTIES (all drafts, identical): each failing (property, keyword) pair yields ONE top-level error. 3 props each failing type => 3. One prop failing two keywords (type+minLength) => 2. Two props each failing two keywords => 4. Nested descent flattens: {"o":{"p":"s","q":"t"}} with properties.o.properties.{p,q}:integer => 2 top-level errors; 3-level nesting with one leaf failure => 1. Properties not present in the instance are skipped. Boolean subschemas work: properties:{a:false,b:false} with both present => 2; properties:{a:true} => 0. `properties` whose value is not an object CRASHES: {"properties":["a"]} or "a" => exit 1, AttributeError: 'list'/'str' object has no attribute 'items' at jsonschema/_keywords.py:294.

PATTERNPROPERTIES (all drafts incl. draft3): regex is SEARCH, not fullmatch — pattern "a" matches key "xay" (1 error). A key matching N patterns is validated against ALL N subschemas and yields N separate top-level errors: {"abc":"s"} with patterns "^a"(integer) and "c$"(boolean) => 2; with 3 matching patterns all failing => 3. Boolean false subschema per matching key: {"pa":1,"pb":2} with patternProperties{"^p":false} => 2. A key covered by BOTH properties and patternProperties is validated by both: {"pa":"s"} with properties.pa:integer + patternProperties."^p":boolean => 2. Invalid regex CRASHES at validation time: patternProperties:{"[":{...}} => exit 1, re.error: unterminated character set. Non-object patternProperties (a list) => exit 1, AttributeError ... 'items' at _keywords.py:20.

ADDITIONALPROPERTIES (all drafts incl. draft3): "extra" = instance keys not in `properties` and not matching any `patternProperties` regex (properties keys count as covered even if absent from the instance... more precisely, a key present in the instance and named in `properties` is not extra; properties entries absent from the instance are irrelevant). CRITICAL COUNTING ASYMMETRY: additionalProperties:false yields exactly ONE aggregate error no matter how many extras (1 extra => 1, 3 extras => 1, 5 extras => 1); additionalProperties as a SCHEMA yields ONE ERROR PER FAILING EXTRA PROPERTY (3 failing extras => 3, 5 => 5). Zero extras => 0 errors either way. Combined: {"a":1,"pb":2,"zz":3,"yy":4} with properties{a},patternProperties{"^p"},additionalProperties:false => 1 (both extras folded into one error); same shape with additionalProperties:{type:"integer"} and 2 failing extras => 2. Non-boolean, non-object additionalProperties uses PYTHON TRUTHINESS: falsy values 0, "", null, [] all behave exactly like `false` (1 aggregate error when extras exist, 0 when none); truthy non-object values like "nope" or 5 are silently ignored (0 errors, no crash). properties:{},patternProperties:{},additionalProperties:false with one key => 1.

REQUIRED — array form (draft4/6/7/2019-09/2020-12 only): one top-level error PER MISSING ENTRY. 3 missing => 3, 5 missing => 5, 1 missing of 3 => 1, none missing => 0. Duplicates are NOT deduplicated: required:["a","a","b"] with {} => 3 errors. Non-string entries are compared as-is: required:[1,2] with {} => 2 errors. required:[] => 0. A key present with value null or false satisfies required (0 errors). DRAFT3 IGNORES array-form `required` entirely at top level (True/0 even with 5 missing) — draft3 has no top-level required validator at all. Malformed forms in draft4+: required:true or required:false CRASHES (exit 1, TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable at _keywords.py:307, raised from the is_valid call); required:5 CRASHES the same way; required:"abc" does NOT crash — Python iterates the string char-by-char, so {} => 3 errors (a,b,c) and {"a":1,"b":1,"c":1} => 0; required:{"a":1} iterates dict keys => 1 error. All of these malformed forms are silently ignored in draft3 (True/0).

REQUIRED — draft3 boolean form inside a property subschema: {"properties":{"a":{"required":true},...}} yields one error per missing required property (3 missing => 3, 1 missing => 1). It uses PYTHON TRUTHINESS of the `required` value, not strict boolean: required:1 => required, required:"x" => required, required:["x"] (non-empty array!) => required (so {"properties":{"a":{"required":["x"]}}} with {} gives 1 error in draft3), while required:false, 0, "", [], {} => not required. When the property IS present, draft3 required contributes nothing and the rest of the subschema still applies ({"a":"s"} with {required:true,type:"integer"} => 1). In draft4+ a boolean `required` nested inside a property subschema is harmless when the property is ABSENT (subschema never runs => 0 errors), but would crash if the property were present with a bool/number required.

DEPENDENCIES (draft3, draft4, draft6, draft7 ONLY — COMPLETELY REMOVED in 2019-09 and 2020-12, where it is silently ignored: every dependencies probe under d19/d20 returned True/0, including malformed dependencies:"garbage" and dependencies:{a:false}, which do not even crash there). Trigger key absent => no evaluation. Array-of-strings form: one error per missing dependency (3 missing => 3); non-string array elements compared as-is ([1,2] => 2 errors); empty array => 0. Two triggers each missing one dep => 2. Schema form: the dependency subschema's errors bubble up as separate TOP-LEVEL errors (2 failing props inside the dependency schema => 2; a dependency schema with required:["x","y"] => 2 in draft4/6/7 but 0 in draft3 since draft3 lacks array-required; a dependency schema with additionalProperties:false => 1). Boolean schema values: draft4/6/7 accept dependencies:{a:false} => 1 error and dependencies:{a:true} => 0; DRAFT3 CRASHES on both (exit 1, TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable at _legacy_keywords.py:41 dependencies_draft3). Single-string form: ONLY draft3 supports it (dependencies:{a:"x"} with {"a":1} => 1 error, with {"a":1,"x":2} => 0); draft4/6/7 CRASH on a string dependency (exit 1, AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get' in referencing/jsonschema.py:56 _legacy_dollar_id, reached via validators.py:421 descend — i.e. they try to treat the string as a subschema). A trigger key whose value is null still triggers.

DEPENDENTREQUIRED / DEPENDENTSCHEMAS (2019-09 and 2020-12 ONLY; silently ignored — True/0 — in draft3/4/6/7). dependentRequired: one error per missing entry (3 missing => 3). Its value is iterated with Python semantics, so a STRING value iterates characters: dependentRequired:{a:"x"} => 1 error, {a:"xy"} => 2 errors. dependentRequired:{a:true} CRASHES (exit 1, 'bool' object is not iterable). dependentSchemas: subschema errors bubble to top level (1 failing prop => 1; required:["x","y"] inside => 2); dependentSchemas:{a:false} => 1 error; dependentSchemas:{a:"x"} CRASHES (exit 1, AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get', referencing/jsonschema.py:50 _dollar_id). Trigger key with null value still triggers.

PROPERTYNAMES (draft6+ ONLY; silently ignored in draft3 and draft4 — True/0 even when every name violates). Each (failing name, failing keyword) pair is a separate top-level error: 2 bad names with maxLength:1 => 2; 1 name failing both maxLength and pattern => 2; 2 names each failing 2 keywords => 4. propertyNames:false with 2 keys => 2 errors (one per key); propertyNames:true => 0. Empty object => 0 regardless. Names are always validated as STRINGS, so propertyNames:{type:"integer"} fails for every key (1 key => 1) and {"12":1} passes {type:"string"}; propertyNames:{minLength:1} rejects the empty-string key. propertyNames:"x" (non-schema) CRASHES in draft6+ (exit 1, AttributeError 'str' has no attribute 'get') but is ignored in draft3/4.

MINPROPERTIES / MAXPROPERTIES (draft4+ ONLY; silently ignored in draft3). Exactly 1 error each when violated; both violated => 2. maxProperties:0 with {} => 0. minProperties:-1 => 0. Floats work: maxProperties:1.5 with 2 keys => 1 error; minProperties:1.0 with 1 key => 0. A string bound CRASHES in draft4+ (exit 1, TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'str' at _keywords.py:313) but is ignored in draft3.

UNEVALUATEDPROPERTIES (2019-09 and 2020-12 ONLY; silently ignored in draft3/4/6/7 — {x,y} with unevaluatedProperties:false => True/0 there). ALWAYS YIELDS AT MOST ONE TOP-LEVEL ERROR, aggregating all unevaluated keys — 3 unevaluated => 1, 5 unevaluated => 1. Even in SCHEMA form it collapses to 1: unevaluatedProperties:{type:"integer"} with 3 failing string props => 1 error (contrast additionalProperties schema form, which gives 3). With 3 props all passing the schema => 0; 1 of 3 failing => 1. unevaluatedProperties:true or {} => 0. Non-object instance => 0. Values that are neither boolean nor object CRASH: unevaluatedProperties:"nope" and unevaluatedProperties:0 both exit 1 (AttributeError 'str'/'int' has no attribute 'get' — it is descended into as a subschema).
  Annotation sources that DO mark keys evaluated: `properties` (marks the key EVEN IF ITS SUBSCHEMA FAILS — {"a":"s"} with properties.a:integer + unevaluatedProperties:false => 1 error total, the type error only, proving 'a' was still annotated); `patternProperties` (real regex matching, correct); `unevaluatedProperties:true`; passing `allOf` branches; passing `anyOf`/`oneOf` branches only; `if` (annotates when the if-subschema PASSES, even with no then/else); `then`/`else` when taken; a successfully-applied `$ref`; `dependentSchemas` when triggered; and $ref together with sibling `properties` in 2019-09/2020-12 (both annotate). Nested allOf-within-allOf annotations propagate up correctly.
  Annotation sources that DO NOT mark keys evaluated: `required`, `minProperties`/`maxProperties`, `propertyNames`, `dependentRequired`, an untriggered `dependentSchemas`, a FAILING allOf branch (allOf:[{properties:{a:{type:"integer"}}}] with {"a":"s"} => 2 errors: the type error plus the unevaluated error, whereas the same properties at top level gives only 1), a failing anyOf/oneOf branch (anyOf:[{properties:{a:{}}},{properties:{b:{type:"integer"}},required:["b"]}] with {"a":1,"b":"s"} => 1 unevaluated error because branch 2 failed), an `if` whose subschema FAILS, a `$ref` resolving to `false`, and the subschema inside `not` (not:{properties:{a:{type:"string"}},required:["a"]} with {"a":1} => 1 unevaluated error). `dependencies` cannot annotate in 2019-09/2020-12 because the keyword no longer exists there.
  MAJOR IMPLEMENTATION BUG TO REPLICATE — additionalProperties annotation is key-based, not value-based: for `additionalProperties`, the annotation collector treats the subschema as a mapping and marks as evaluated any instance key that is literally a KEY OF THAT SUBSCHEMA OBJECT (not the properties the keyword actually applied to). Consequences, all verified: additionalProperties:true + unevaluatedProperties:false with {x,y} => 0 errors (boolean true marks every instance key), but additionalProperties:{} => 1 error, additionalProperties:{type:"integer"} with {"x":1,"y":2} (both passing) => 1 error, additionalProperties:{type:"integer"} with instance {"type":1} => 0 ERRORS (the key named "type" is "evaluated" because "type" is a key of the subschema), {"type":1,"y":2} => 1, additionalProperties:{minLength:2} with instance {"minLength":"aaa"} => 0, and additionalProperties:{type:"integer"} with {"q":1} => 1. The same key-based hack applies to a nested `unevaluatedProperties` used as an annotation source: allOf:[{unevaluatedProperties:{type:"integer"}}] + outer unevaluatedProperties:false gives 0 for instance {"type":1} but 1 for {"q":1}; allOf:[{unevaluatedProperties:true}] gives 0. `properties` happens to look correct under this scheme because its keys ARE property names.
  Stacking: additionalProperties:false + unevaluatedProperties:false with 3 extras => 2 errors (1 aggregate additionalProperties + 1 aggregate unevaluated); additionalProperties:false with 1 extra + unevaluatedProperties:false => 2 in 2019/2020 vs 1 in draft3-7. A nested unevaluatedProperties inside an anyOf branch that fails produces 1 top-level anyOf error.

DRAFT3 `extends` (draft3 ONLY; silently ignored in draft4/7/2020-12). Single-schema form: the extended schema's errors bubble up as separate top-level errors (1 failing prop => 1, 2 failing props => 2). Array form: errors from all elements bubble up (2 elements each failing => 2); all passing => 0; extends:[] => 0. extends combined with local keywords accumulates: extends:{properties:{a:{type:"integer"}}} + properties:{a:{type:"boolean"}} with {"a":"s"} => 2. Draft3 `required:true` inside an extends subschema works => 1. extends:true CRASHES (exit 1, TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable at _legacy_keywords.py:88 extends_draft3).

ACCUMULATION SANITY CHECK: instance {"a":"s","x":1,"y":2} against {properties:{a:{type:"integer"}}, additionalProperties:false, required:["q","r"], minProperties:9, maxProperties:1} gives 6 in draft4/6/7/2019/2020 (1 properties + 1 aggregate additionalProperties + 2 required + 1 minProperties + 1 maxProperties) and 2 in draft3 (properties + additionalProperties only, since required-array/minProperties/maxProperties do not exist there).

$REF SIBLING NOTE (affects object-keyword counting): in draft4/6/7 a sibling `properties` or `required` next to `$ref` is IGNORED (=> 1 error from the ref target only), while in 2019-09/2020-12 both apply (=> 2 errors).

CRASH SUMMARY (all exit code 1, full Python traceback on stderr, empty stdout — the exception is raised from the `is_valid` call at test13.py line 18, so nothing is printed at all): required:true/false/number (draft4+); dependencies:{k:"string"} (draft4/6/7); dependencies:{k:bool} (draft3); extends:true (draft3); dependentRequired:{k:true} and dependentSchemas:{k:"string"} (2019/2020); unevaluatedProperties: non-bool non-object (2019/2020); propertyNames: non-schema (draft6+); minProperties/maxProperties: string (draft4+); properties or patternProperties not an object (all drafts); invalid regex in patternProperties (all drafts).
gotchas: additionalProperties:false yields exactly ONE aggregate error regardless of how many extra properties (3 extras => 1 error), but additionalProperties as a SCHEMA yields ONE ERROR PER FAILING EXTRA (3 failing extras => 3 errors). Same keyword, two totally different counting rules.
unevaluatedProperties ALWAYS yields at most 1 top-level error, even in schema form with 3 failing properties (=> 1, not 3). This is the opposite of additionalProperties schema form.
Non-boolean, non-object additionalProperties uses Python truthiness: 0, "", null, and [] all behave exactly like false (aggregate error); "nope" and 5 are silently ignored with 0 errors.

required is iterated with Python semantics and NOT deduplicated: required:["a","a","b"] with {} => 3 errors; required:"abc" iterates characters => 3 errors; required:{"a":1} iterates dict keys => 1 error; but required:true/false/5 CRASHES with TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable.

Draft3 completely IGNORES array-form top-level `required` (0 errors even with 5 missing), and ignores minProperties/maxProperties/propertyNames/unevaluatedProperties/dependentRequired/dependentSchemas. Conversely draft4+ ignores draft3's boolean `required` inside property subschemas (when the property is absent) and ignores `extends`.

Draft3 `required` inside a property subschema tests PYTHON TRUTHINESS, not strict boolean: required:["x"] (a non-empty array) makes the property required, as do 1 and "x"; required:[] , {}, 0, "" do not.

`dependencies` is COMPLETELY REMOVED in 2019-09 and 2020-12 — silently ignored, 0 errors, and even malformed values like dependencies:"garbage" or {a:false} do not crash there. Conversely dependentRequired/dependentSchemas are silently ignored in draft3/4/6/7.

Single-string dependency (dependencies:{a:"x"}) is valid ONLY in draft3; in draft4/6/7 it CRASHES (AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get') because it is descended into as a subschema. Boolean dependency values are the mirror image: fine in draft4+, CRASH in draft3.

THE BIG ONE — unevaluatedProperties annotation for `additionalProperties` is key-based, not value-based: it marks instance keys that are literally KEYS OF THE additionalProperties SUBSCHEMA OBJECT. So additionalProperties:{type:"integer"} + unevaluatedProperties:false marks a property named "type" as evaluated (instance {"type":1} => 0 errors) while marking normal properties unevaluated ({"q":1} => 1 error). additionalProperties:true marks everything; additionalProperties:{} marks nothing. The same key-hack applies to a nested `unevaluatedProperties` used as an annotation source.

Top-level `properties` annotates a key for unevaluatedProperties EVEN WHEN THE SUBSCHEMA FAILS ({"a":"s"} + properties.a:integer + unevaluatedProperties:false => 1 error), but the identical `properties` inside a FAILING allOf branch does NOT annotate (=> 2 errors). Branch keywords (allOf/anyOf/oneOf/if/$ref) are validity-gated; in-place keywords are not.
`if` annotates for unevaluatedProperties whenever the if-subschema passes, even with no then/else. A failing `if`, a failing $ref (to false), and the subschema inside `not` never annotate.

patternProperties uses regex SEARCH (unanchored) — pattern "a" matches key "xay" — and a key matching N patterns produces N separate errors, plus additional errors if the key is also under `properties`.
propertyNames is draft6+ only and produces one error per (failing key, failing keyword) pair — 2 keys each failing 2 keywords => 4 errors; propertyNames:false with 2 keys => 2 errors (not 1).

Malformed schemas crash the whole program (exit 1, traceback, EMPTY stdout — no validator name line is printed) because the exception is raised inside the is_valid call. Crashers include: non-object properties/patternProperties, invalid regex, string min/maxProperties (draft4+), non-schema propertyNames (draft6+), extends:true (draft3), unevaluatedProperties as a non-bool scalar.
In draft4/6/7 sibling object keywords next to $ref are ignored (1 error), while in 2019-09/2020-12 they apply alongside the ref (2 errors) — this silently changes object-keyword error counts.
A key present with value null or false satisfies `required` and still triggers `dependencies`/`dependentRequired`; presence is key-membership, not truthiness.

result.family: Array keywords across drafts (items / prefixItems / additionalItems / contains / minContains / maxContains / uniqueItems / minItems / maxItems / unevaluatedItems)
result.findings:
All results below are OBSERVED from 528 black-box runs of /workspace/dataset/test13_executable. Line 3 = number of TOP-LEVEL errors from iter_errors.

DISPATCH: `items` has three distinct implementations. (A) draft3/draft4 -> `_legacy_keywords.items_draft3_draft4`; (B) draft6/draft7/2019-09 -> legacy items_draft6_draft7_draft201909; (C) 2020-12 -> `_keywords.items` (pure "applies to every element at index >= len(prefixItems)").

items AS A SINGLE SCHEMA: identical in every draft. `{"items":{"type":"string"}}` on [1,2,3] -> False/3. Each element yields its OWN top-level error, and each FAILING KEYWORD inside the subschema also yields its own top-level error: `{"items":{"type":"string","minimum":10}}` on [1,2,3] -> 6 errors; `{"items":{"type":"integer","minLength":5}}` on ["a","b"] -> 4. Descended errors nest multiplicatively: `{"items":{"items":{"type":"string"}}}` on [[1,2],[3,4]] -> 4; `{"items":{"properties":{"a":{...},"b":{...}}}}` on two bad objects -> 4; `{"items":{"items":{"type":"integer"},"minItems":3}}` on [[1,2],[3,"x"]] -> 3. `items` never fires on non-array instances (0 errors, all drafts).

items AS AN ARRAY (tuple form): works in draft3, draft4, draft6, draft7 AND 2019-09 (all yield identical counts). [1,2,3] with items:[str,str,str] -> 3; items:[str] -> 1 (only index 0 checked); items:[] -> True/0; a tuple LONGER than the instance only checks min(len) positions (items:[{},{},{},{}] on [1,2,3] -> 0 errors; four failing schemas on a 3-array -> 3 errors). In 2020-12 array-form items is NOT tuple validation and NOT ignored — it CRASHES: `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'` raised from jsonschema/_keywords.py line 78 (items) -> validators.descend -> referencing/jsonschema.py `_dollar_id`, exit code 1, empty stdout, traceback on stderr. The crash happens only if at least one element is actually descended into: 2020-12 items:[...] on [] or on a non-array instance -> True/0 (no crash), and prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + items:[{"type":"string"}] on [1,2,3] -> True/0 (no leftover elements), but the same schema on [1,2,3,4] -> crash. Any non-boolean, non-object items value (string, number) crashes the same way in every draft that treats it as a schema (2020-12, 2019-09, draft6, draft7, draft4/3 crash too but with the bool/iterate path or descend path).

items AS A BOOLEAN: draft3 and draft4 CRASH unconditionally on items:true and items:false (`TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable` at _legacy_keywords.py line 100 items_draft3_draft4), exit 1 — and it crashes even for the EMPTY array [] (only a non-array instance escapes, giving True/0). draft6/draft7/2019-09 treat boolean items as a schema applied to every element: items:false on [1,2,3] -> 3 errors (one per element), on [] -> 0; items:true -> 0. 2020-12 special-cases false: items:false on [1,2,3] -> exactly 1 error (an aggregate "too many items" error), prefixItems:[{"type":"integer"}] + items:false on [1,2,3] -> 1, prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + items:false on a 10-element array -> 1, on [] -> 0.

prefixItems: recognized ONLY by 2020-12. Completely ignored (0 errors) in draft3/4/6/7 AND 2019-09. 2020-12: prefixItems:[str,str,str] on [1,2,3] -> 3 errors; prefixItems:[str] -> 1; prefixItems:[] -> no-op; prefixItems:[true,false,true] on [1,2,3] -> 1 (the `false` at index 1). prefixItems must be a LIST: prefixItems:{} (empty object) -> True/0 by accident (zip over zero keys), prefixItems:{"a":{...}} (non-empty object) -> CRASH, prefixItems:true -> CRASH, prefixItems:"xyz" -> CRASH (exit 1). In 2020-12, `items` starts at index len(prefixItems).

additionalItems: honored in draft3, draft4, draft6, draft7, 2019-09; IGNORED entirely in 2020-12 (prefixItems + additionalItems:false -> True/0). Guard semantics: additionalItems does nothing unless `items` is present AND is a list. items absent -> ignored; items a dict/object -> ignored (items:{"type":"integer"} + additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> True/0); items a BOOLEAN -> CRASH `TypeError: object of type 'bool' has no len()` at _legacy_keywords.py line 113 additionalItems, in draft3/4 (crashes earlier in items), draft6, draft7 and 2019-09; a non-array instance escapes the crash (True/0). Counting: additionalItems:false yields exactly ONE aggregate error no matter how many extras (items:[{}] + additionalItems:false on a 5-array -> 1; items:[{},{},{}] + additionalItems:false on a 10-array -> 1). additionalItems as a SCHEMA yields one error PER extra element per failing keyword (items:[{}] + additionalItems:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 2; on [1..5] -> 4). Tuple errors and additionalItems errors ADD: items:[int] + additionalItems:{int} on ["a","b","c"] -> 3 (1 tuple + 2 additional); items:[int,int] + additionalItems:false on ["a","b","c","d"] -> 3 (2 tuple + 1 aggregate); items:[false] + additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 2.

contains: ignored in draft3 and draft4 (always 0 errors). Present in draft6+, and always yields AT MOST 1 top-level error (sub-errors go into context). `{"contains":{"type":"string"}}` on [1,2,3] -> 1; on [1,"a",3] -> 0; on [] -> 1 in draft6/7/2019-09/2020-12 (empty array always fails contains unless minContains:0); `contains:true` on [] -> 1; `contains:false` on [1] -> 1. Non-array instance -> 0. contains:"xyz" (non-schema) -> CRASH.

minContains/maxContains: recognized only in 2019-09 and 2020-12; silently ignored in draft6/draft7 (which still apply plain contains with an implicit min of 1). Key cross-draft divergence: `{"contains":{"type":"string"},"minContains":0}` on [1,2,3] or on [] gives False/1 in draft6 and draft7 (minContains ignored, contains still requires a match) but True/0 in 2019-09 and 2020-12. minContains/maxContains without `contains` are inert in every draft (0 errors). The contains family emits at most ONE error total: minContains:5 + maxContains:1 with 0 matches -> 1; minContains:2 + maxContains:1 with 3 matches -> 1 (only the maxContains violation); minContains:0 + maxContains:0 with 1 match -> 1; minContains:0 + maxContains:0 on [] -> 0. Floats work (minContains:2.0 -> ok with 3 matches); negative minContains:-1 -> ok. minContains:"x" -> CRASH.

uniqueItems: identical in every draft (draft3 through 2020-12), always at most ONE error regardless of how many duplicate groups ([1,1,2,2,3,3] -> 1; 200-element array with one dup -> 1; 500 objects with one dup -> 1). Equality is Python-like but with an explicit bool/number distinction: 1 vs 1.0 EQUAL (dup), 100 vs 1e2 EQUAL, 0 vs -0 EQUAL, [1] vs [1.0] EQUAL, {"a":1,"b":2} vs {"b":2,"a":1} EQUAL (key order irrelevant), [null,null] dup, ["a","a"] dup, [[1],[1]] dup, [{},{}] dup, [[[1],"a"],[[1],"a"]] dup. But booleans are NEVER equal to numbers at ANY depth: [1,true] unique, [0,false] unique, [{"a":false},{"a":0}] unique, [[false],[0]] unique, [{"a":[true]},{"a":[1]}] unique, [[{"x":true}],[{"x":1}]] unique. Cross-type non-equalities: [] vs {} unique, {} vs [] unique, "" vs 0 unique, null vs false unique, null vs 0 unique, 1 vs "1" unique. uniqueItems is TRUTHY-tested, not strictly boolean: uniqueItems:"yes" and uniqueItems:1 enforce uniqueness; uniqueItems:0 and uniqueItems:false do not. Non-array instances (strings, objects) -> 0 errors even with repeated chars/keys.

minItems/maxItems: identical in all drafts, one error each, and they ADD: {"minItems":5,"maxItems":1} on [1,2,3] -> 2 errors. minItems:3 on [1] -> 1; maxItems:1 on [1,2,3] -> 1; maxItems:0 on [1] -> 1; minItems:0 -> 0; minItems:-1 -> 0; floats compare numerically (minItems:2.5 on [1,2,3] -> 0, maxItems:2.5 on [1,2,3] -> 1). Non-array instance -> 0. Non-numeric values CRASH: minItems:"3" -> TypeError, maxItems:null -> TypeError (exit 1).

unevaluatedItems: recognized ONLY in 2019-09 and 2020-12; completely ignored (0 errors) in draft3/4/6/7. It yields AT MOST ONE top-level error, ever, regardless of how many items are unevaluated or how many keywords in its subschema fail: unevaluatedItems:false on a 10-element array -> 1; unevaluatedItems:{"minLength":5} on ["a","b","c"] -> 1; unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer","minLength":5} on ["a","b","c"] -> 1. Crucially it is NOT a plain "no unevaluated items allowed" check — the subschema is actually applied and the error only appears if some unevaluated item FAILS it: unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer"} on [1,2,3] -> True/0, on [1,"a"] -> 1, on ["a","b"] -> 1. unevaluatedItems:true / {} -> 0. Non-array instance -> 0. unevaluatedItems:"xyz" -> CRASH.
  Evaluation tracking (which indexes count as evaluated) is computed from the SAME schema object only, and includes: `items` when it is a schema/bool (marks ALL indexes evaluated, even if items itself produced errors — items:{"type":"string"} + unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 3 errors, not 4; items:{"type":"string"} + unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer"} -> 3, not 4); `items` in tuple form under 2019-09 (items:[{},{},{}] covers all 3 -> 0 errors; items:[{},{}] leaves index 2 -> 1 error); `prefixItems` under 2020-12 only (prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + unevaluatedItems:false -> True/0 in 2020-12 but False/1 in 2019-09 where prefixItems is unknown); `additionalItems` under 2019-09 when items is a tuple (items:[{},{}] + additionalItems:{} + unevaluatedItems:false -> 0; with additionalItems:false -> 1 total, which is the additionalItems aggregate error, not an unevaluatedItems error); `contains` marks ONLY the MATCHING indexes evaluated (contains:{"type":"integer"} on [1,2,3] + unevaluatedItems:false -> 0; on [1,"a",3] index 1 stays unevaluated -> with unevaluatedItems:false -> 1, with unevaluatedItems:{"type":"string"} -> 0, with unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer"} -> 1); and it recurses into allOf, anyOf, oneOf, if/then/else and $ref (allOf:[{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]}] -> 0; allOf:[{prefixItems:[{},{}]}] -> 1; allOf:[{items:{"type":"integer"}}] -> 0; allOf:[{contains:{"type":"integer"}}] -> 0; anyOf/oneOf covering branch -> 0; if:{prefixItems:[{const:1}]} + then:{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]} with matching if -> 0, with non-matching if and no else -> 1; if:{type:"string"} + else:{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]} -> 0; $ref:{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]} -> 0; $ref:{items:{"type":"integer"}} -> 0). `not` does NOT contribute evaluated indexes (not:{...} + unevaluatedItems:false -> 1). unevaluatedItems placed INSIDE an allOf branch does NOT see the parent's sibling prefixItems: {"allOf":[{"unevaluatedItems":false}],"prefixItems":[{},{},{}]} -> False/1.
  unevaluatedItems errors ADD to sibling errors: prefixItems:[{"type":"string"}] + unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 2 (1 prefixItems + 1 unevaluated); anyOf:[failing branch] + unevaluatedItems:false -> 2; contains fails + minContains:1 + unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] with contains:{"type":"string"} -> 2; unevaluatedItems:false + minItems:5 (2019-09) -> 2.

COMBINED COUNTS observed: items 3-fail + minItems + maxItems + uniqueItems(unique) -> 5; items 3-fail + uniqueItems(dup) -> 4; items:{"type":"string"} + contains:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 4 (3 items + 1 contains); type:"array" + items:{"type":"string"} + minItems:5 on [1,2,3] -> 4; uniqueItems + contains + minItems:5 + maxItems:2 + items:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 6.

CRASH BEHAVIOR: every crash prints NOTHING on stdout, prints a Python traceback plus a `[PYI-NNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13' due to unhandled exception!` line on stderr, and exits with code 1. 40 of the 528 vectors crash.
gotchas: 2020-12 with array-form `items` does NOT ignore it and does NOT do tuple validation — it CRASHES (AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get', exit 1, empty stdout). But only if at least one element actually gets descended into: items:[...] on [], on a non-array instance, or fully covered by prefixItems yields True/0 with no crash.
2019-09 STILL supports tuple-form `items` + `additionalItems` (identical counts to draft7). Only 2020-12 dropped them. Do not lump 2019-09 with 2020-12 for items/additionalItems.
draft3 and draft4 CRASH on boolean `items` (true OR false) — 'bool' object is not iterable — even when the instance is the EMPTY array []. Only a non-array instance avoids the crash.
`additionalItems` CRASHES (object of type 'bool' has no len()) in draft6, draft7 and 2019-09 whenever `items` is a boolean. It is silently inert when items is absent or is an object/dict.

2020-12 `items:false` yields exactly ONE aggregate error (a 'too many items' style error), whereas draft6/7/2019-09 `items:false` yields ONE ERROR PER ELEMENT. Same for additionalItems:false (1 aggregate) vs additionalItems:{schema} (1 per extra element).
`prefixItems` is ignored in 2019-09 (not just in draft7) — 2019-09 does not know it at all, so prefixItems + unevaluatedItems:false behaves completely differently between 2019-09 and 2020-12.
`unevaluatedItems` NEVER produces more than 1 top-level error, even when 10 items each fail 2 keywords of its subschema. Do not descend-and-yield per item.
`unevaluatedItems` DOES apply its subschema (unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer"} on [1,2,3] is VALID). It is not a bare 'nothing unevaluated allowed' check.
`items` marks all indexes evaluated for unevaluatedItems purposes EVEN WHEN items itself fails — so items:{"type":"string"} + unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] gives 3, not 4.
`contains` marks only the MATCHING indexes as evaluated; non-matching indexes remain unevaluated and are then checked by unevaluatedItems.
`not` does not contribute evaluated indexes; allOf/anyOf/oneOf/if/then/else/$ref do. unevaluatedItems inside an allOf branch cannot see the parent schema's sibling prefixItems/items.

minContains:0 is a real draft-version fork: with contains and 0 matches it is VALID in 2019-09/2020-12 but INVALID (1 error) in draft6/draft7 where minContains is unknown and plain contains still requires >=1 match.
The whole contains/minContains/maxContains group emits AT MOST 1 top-level error, never 2, even when you construct minContains:5 + maxContains:1.
minItems and maxItems DO both fire (2 errors) when both are violated — unlike the contains group.

uniqueItems equality treats booleans as distinct from numbers at every nesting depth ([1,true] unique, [{"a":false},{"a":0}] unique) while treating 1 and 1.0 (and 100 vs 1e2, 0 vs -0) as equal. Object key order is irrelevant.
uniqueItems is truthiness-tested, not boolean-tested: uniqueItems:1 and uniqueItems:"yes" enforce uniqueness; uniqueItems:0 does not.
`contains` is completely ignored in draft3 and draft4 (0 errors even for contains:false).

Non-numeric minItems/maxItems ("3", null) and non-schema contains/minContains/items/prefixItems/unevaluatedItems values raise Python TypeError/AttributeError and exit 1 with empty stdout — no validation error, a hard crash.
prefixItems:{} (empty object) accidentally passes as a no-op in 2020-12, while prefixItems:{"a":{...}}, prefixItems:true and prefixItems:"xyz" crash.
Tuple-form items longer than the instance array only validates min(len(items), len(instance)) positions and never errors for the missing positions.

result.findings:
GENERATOR: /workspace/probes/gen_refs.js (node, execFileSync, real captured stdout+exit). Stats helper /workspace/probes/stats.js. 481 vectors, 0 duplicates; 313 exit 0, 168 exit 1. On crash stdout is EMPTY (all 3 lines are lost — the print happens after iter_errors), exit code 1, traceback on stderr, plus a PyInstaller line "[PYI-NNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13' due to unhandled exception!".

=== 1. BASIC POINTER REFS ===
"#/definitions/x" and "#/$defs/x" both resolve as PLAIN JSON POINTERS in EVERY draft (3,4,6,7,2019-09,2020-12). The pointer walk is purely structural; it does not care whether the containing keyword is a known keyword for that draft. So `{"$schema":draft-07,"$ref":"#/$defs/a","$defs":{"a":{"type":"integer"}}}` works, and `{"$schema":draft-03,"$ref":"#/$defs/a",...}` works. A failing ref target contributes exactly the errors the target schema itself produces, as TOP-LEVEL errors (no wrapping): `$ref -> {"minLength":10,"pattern":"^z"}` on "x" = 2 errors in all drafts. Chained refs (a->b->c) do not add errors. Two properties both ref-ing the same failing def = 2 errors. `allOf:[{$ref:->3 failures}]` = 3 top-level errors (allOf descends). `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`not` wrapping a ref = 1 top-level error (sub-errors go to .context).

=== 2. $ref SIBLING KEYWORDS (the headline cross-draft difference) ===
draft-03/04/06/07: when "$ref" is present in a schema object, ALL other keywords in that object are IGNORED. `{"$ref":"#/definitions/a","minLength":10,"definitions":{"a":{"type":"string"}}}` on "x" => True / 0 errors in draft3,4,6,7. `{"$ref":"#/$defs/a","type":"integer","$defs":{"a":{"type":"string"}}}` on "x" => True/0 in draft3-7.
2019-09 and 2020-12: siblings ARE applied and each contributes its own top-level error. Same first schema => False / 1. `{"$ref":"#/$defs/a"(type:integer),"minLength":10,"pattern":"^z"}` on "x" => draft3/4/6/7: False/1 (only the $ref error); 2019-09 & 2020-12: False/3. Adding "maxLength":0 => 1 vs 4. `{"anyOf":[{"type":"integer"}],"$ref":"#/anyOf/0"}` on "x" => 1 error in draft3-7, 2 errors in 2019-09/2020-12 (anyOf runs too). This suppression is total, not just for validation keywords — see §5.

=== 3. ROOT/SELF RECURSION ===
`{"$ref":"#"}` at the TOP LEVEL is an infinite loop => RecursionError, exit 1, in EVERY draft. Same for `{"$ref":""}` (empty ref = whole document) in every draft. Same for `{"$id":"http://x/root","allOf":[{"$ref":"http://x/root"}],"type":"integer"}` in draft6/7/2019/2020 (draft-03 gives False/1 there because draft3 has no allOf). Same for `{"$anchor":"root","type":"integer","allOf":[{"$ref":"#root"}]}` in 2020-12. Recursion that is guarded by instance structure is fine: `{"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"$ref":"#"}}}` terminates and yields 1 error per failing level that bubbles to top level ({"a":{"a":1}} => 1 error, {"a":{"a":{"a":1}}} => 1 error). Mutually recursive $defs a<->b under allOf also RecursionError. Self-ref by absolute $id + pointer (`$id:"http://x/root"`, `$ref:"http://x/root#/$defs/a"`) works in draft6+; draft-04 fails (uses "id") ; draft-03 returns True/0 because allOf is unknown to draft3.

=== 4. JSON-POINTER ESCAPING / PERCENT-DECODING ===
The fragment is percent-DECODED before pointer escaping is undone. All of these resolve: `#/$defs/a~1b` -> key "a/b"; `#/$defs/a~0b` -> key "a~b"; `#/$defs/tilde~01` -> key "tilde~1"; `#/$defs/a%20b` -> key "a b"; a LITERAL space also works: `#/$defs/a b` -> key "a b"; `#/$defs/a%25b` -> key "a%b"; `#/$defs/a%2525b` -> key "a%25b"; `#/$defs/a%23b` -> key "a#b"; `#/$defs/a"b` -> key 'a"b'; `#/$defs/` -> key ""; `#/$defs/a+b` -> key "a+b" (NO plus-to-space decoding). An INVALID percent escape is left literal: `#/$defs/a%b` -> key "a%b" (does not raise). Order matters: percent-decode FIRST, then ~1/~0 unescape (so `%7E1` would become `~1` -> "/" — untested but implied).

=== 5. $id / id BASE URI (many surprises) ===
Which keyword names the identifier is per-draft: draft-03 and draft-04 use "id"; draft-06/07/2019-09/2020-12 use "$id". The wrong one is completely inert (e.g. `id` in draft-07 => Unresolvable; `$id` in draft-04 => Unresolvable).
BIG GOTCHA (draft 3/4/6/7 only): the identifier of a schema object is IGNORED WHEN "$ref" IS A SIBLING. So for `{"$schema":draft-07,"$id":"http://x/","$defs":{"a":{"$id":"b",...}},"$ref":"http://x/b"}` the ROOT $id is dropped (because root has $ref), the base stays "", the subresource registers under just "b", and `$ref:"http://x/b"` is Unresolvable(exit 1) while `$ref:"b"` RESOLVES. Move the $ref off the root (e.g. into properties/p) and the root $id is honored again: then BOTH "b" and "http://x/b" resolve under draft-06/07. Under 2019-09/2020-12 the root $id is ALWAYS honored, even with a sibling $ref, so both forms resolve there. Same asymmetry with draft-03/04 + "id".
WHICH SUBSCHEMAS GET CRAWLED FOR ids/anchors is draft-dependent: draft-03/04/06/07 crawl "definitions" but NOT "$defs"; 2019-09/2020-12 crawl BOTH "$defs" and "definitions". Hence `{"$schema":draft-07,"$defs":{"a":{"$id":"http://y/b",...}},"$ref":"http://y/b"}` => Unresolvable, while the same with "definitions" => resolves; both resolve under 2019-09/2020-12. ids inside applicator positions (properties/p) ARE crawled in draft-06+ (`{"properties":{"p":{"$id":"http://y/b","type":"integer"}},"allOf":[{"$ref":"http://y/b"}]}` => 2 errors in draft6/7/2019/2020; draft-03 => 1 error since allOf unknown; draft-04 => exit 1 since $id unknown).
Relative-reference resolution is normal RFC3986: `$id:"http://x/a/c.json"` + subresource `$id:"e.json"` registers http://x/a/e.json (so `$ref:"e.json"` and `$ref:"http://x/a/e.json"` work, `$ref:"http://x/e.json"` does not); subresource `$id:"/e.json"` registers http://x/e.json. Nested $id creates a new base for inner pointers: `$id:"http://y/"` subresource with `$ref:"#/$defs/b"` inside resolves within that subresource, and `http://y/#/$defs/b` works from outside. `$id:""` and `$id:"http://x/#"` are accepted with no ill effect.

=== 6. ANCHORS / PLAIN-NAME FRAGMENTS ===
Anchor keyword per draft: draft-03/04 => `"id":"#foo"`; draft-06/07 => `"$id":"#foo"`; 2019-09/2020-12 => `"$anchor":"foo"` (a `$id:"#foo"` in 2019-09/2020-12 is NOT an anchor => NoSuchAnchor). Using the wrong flavor raises `NoSuchAnchor: 'foo' does not exist within {...whole root schema repr...}`, exit 1. Anchors are scoped to their containing resource: `{"$defs":{"a":{"$id":"b","$anchor":"c",...}},"allOf":[{"$ref":"#c"}]}` => NoSuchAnchor (anchor lives in resource "b"), while `$ref:"b#c"` resolves. `http://x/#foo` with root `$id:"http://x/"` resolves. Anchor discovery obeys the same crawl rules as §5 (draft-07 does not crawl `$defs`, so `$defs`-nested `$id:"#foo"` is NoSuchAnchor in draft-07).

=== 7. $recursiveRef / $recursiveAnchor / $dynamicRef / $dynamicAnchor ===
`$recursiveRef`/`$recursiveAnchor` are keywords ONLY in 2019-09. In draft-07 and in 2020-12 they are unknown/ignored: `{"$recursiveAnchor":true,"type":"object","properties":{"p":{"$recursiveRef":"#"}}}` on {"p":1} => draft-07 True/0, 2020-12 True/0, 2019-09 False/1. A bare `{"$recursiveRef":"#"}` at root in 2019-09 => RecursionError exit 1; in draft-07/2020-12 => True/0. `$recursiveAnchor:false` behaves the same as true for the simple root case tested (2019-09, {"p":1} => False/1).
`$dynamicRef`/`$dynamicAnchor` are keywords ONLY in 2020-12; ignored in draft-07 and 2019-09. `{"$dynamicAnchor":"n","type":"object","properties":{"p":{"$dynamicRef":"#n"}}}` on {"p":1} => draft-07 True/0, 2019-09 True/0, 2020-12 False/1. Bare `{"$dynamicRef":"#nope"}` => 2020-12 NoSuchAnchor exit 1; draft-07/2019-09 True/0. In 2020-12 a `$dynamicAnchor` ALSO registers as a plain anchor (`$ref:"#n"` finds a `$dynamicAnchor:"n"`), and a `$dynamicRef` will happily bind to a plain `$anchor` too (both give False/1 in the tested cases).

=== 8. META-SCHEMA REFS ARE FULLY OFFLINE ===
All official meta-schemas are bundled; no network is attempted (an unresolvable http ref fails in ~0.37 s). `$ref` to any of draft-03/04/06/07 schema#, 2019-09 schema, 2020-12 schema, 2020-12 meta/core, 2020-12 meta/validation, 2019-09 meta/validation all RESOLVE. Trailing "#" optional ("http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema" works). The UNVERSIONED "http://json-schema.org/schema#" is Unresolvable (exit 1). Error counts against meta-schemas: instance "x" vs draft-03/04/06/07 meta => 1 error each; vs 2019-09 meta => 7; vs 2020-12 meta => 8 (each of the 7 allOf `$ref`s to meta/* yields one top-level error, plus the type error). Instance {"type":"string"} vs draft-07 meta => True/0; {"type":"bogus"} => 1; {"type":"bogus","minLength":"x"} => 2. Instance {} vs 2020-12 meta => True/0. Pointers into meta-schemas work where the target exists: `draft-07/schema#/definitions/nonNegativeInteger` (-5 => 1 error, 5 => 0), `draft-07/schema#/properties/type`, `2020-12/meta/validation#/$defs/nonNegativeInteger`. But `2020-12/schema#/$defs/nonNegativeInteger` is PointerToNowhere (2020-12 top meta-schema has no $defs of that name) and the exception message dumps the whole meta-schema dict.

=== 9. FAILURE MODES (all exit 1, empty stdout) ===
- Missing JSON pointer: `jsonschema.exceptions._WrappedReferencingError: PointerToNowhere: '/nope' does not exist within {<repr of the resource the pointer was resolved against>}` — same in all 6 drafts.
- Unknown/absolute URI: `_WrappedReferencingError: Unresolvable: <uri>` — for http://example.com/x, https://example.com/x#/foo, urn:uuid:..., file:///etc/passwd, "nope", "other.json", and any $id-relative miss. No network I/O.
- Missing anchor: `_WrappedReferencingError: NoSuchAnchor: 'foo' does not exist within {<root schema repr>}`.
- Infinite ref loops: `RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded` (23 vectors).
- $ref value not a string: `AttributeError: 'int'/'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'`; `$ref:true` -> 'bool'; `$ref:[]` -> 'list'; `$ref:{}` -> 'dict'. Raised before any resolution.
- Pointer that traverses a LIST at a position the draft considers a schema slot: `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'` (raised in referencing/jsonschema.py `_dollar_id` while computing the sub-resource id). This is the ONE case that is draft-sensitive in a nasty way: `{"items":[{...}],"$ref":"#/items/0"}` CRASHES in 2020-12 (items is a single-schema slot there, so the array itself is fed to id()) but WORKS in draft-03/04/06/07 and 2019-09 (items is an array-of-schemas slot). `{"prefixItems":[{...}],"$ref":"#/prefixItems/0"}` works in 2020-12. `{"$defs":{"a":[{...}]},"$ref":"#/$defs/a/0"}` CRASHES in 2019-09/2020-12 ($defs is a schema-map slot there) but WORKS in draft-03/04/06/07 ($defs unknown, no id() call). `#/anyOf/0` never crashes (anyOf is an array-of-schemas slot everywhere it exists). Merely HAVING a list in a schema slot is harmless — the crash only happens when the $ref pointer walks through it (`{"$defs":{"a":[{...}]},"type":"integer"}` is fine).
- Ref target resolves to a non-schema value: a plain string or list target gives `AttributeError: 'str'/'list' object has no attribute 'items'` (raised by iter_errors); a number or null target gives `TypeError: argument of type 'int'/'NoneType' is not iterable` (raised by the `"$ref" in schema` membership test). e.g. `{"$ref":"#/title","title":"t"}`, `{"$ref":"#/enum","enum":[1,2]}`, `{"enum":[1,2],"$ref":"#/enum/0"}`, `{"definitions":{"a":"nonschema"},"$ref":"#/definitions/a"}`.
- Boolean ref targets: `{"definitions":{"a":false},"$ref":"#/definitions/a"}` => draft-06/07/2019/2020 give False/1 and `true` gives True/0, but draft-03 and draft-04 CRASH with `TypeError: argument of type 'bool' is not iterable` (those drafts have no boolean-schema support).
- Object-but-not-schema target is fine: `{"definitions":{"a":{"type":"integer"}},"$ref":"#/definitions"}` resolves to {"a":{...}} which has only unknown keywords => True/0.

=== 10. REFS IN APPLICATOR POSITIONS (counting) ===
Refs under properties, items, additionalProperties, patternProperties, propertyNames, dependentSchemas, allOf all bubble their target's errors to top level one-for-one. `if`/`then` with a ref that the instance fails only in `if` => True/0 (if-failure is not an error). Counts observed: 2 properties each failing = 2; array items with 2 bad elements = 2; allOf with a 3-failure target = 3.
gotchas: draft-03/04/06/07: ANY sibling of $ref is ignored — including validation keywords AND $id/id. 2019-09/2020-12: siblings are applied and each yields its own separate top-level error (so {"$ref":X,"minLength":10,"pattern":"^z"} on a bad string = 1 error in draft7 but 3 in 2020-12).

Because $id is suppressed by a sibling $ref in draft 3/4/6/7, a ROOT schema of the form {"$id":"http://x/","$ref":...} loses its base URI entirely: $ref "http://x/b" becomes Unresolvable while the relative $ref "b" resolves. The same schema with the $ref moved one level down (into properties) resolves both. 2019-09/2020-12 do not have this quirk.
Identifier keyword is per-draft: draft-03/04 use "id", draft-06+ use "$id". The other spelling is completely inert (no error, just Unresolvable later).
Anchor spelling is per-draft: draft-03/04 = id:"#foo", draft-06/07 = $id:"#foo", 2019-09/2020-12 = $anchor:"foo". $id:"#foo" in 2019-09/2020-12 is NOT an anchor and yields NoSuchAnchor.

$id/$anchor discovery only crawls keywords the draft knows: draft-03/04/06/07 crawl "definitions" but NOT "$defs"; 2019-09/2020-12 crawl both. Plain JSON-pointer refs like "#/$defs/a" still work in every draft though — pointer resolution is purely structural and draft-agnostic.

A JSON pointer that walks into an ARRAY sitting in a slot the draft treats as a single schema crashes with AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'. #/items/0 works in draft3-7 and 2019-09 but CRASHES in 2020-12; #/$defs/a/0 works in draft3-7 but CRASHES in 2019-09/2020-12; #/prefixItems/0 and #/anyOf/0 always work.

Every resolution failure is a hard crash (exit 1, empty stdout, traceback), never a validation error: PointerToNowhere, Unresolvable, NoSuchAnchor (all wrapped as jsonschema.exceptions._WrappedReferencingError), plus RecursionError for loops.
{"$ref":"#"} or {"$ref":""} at the ROOT is an unguarded infinite loop => RecursionError in every draft; the same $ref nested under properties terminates because the instance bottoms out.

No network is ever attempted. All official meta-schemas (draft-03/04/06/07, 2019-09, 2020-12, and the 2019-09/2020-12 meta/* vocabularies) are bundled and $ref-able offline. But the unversioned "http://json-schema.org/schema#" is Unresolvable.

Error counts against meta-schemas are large and specific: instance "x" vs 2019-09 meta = 7 top-level errors, vs 2020-12 meta = 8, vs draft-03/04/06/07 meta = 1 each (the 2019/2020 metas are allOf-of-vocabularies, and each allOf branch yields one top-level error).

$recursiveRef/$recursiveAnchor exist ONLY in 2019-09; $dynamicRef/$dynamicAnchor exist ONLY in 2020-12. In the other drafts they are unknown keywords and are silently ignored (True/0), so the same schema can flip result across 2019-09 and 2020-12.
In 2020-12 a $dynamicAnchor also registers as a plain anchor ($ref "#n" finds it) and $dynamicRef will bind to a plain $anchor.

Ref targets that are not objects/booleans crash with two different exception types: str/list target => AttributeError ... has no attribute 'items'; int/null target => TypeError: argument of type 'X' is not iterable.
Boolean ref targets work in draft-06+ (false => 1 error, true => 0) but crash draft-03/draft-04 with TypeError: argument of type 'bool' is not iterable.
Fragments are percent-decoded BEFORE ~1/~0 unescaping; invalid escapes like %b are left literal; '+' is NOT decoded to a space; a literal space in the pointer works unencoded.
