=== DRAFT-3 `required` (boolean) EXACT SEMANTICS ===
Only honored when the subschema sits as a VALUE OF `properties` and the key is ABSENT from the object instance. It is a plain PYTHON TRUTHINESS test on the value, not `is True`: true->required, 1->required, "yes"->required, ["x"]->required; false/0/null/{}/""/[] -> not required. `required` at the top level of a schema, or inside `patternProperties`, `additionalProperties`, `items`, or `dependencies` subschemas, is a no-op (only the `properties` validator reads it). It is skipped entirely when the instance is not an object. Each missing required property yields ONE separate top-level error ({} with 3 required props -> 3 errors). It composes additively with the same property's other keywords when the key IS present.

=== DRAFT-3 `dependencies` ===
Dispatch: str -> single required name; dict/Mapping -> descend as a schema; ANYTHING ELSE -> iterate it as a collection of required names. So true/false/5 -> TypeError "'bool'/'int' object is not iterable" (CRASH). Array form yields ONE error PER MISSING name ({"a":1} + {a:["b","c","d"]} -> 3 errors); empty array -> 0. Schema form descends and each sub-error bubbles to TOP LEVEL ({"a":1} + a:{properties:{b:{required:true},c:{required:true}}} -> 2 errors). Multiple triggering keys each contribute independently. Skipped when instance is not an object. NOTE draft4 dispatch DIFFERS: list/tuple -> required names; everything else (incl. bool AND str) -> descend as schema, so a string value CRASHES in d4/d6/d7 but a boolean value is fine (treated as boolean schema, 0 errors).

=== DRAFT-3 `disallow` ===
Accepts a string or an ARRAY; each entry may be a type name OR an inline schema. Internally reuses the draft3 `type` checker, so "any" matches everything and an unknown type name raises UnknownType. Yields ONE error PER MATCHING entry: disallow ["integer","number"] on 1 -> 2 errors; ["integer","object","any"] on {} -> 2 errors; ["integer","boolean","null","array","object"] on "s" -> 0. Inline-schema entries yield at most 1 error each no matter how many sub-errors the inline schema would have produced. A bare OBJECT (non-array, non-string) disallow value CRASHES: it iterates the dict's KEYS as type names -> UnknownType 'type'.

=== DRAFT-3 `extends` ===
Value may be a single schema object or an ARRAY of schema objects. All sub-errors are yielded as SEPARATE TOP-LEVEL errors (no context nesting): extends:[{type:"string"},{type:"boolean"},{type:"array"}] on 1 -> 3 errors; extends:{properties:{a:{type:"string"},b:{type:"string"}}} on {"a":1,"b":2} -> 2 errors. Empty array -> 0. Composes additively with the parent schema's own keywords ({type:"string",extends:{type:"boolean"}} on 1 -> 2 errors). Nested `extends` inside `extends` works. `extends:true`/`extends:false` CRASHES (TypeError 'bool' object is not iterable) — booleans are NOT accepted here even though they are accepted as `properties` values. `extends:[1]` also crashes.

=== DRAFT-3 `divisibleBy` (and draft4 `multipleOf`) — SAME UNDERLYING FUNCTION ===
Traceback shows divisibleBy routes to `_keywords.py multipleOf`. Skipped when instance is not a number (strings, bools -> 0 errors; bool is not a number). divisor 0 -> ZeroDivisionError CRASH; string divisor -> TypeError CRASH. Float divisor path uses the QUOTIENT test (`int(instance/dB) != instance/dB`), so 0.0075 divisibleBy 0.0001 PASSES and 0.3 divisibleBy 0.1 FAILS. On float-division OVERFLOW the code falls back to an EXACT RATIONAL test: 1e308 divisibleBy 0.5 / 0.25 / 0.0625 -> PASS (dyadic divisors), while 1e308 divisibleBy 0.1 / 0.123 / 0.3 / 1e-10 -> FAIL. Integer divisor path uses plain modulo (1.5 divisibleBy 1 -> fail; 6 divisibleBy -1.5 -> pass). CAUTION: JSON `1.0` is a float in Python but many JSON serializers emit `1` — `divisibleBy:1.0` (float) and `divisibleBy:1` (int) took the two different code paths but agreed here.

=== DRAFT-3 `type` with inline schemas ===
`type` may mix type-name strings and inline schema objects: {type:["string",{type:"integer"}]} on 1 -> 0 errors; on a failing value -> exactly 1 error regardless of how many sub-errors the inline schema produced ({type:[{properties:{a:{type:"string"}}}]} on {"a":1} -> 1 error). Empty `type:[]` -> 1 error. Duplicates collapse to 1 error. `type:["any"]` passes anything. `type:[true]` CRASHES (UnknownType). Unknown type name (e.g. "zzz") CRASHES with jsonschema.exceptions.UnknownType in BOTH d3 and d4.

=== ERROR-COUNTING RULES (identical shape in d3/d4) ===
Descending keywords yield each sub-error as its own TOP-LEVEL error: properties, patternProperties, additionalProperties(schema form), items(both forms), additionalItems(schema form), dependencies(schema+array forms), draft3 extends, draft3 disallow(one per matching entry), draft4 allOf. Nesting is transparent — {"a":[{"b":1},{"b":2}]} through properties->items->properties -> 2 top-level errors; 3-level nesting with 1 leaf failure -> 1. Non-descending / single-error keywords: type (1 even for array form / inline schemas), enum, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, pattern, minItems, maxItems, uniqueItems, minProperties, maxProperties, additionalProperties:FALSE (ONE error listing all unexpected keys, even for 3 extras), additionalItems:FALSE (ONE error), draft4 anyOf/oneOf/not (always exactly 1, sub-errors live in .context; oneOf matching 2 or 3 branches -> 1; empty anyOf/oneOf -> 1; empty allOf -> 0). `required` (draft4 array form) yields one error per missing name, duplicates counted twice (["a","a"] -> 2). Sibling keywords at the same level are fully additive: {type:"string",enum:["a"],minimum:5,divisibleBy:7,disallow:"integer"} on 1 -> 5 errors.

=== OTHER CONFIRMED DETAILS ===
- Equality is TYPE-AWARE: enum [true] vs instance 1 -> error; enum [0] vs false -> error; enum [1.0] vs 1 -> OK; uniqueItems on [1,true] and [0,false] -> unique; on [1,1.0] -> NOT unique; on [{"a":1,"b":2},{"b":2,"a":1}] -> NOT unique.
- enum with a non-list value (e.g. "abc") does NOT crash; it iterates the string's characters.
- Boolean schemas: `properties:{a:true}` / `{a:false}` WORK in d3 and d4 (false -> 1 error). But `items:true` / `items:false` CRASH in d3 and d4 (TypeError 'bool' object is not iterable — the legacy items validator only distinguishes "object" vs iterable). `extends:true/false` crashes; `dependencies:{a:true}` crashes in d3 but is fine in d4.
- Regex is Python `re` and UNANCHORED (re.search): pattern "abc" matches "xabcx". Invalid regex in `pattern` or a `patternProperties` key -> re.error CRASH.
- Numeric keywords skip non-numbers and booleans silently (minimum:5 on "z" or on true -> 0 errors). String keywords skip non-strings (maxLength on 12345 or on an array -> 0). minItems/uniqueItems skip non-arrays; minProperties skips non-objects.
- Base URI: `id` in d3/d4 registers subschema resources — {id:"http://ex.com/r.json", definitions:{X:{id:"other.json"}}, $ref:"other.json"} RESOLVES; {id:"http://ex.com/a/", definitions:{X:{id:"b/c.json"}}, $ref:"b/c.json"} resolves. Anchor form {id:"#foo"} + $ref "#foo" resolves in d3/d4; the same with `$id` raises NoSuchAnchor. BUT the ROOT's own absolute URI is NOT self-resolvable: {id:"http://ex.com/r.json", $ref:"http://ex.com/r.json#/definitions/X"} raises Unresolvable in every draft (same for $id in d6+).
- Unresolvable "#/nope" pointer -> jsonschema.exceptions._WrappedReferencingError: PointerToNowhere, exit 1.
- Unknown keywords (fooBar, maxDecimal) are silently ignored.

=== CRASH BEHAVIOR ===
All failures print a Python traceback to STDERR, produce EMPTY STDOUT, and exit with code 1 (PyInstaller adds a final "[PYI-NNNNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13'..." line). Exception types observed: ZeroDivisionError (divisibleBy/multipleOf 0), TypeError 'bool'/'int' object is not iterable (d3 dependencies non-str/non-dict, d3/d4 items bool, d3 extends bool, d4 required non-array on an OBJECT instance), TypeError argument 'key': unhashable type: 'dict' (d4+ type array with inline schema), TypeError unorderable/unsupported for str minimum or str divisibleBy, AttributeError 'str' object has no attribute 'get' (d4/d6/d7 string dependency), jsonschema.exceptions.UnknownType (unknown type name, d3 disallow given a dict, d4 type "any", d3 type [true]), jsonschema.exceptions._WrappedReferencingError (PointerToNowhere / NoSuchAnchor / Unresolvable), and re.error for bad regexes. Note d4 `required:true` only crashes when the instance IS an object; against a non-object instance the validator returns early with 0 errors.

WORKSPACE NOTE: /workspace/probes is shared and a parallel agent and I clobbered each other's generic filenames (run.js / p1.json). /workspace/probes/error-counting-deep.jsonl currently contains 504 useless `{"out":"","exit":1}` lines (252 mine, 252 theirs) and should be regenerated by whoever owns it. My own generators are isolated in /workspace/probes/_d3work/ and my deliverable file is clean and verified.
gotchas: Draft3 IGNORES allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not entirely — a schema {"$schema":draft-03,"anyOf":[{"type":"string"}]} validates ANY instance as True/0.
Draft3 IGNORES minProperties/maxProperties, required-as-array, const, contains, propertyNames, if/then/else, multipleOf, dependentRequired, prefixItems, unevaluatedProperties.
Draft4 IGNORES divisibleBy, disallow, extends, const, contains, propertyNames, if/then/else, dependentRequired, and numeric exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum.

Draft3 boolean `required` is a PYTHON TRUTHINESS test, not `=== true`: 1 and "yes" and ["x"] make the property required; 0, null, "", {}, [] do not. Same truthiness rule applies to draft3/draft4 boolean exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum ("yes" enables exclusivity, 0 disables).

Draft3 boolean `required` is ONLY read by the `properties` validator. Top-level `required:true`, or `required:true` inside patternProperties/additionalProperties/items/dependencies subschemas, is a silent no-op.

In draft3 AND draft4, type "integer" does NOT match 1.0 (a JSON float). It only matches Python ints. From draft6 onward 1.0 IS an integer. This is the single most-missed d3/d4 difference for a JS reimplementation, where 1.0 and 1 are the same value — you must track whether the JSON text had a fractional part/exponent.

`dependencies` dispatch differs between draft3 and draft4: draft3 is (str -> single required | dict -> schema | else -> ITERATE as required names), draft4 is (list/tuple -> required names | everything else -> SCHEMA). Consequence: a string dependency works in d3 but throws AttributeError in d4/d6/d7; a boolean dependency throws TypeError in d3 but is a valid boolean schema in d4.
Draft 2019-09 and 2020-12 dropped `dependencies` completely — it is silently ignored there, so {"dependencies":{"a":["b"]}} is True/0 under 2019-09/2020-12 but False under d3-d7.

Boolean subschemas are accepted as `properties` values in d3/d4 but CRASH as `items` values (TypeError 'bool' object is not iterable), as `extends` values, and (d3 only) as `dependencies` values. Do not assume 'booleans are schemas everywhere'.
`disallow` yields ONE ERROR PER MATCHING ENTRY, not one error total: disallow:["integer","number"] on 1 gives 2 top-level errors. And "any" matches everything.
`extends` sub-errors bubble up as SEPARATE TOP-LEVEL errors (like allOf), whereas `disallow` inline-schema entries and `type` inline-schema entries collapse to exactly ONE error each.
An unknown type name (e.g. type:"zzz") or type:"any" in draft4 raises UnknownType and exits 1 — it does not simply fail validation. type:"any" is valid ONLY in draft3.
type arrays containing inline schema objects are draft3-only; in d4+ they crash with 'unhashable type: dict'.
additionalProperties:false and additionalItems:false each emit exactly ONE error no matter how many extra properties/items there are — do not emit one per extra.
anyOf/oneOf/not always emit exactly 1 top-level error (children go into .context), but allOf and extends emit N.
Draft3/Draft4 use `id` (not `$id`) for base URI and `#anchor`. A `$id` anchor in d3/d4 causes NoSuchAnchor and a crash. Conversely `id` is ignored from draft6 on.
The ROOT schema's own id/$id URI is not self-resolvable: $ref to the root's absolute URI raises Unresolvable, even though $ref to a nested subschema's id does resolve.
$ref suppresses ALL sibling keywords in d3/d4/d6/d7 (including extends, properties, allOf) but siblings ARE applied in 2019-09/2020-12 (that case gives 2 errors instead of 1).
`format` is never enforced (no format_checker is passed) in any draft, for any format name — always 0 errors.

divisibleBy/multipleOf: divisor 0 -> ZeroDivisionError crash; float divisors use the quotient test (so 0.0075 divisibleBy 0.0001 PASSES) and fall back to EXACT RATIONAL arithmetic on overflow (1e308 divisibleBy 0.5 passes, 1e308 divisibleBy 0.1 fails). Naive JS `x % d === 0` gets several of these wrong.
Equality is type-aware: booleans are never equal to 0/1 for enum or uniqueItems, but 1 and 1.0 ARE equal. Object key order does not affect uniqueItems.
enum with a non-array value does not crash; it is iterated (a string is iterated by character).
$defs/definitions are inert containers, but JSON-pointer $refs into them resolve in every draft including draft3 — pointer resolution is purely structural.

The https:// spelling of the draft-03/draft-04 URIs is NOT recognized and falls back to Draft202012Validator with a stderr warning; the http:// spelling with or without the trailing '#' is recognized.
Every crash yields EMPTY stdout plus exit code 1 — a reimplementation must distinguish 'throws' from 'invalid'.

result.family: Top-level error counting (iter_errors length) across nesting depth, all drafts
result.findings:
FILE: /workspace/probes/error-counting-deep.jsonl — 709 vectors, all re-verified reproducible (random 1-in-17 resample: 0 mismatches). 661 exit-0, 48 exit-1 crashes. Invariant holds in every single vector: line2 == "True" IFF line3 == "0". Max observed count 20.

THE CORE RULE. Every keyword validator is a generator. `len(list(iter_errors(instance)))` = the sum over all keywords present in the ROOT schema (in schema dict order, order irrelevant to count) of the number of errors that keyword's generator yields. A keyword is either DESCENDING (it re-runs the whole validator on a child instance/subschema and re-yields every produced error unchanged, so counts multiply/sum recursively without bound) or COLLAPSING (it swallows all sub-errors into a single ValidationError whose .context holds them, contributing at most 1).

DESCENDING KEYWORDS (nested errors bubble up as separate top-level errors):
properties (sum over listed props present in instance), patternProperties (sum over every (pattern, matching prop) pair — a prop matching 2 patterns is validated twice and BOTH sets of errors count; no dedup), additionalProperties WHEN ITS VALUE IS AN OBJECT (sum over each additional prop), items in schema form (sum over every element), items in array/tuple form (drafts 3/4/6/7/2019 only — sum over zip(schemas, elements)), prefixItems (2020-12 only), additionalItems in schema form (drafts 3–2019; sum over each extra element beyond the tuple), propertyNames (sum over every property NAME validated as a string — 3 names x 2 failing keywords = 6), allOf (sum over all branches; it does NOT short-circuit), if/then and if/else (the chosen branch's errors are yielded raw — `then` failing 3 keywords => 3 top-level errors; the `if` subschema's own errors are always discarded and contribute 0), $ref / $dynamicRef (the target schema's errors are yielded raw), dependencies in SCHEMA form (drafts 3/4/6/7 only), dependentSchemas (2019/2020 only), extends (draft 3 only; object or array form, sum over all).

COLLAPSING KEYWORDS (exactly 0 or 1 error, no matter how deep or how many sub-failures):
anyOf (1), oneOf (1, whether 0 branches match or >1 match), not (1), contains (1 — never one-per-element; also 1 when the array is empty, 1 when minContains/maxContains are violated, and if contains + minContains + maxContains all conceptually fail it is still exactly 1 total), unevaluatedProperties (1 total whether false or a schema, whether 1 or 3 unevaluated props each failing 3 keywords), unevaluatedItems (1 total), additionalProperties WHEN false (1 total no matter how many extras: 3 or 5 extras => 1), additionalItems: false (1 total no matter how many extra elements), items: false IN 2020-12 ONLY (1 total — jsonschema special-cases `items is False` into one "Expected at most N items but found M extra" error), type (1, including list form), enum (1, including enum: []), const (1), format (ALWAYS 0 — no FormatChecker is attached), all scalar bounds (minimum/maximum/exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum/multipleOf/divisibleBy/minLength/maxLength/pattern/minItems/maxItems/uniqueItems/minProperties/maxProperties), disallow (draft 3, 1).

PER-ITEM COLLECTIONS (one error per missing key, not one per keyword):
required as an array yields exactly one error PER missing key (3 missing => 3; 12 missing => 12). dependencies in ARRAY form (d3–d7) yields one error per missing dependent key per trigger key ({a:[x,y],b:[z,w]} with a,b present => 4). dependentRequired (2019/2020) same. draft-3 `required: true` inside properties yields 1 error per missing property.

MEASURED EXAMPLES (2020-12 unless noted): N sibling failing keywords at root => exactly N (verified 1..8: {type,minLength,pattern,enum,maxLength,const} on "ab" => 6; 8 numeric siblings on 7 => 8). properties with N failing children each failing M keywords => N*M (3x3 => 9, 2x2 => 4). items schema with N elements each failing M => N*M (3x3 => 9, 10 items x 2 kw => 20). Nesting is fully multiplicative: 2 items x 2 props x 2 kw => 8; 3 items x 2 props x 2 kw => 12; items(2) x properties x allOf(3) => 6; items(3) x properties x allOf(3) => 9; items(2) x properties x if/then(allOf 3) => 6; items(2) x properties x $ref(2 kw) => 4. Depth is unbounded and does not collapse: 40-level nested properties => 1; 200-level nested allOf => 1; 3-level nested properties with a leaf failing 3 keywords => 3; 4-level => 3; failing 3 sibling keywords at each of 3 object levels plus a 3-failure leaf => 12. Collapsers absorb arbitrary depth: anyOf/oneOf/not/contains/unevaluatedProperties wrapping a subtree that would produce 6 errors each produce exactly 1; the same subtree under allOf/if-then/$ref/dependentSchemas produces 6.

COMBINATION ARITHMETIC (all additive at the same level): properties+patternProperties+additionalProperties:false on {a:1,ab:2,zz:3} => 4 (1 + 2 + 1); adding a second overlapping pattern => 5; patternProperties+additionalProperties(schema) => 3; items(3 fails)+contains(1)+minItems(1) => 5; propertyNames(2)+required(1)+additionalProperties:false(1) => 4; minProperties+maxProperties+required(2 missing)+additionalProperties:false+propertyNames(2)+type => 8; minItems+maxItems+uniqueItems+items(2)+contains+type => 7; 5 propertyNames failures + 5 additionalProperties failures => 10. A "monster" schema (root type + required + property with type + minItems + 2 items x (allOf 2 + if/then 1)) => 10, exactly the sum of parts.

=== 1. $schema -> validator class (validator_for) ===
Exactly six URIs are registered, and only these exact spellings (each also accepted with a single trailing '#'):

  http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema  -> Draft4Validator
  http://json-schema.org/draft-06/schema  -> Draft6Validator

Scheme is NOT interchangeable: 03/04/06/07 are registered under http:// ONLY; 2019-09/2020-12 under https:// ONLY. 'https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#' and 'http://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' are UNKNOWN. Absent $schema entirely -> Draft202012Validator with NO warning.

=== 2. URI normalization = urlsplit(uri).geturl(), then a functools-cached (hashed) dict lookup ===
- Scheme IS case-folded to lowercase, uniformly, for all six. CORRECTION TO EARLIER NOTES: 'HTTPS://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' resolves to Draft202012Validator with NO warning, and 'HtTpS://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema' -> Draft201909Validator with NO warning. Non-empty query ('?x=1') -> warn.

The key goes into a functools-cached normalize() that HASHES the argument first, then calls urlsplit, whose _coerce_args treats falsy non-str as ''.

=== 6. Top-level error counting (line 3) ===
is_valid and len(list(iter_errors)) are always consistent (False iff count>0). Rules:
- Sibling keywords each yield their own error: {"type":"string","minimum":5,"maxLength":2} on 1 -> 2. {"minimum":10,"maximum":1,"multipleOf":3} on 5 -> 3 (but only 2 in draft3, which has no multipleOf). {"minLength":3,"maxLength":1} -> 2; {"minItems":2,"maxItems":0} -> 2; {"minProperties":3,"maxProperties":1} -> 2 (0 in draft3, which lacks both).
- properties: one error per failing property at ANY depth (yielded via descend): 2 failing props -> 2, 3 -> 3, one failing grandchild -> 1, two failing grandchildren under one child -> 2, a 3-deep single failure -> 1.
- patternProperties: one per failing property; if two patterns both match one property and both fail -> 2.
- additionalProperties as a SCHEMA: one per failing extra property (2 extras failing -> 2). additionalProperties:false: exactly 1 error total no matter how many extras (2 extras -> 1).
- properties + patternProperties + additionalProperties:false all failing on one property -> 2 (properties error + patternProperties error; additionalProperties does not fire because the property is covered).
- propertyNames: one per bad key (2 bad keys -> 2). Ignored (0) in draft3/4.
- items (schema form): one per failing element; nested items ({"items":{"items":{"type":"string"}}} on [[1,2],[3]]) -> 3.
- prefixItems + items: 2 failing -> 2.
- allOf: sub-errors surface individually — {"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"boolean"}]} on 1 -> 2; nested allOf-in-allOf -> 3; an anyOf inside an allOf collapses to 1 for that branch -> allOf[anyOf-fail, type-fail] -> 2. NOTE draft3 has NO allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not, so all of these are True/0 under draft-03.
- anyOf / oneOf / not / if-then / $ref: exactly 1 top-level error each (children live in .context).
- uniqueItems: exactly 1 error regardless of how many duplicate pairs ([1,1,2,2] -> 1).
- contains/minContains/maxContains: 1 error each.
- type as a list: 1 error.
- Combined {"$schema":X,"properties":{a:string,b:string},"type":"array"} on {"a":1,"b":2} -> 3 in every draft, including under an unknown $schema.

=== 8. Types, equality and numbers (the biggest JS-reimplementation traps) ===
- Booleans are NOT numbers here: {"type":"integer"} on true -> False/1 in all six drafts; {"type":"number"} on true -> False/1; {"type":"boolean"} on 1 -> False/1. (jsonschema explicitly excludes bool from the int/number type checks even though Python bool subclasses int.)
- Numeric equality for const/enum is by VALUE across int/float: const 1 accepts instance 1.0 and const 1.0 accepts instance 1 (True/0 in all drafts). enum [1] accepts 1.0.
- -0 equals 0: const 0 accepts -0.0 and const -0.0 accepts 0; enum [0] accepts -0.0. multipleOf 2 on -0.0 -> True/0.
- But bool vs number is NOT equal for const/enum: const 1 on true -> d6+ False/1 (d3/4 True/0 because const is unknown there); const true on 1 -> d6+ False/1; enum [true] on 1 -> False/1; enum [1] on true -> False/1.
- uniqueItems uses the same value equality: [1,1.0] -> DUPLICATE (False/1); [[1,2],[1,2]] -> duplicate; [{"a":1,"b":2},{"b":2,"a":1}] -> duplicate (object key ORDER is irrelevant). But [true,1] -> unique (True/0) and [0,false] -> unique. [1,2,3] -> True/0. [NaN,NaN] -> duplicate (False/1).
- Big integers keep full Python precision: instance 10000000000000000001 with const 10000000000000000001 -> True/0, with const 10000000000000000000 -> False/1 (a JS Number would collapse both to the same double), and {"type":"integer"} accepts it.
- json.loads accepts NaN, Infinity, -Infinity: NaN passes {"type":"number"} (True/0); NaN fails {"const":null} and {"enum":[1]}; Infinity fails {"multipleOf":2} (False/1). 1e400 parses to inf, passes {"type":"number"}, and fails {"maximum":1e308}.
- multipleOf uses Python float division semantics: 4.5 % 1.5 -> True/0; 7.5 with multipleOf 0.1 -> True/0; 0.0075 with multipleOf 0.0001 -> True/0; 1 with multipleOf 0.0001 -> True/0; 1e308 with multipleOf 0.1 -> False/1 (d4+; d3 ignores multipleOf).

=== 9. Strings: length is CODE POINTS, regex is Python `re` ===
- maxLength/minLength count Unicode CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 units. "😀" (one astral emoji) has length 1: {"maxLength":1} -> True/0, {"minLength":2} -> False/1. Two emoji with {"maxLength":2} -> True/0. A JS `.length` implementation would get all three wrong. Combining sequences are NOT normalized: "é" has length 2 ({"maxLength":1} -> False/1) while precomposed "é" has length 1 (True/0). "�" is a normal 1-char string.
- pattern uses Python re.search (UNANCHORED): pattern "b" matches "abc" -> True/0.
- Python `\d`/`\w` are UNICODE-aware by default: pattern "^\\d$" matches "٣" (Arabic-Indic three) -> True/0, while "a" -> False/1. pattern "^\\w$" matches both "_" and "é". JS /\d/ and /\w/ are ASCII-only — this WILL diverge.
- Python `$` matches before a trailing newline: pattern "^a$" on "a\n" -> True/0 (JS would say no match). "^a\\Z" on "a\n" -> False/1. "^a$" on "a\nb" and on "b\na" -> False/1 (no re.MULTILINE).
- Python-only regex syntax is accepted: inline flags "(?i)a" matches "A" -> True/0; named group "(?P<n>x)" works. JS-only syntax is rejected: "(?<n>x)" -> UNCAUGHT re.error "unknown extension ?<n at position 1", exit 1. An invalid pattern like "[" -> UNCAUGHT re.error "unterminated character set at position 0", exit 1. These crashes happen in every draft.
- "format" is NEVER asserted (no format checker is passed): {"format":"email"} on "nope", {"format":"date-time"} on "nope", {"format":"regex"} on "nope" all -> True/0 in every draft.

=== 10. $ref / referencing behavior ===
- Unresolvable JSON pointer: exit 1, "jsonschema.exceptions._WrappedReferencingError: PointerToNowhere: '/definitions/missing' does not exist within {…the whole schema repr…}". Same in all six drafts.
- Any remote or relative $ref that isn't in the schema: exit 1, "_WrappedReferencingError: Unresolvable: http://example.com/nope" (or "Unresolvable: nonexistent.json"). Nothing is fetched from the network or disk.
- {"$ref":"#"} (self-reference to the root) -> exit 1 RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded, in all six drafts.
- Plain-name fragment via {"$id":"#frag"}: works ONLY in draft6 and draft7 (False/1). In d3/d4 and in 2019-09/2020-12 it is exit 1 "_WrappedReferencingError: NoSuchAnchor: 'frag' does not exist within {…}" (2019+ require $anchor; 3/4 use "id").
- {"$id":"http://ex.com/r", "properties":{"a":{"$ref":"http://ex.com/r"}}} (recursion through an absolute $id): d3/d4 -> exit 1 Unresolvable: http://ex.com/r (they honour "id", not "$id"); d6/7/2019/2020 -> False/1.
- Both "$id" and legacy "id" as a base for a local pointer $ref work in all drafts (the pointer resolves against the same document): False/1 each.
- $recursiveRef:"#" -> ignored (True/0) in d3/4/6/7 and in 2020-12, but in 2019-09 it is a real keyword and self-recursion gives exit 1 RecursionError.
- $dynamicRef:"#x" with no matching anchor -> ignored (True/0) in d3/4/6/7/2019, but 2020-12 -> exit 1 "_WrappedReferencingError: NoSuchAnchor: 'x' does not exist within {…}".

=== 11. Miscellaneous validation shape ===
- Boolean SUBSCHEMAS work in every draft at the properties level: {"properties":{"a":false}} on {"a":1} -> False/1 in all six; on {} -> True/0. additionalProperties:true -> True/0. (Only boolean `items` crashes in d3/d4.)
- Keywords that don't apply to the instance type are silently skipped: {"properties":{...}} on 1 -> True/0; {"required":["a"]} on 1 -> True/0; {"items":{...}} on 1 -> True/0.
- Unknown keywords ($comment, "unknownKw", "x") are always ignored.
- oneOf with TWO matching branches -> False/1 in d4+ (True/0 in d3, no oneOf). anyOf with no match -> False/1 in d4+.

=== 12. JSON parsing of the args ===
--a is json.loads'd FIRST (line 11), then --b (line 12), so a malformed instance masks a malformed schema. Bad JSON -> uncaught json.decoder.JSONDecodeError, exit 1, stdout empty. Exact messages: '' / 'nan' / "'1'" / '-.5' / '-' -> "Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)"; '{' -> "Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 2 (char 1)"; '01' -> "Extra data: line 1 column 2 (char 1)". Python's json ACCEPTS NaN / Infinity / -Infinity and tolerates surrounding whitespace and trailing newlines.

=== 13. CLI / argparse (prog name "test13_executable") ===
- --a and --b are required=True, type=str. '--a=VAL' and '--a VAL' both work; order is free.
- Repeated options: LAST WINS, no error ('--a 1 --a "x"' uses "x"; '--a 1 --b {} --b false' -> False/1; '--a 1 --b {} --a 2' uses 2).
- Values may contain spaces, newlines and non-ASCII UTF-8; all pass through untouched.
- Missing args: exit 2, stdout empty, stderr exactly "usage: test13_executable [-h] --a A --b B\ntest13_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --a, --b\n" (with only "--a" or only "--b" when just one is missing).
- Unknown option / stray positional: exit 2, "…error: unrecognized arguments: --c 1" (or "extra", "5", "--"). The REQUIRED-argument check fires BEFORE the unrecognized check, so '-a 1 -b {}' reports "the following arguments are required: --a, --b" and '-a 1 --b {}' reports "required: --a". Single-dash '-a'/'-b' are not registered. Uppercase '--A/--B' -> required-args error.
- '-h'/'--help' go to STDOUT with exit 0, exactly: "usage: test13_executable [-h] --a A --b B\n\noptions:\n  -h, --help  show this help message and exit\n  --a A       instance (JSON string)\n  --b B       schema (JSON string)\n" (Python 3.10+ "options:" wording). Help wins even when --a/--b are present and even when placed last.
- Prefix abbreviation is ON: '--h', '--he', '--hel' all print help (exit 0); '--hell' is not a prefix -> exit 2 required-args error.
- Missing value: '--a --b {}' and '--a 1 --b' -> exit 2 "…error: argument --a: expected one argument". Values that look like options are rejected the same way: '--a -x', '--a --1', '--a -Infinity', '--a -1e5'. BUT argparse's negative-number heuristic accepts values matching a plain decimal: '--a -5', '--a -0' (both parse fine, -0 -> Draft202012Validator/True/0) and '--a -.5' (accepted by argparse, then fails in json.loads with exit 1). The '=' form bypasses the heuristic entirely: '--a=-Infinity --b={}' parses to -inf and prints Draft202012Validator/True/0; '--a=--b --b={}' is accepted by argparse and fails later in json.loads.
- Empty-string values: '--a "" --b {}' and '--a= --b=' -> exit 1 JSONDecodeError.
- '--' separator: '-- --a 1 --b {}' -> exit 2 "required: --a, --b"; '--a 1 -- --b {}' -> exit 2 "required: --b"; '--a 1 --b {} --' -> exit 2 "unrecognized arguments: --"; bare '--', '-', '-x' alone -> exit 2 required-args error.

=== 14. Exit codes ===
0 = normal (exactly 3 stdout lines; a DeprecationWarning may accompany on stderr), or -h/--help. 1 = uncaught Python exception (traceback on stderr, stdout EMPTY — all three prints come after validation). 2 = argparse usage error (usage + error on stderr, stdout empty).

=== 15. Vector file ===
/workspace/probes/validator-selection.jsonl, 1088 lines of JSONL. Each line: {"a": <instance JSON text>, "b": <schema JSON text>, "out": <exact stdout>, "exit": <int>} plus "stderr" when non-empty and "argv" for CLI-shape probes (for those, a/b are null). I re-ran 16 randomly chosen lines spanning the original 315 and the 773 appended ones and every one matched byte-for-byte (PYI process numbers normalized), so the file is machine-generated and trustworthy. The only defect found was in the prior PROSE, not the data: the claim that 'HTTPS://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' emits the deprecation warning is false (line 52 records no stderr), and the claim that type:"integer" rejects 1.0 in draft3/draft4 is false (all six drafts accept it).
gotchas: CORRECTION to prior findings: scheme case-folding is uniform. 'HTTPS://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' and 'HtTpS://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema' resolve cleanly with NO deprecation warning. Only HOST or PATH case changes make a URI unknown.
CORRECTION to prior findings: {"type":"integer"} ACCEPTS 1.0 (and 1e2) in ALL six drafts, including draft-03 and draft-04. There is no float rejection.

maxLength/minLength count Unicode CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 code units. One astral emoji has length 1, so {"maxLength":1} passes and {"minLength":2} fails. A JS `.length` implementation gets this backwards. Combining marks are NOT normalized ('e'+U+0301 is length 2).

pattern is Python re.search: UNANCHORED, `\d`/`\w` are Unicode-aware (matches Arabic-Indic digits and accented letters), and `$` matches before a trailing newline so '^a$' MATCHES "a\n". Inline flags '(?i)' and '(?P<n>...)' work; JS '(?<n>...)' and any invalid pattern raise re.error and exit 1.
'format' is never asserted — no format checker is installed, so {"format":"email"} on garbage is always True/0 in every draft.

Booleans are never numbers: {"type":"integer"}/{"type":"number"} reject true; const/enum treat true and 1 as different; uniqueItems considers [true,1] and [0,false] UNIQUE. But 1 and 1.0 (and 0 and -0) ARE equal for const/enum/uniqueItems, and object key order is irrelevant for uniqueItems deep equality.
Big integers keep exact Python precision: const 10000000000000000001 distinguishes from ...000 (a JS double cannot).
json.loads accepts NaN / Infinity / -Infinity. NaN passes {"type":"number"}, and [NaN,NaN] is a uniqueItems DUPLICATE.

Draft-03 has NO allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not/multipleOf/minProperties/maxProperties/const/contains/propertyNames/numeric-exclusive/if-then. So {"not":{}} on 1 is True/0 in draft3 but False/1 in draft4+. Draft-03-only keywords: divisibleBy, disallow, extends, per-property required:true, and type-as-list-of-SCHEMAS (which crashes with 'unhashable type: dict' in draft4+).
Draft-06 still has NO if/then/else — that is draft-07+. Draft-06 does add const, contains, propertyNames and numeric exclusiveMinimum/Maximum.
items as a BOOLEAN crashes draft3/draft4 with TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable (even items:true on []). items:false on [1,2] gives 2 errors in draft6/7/2019 but exactly 1 error in 2020-12.

items as an ARRAY crashes 2020-12 (AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'), and so does additionalItems alongside it. The same crash happens with no $schema at all and after any unknown-$schema fallback, since the fallback is 2020-12.

dependencies STRING form {"a":"b"} works in draft3 (False/1), CRASHES in draft4/6/7 (AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'), and is ignored in 2019/2020. dependencies SCHEMA form is ignored in draft3, honoured in 4/6/7, ignored in 2019/2020.
minContains:0 with contains on an empty array: True/0 in draft3/4 (both unknown), FALSE/1 in draft6/7 (contains applies, minContains does not), True/0 in 2019/2020.

$ref edge cases all exit 1: missing pointer -> PointerToNowhere, any remote/relative URI -> Unresolvable (nothing is fetched), {"$ref":"#"} -> RecursionError. Plain-name fragment via {"$id":"#frag"} works ONLY in draft6/7; elsewhere it is NoSuchAnchor + exit 1. Absolute-$id recursion works in 6+ but is Unresolvable in 3/4.

$recursiveRef is live only in 2019-09 (self-ref -> RecursionError, exit 1) and inert everywhere else; $dynamicRef is live only in 2020-12 (unknown anchor -> NoSuchAnchor, exit 1) and inert everywhere else.

Error counts: additionalProperties:false yields exactly ONE error no matter how many extras, and uniqueItems yields exactly one; but properties/patternProperties/propertyNames/items/additionalProperties-as-schema yield one PER failing child at any depth, and allOf yields one per failing branch (recursively).
type:"any" is valid only in draft-03; in draft-04+ it raises UnknownType and exits 1 with EMPTY stdout, even when the keyword sits in a nested subschema.

argparse negative-number heuristic: '--a -5', '--a -0', '--a -.5' are accepted as values, but '--a -1e5' and '--a -Infinity' are rejected with 'expected one argument'. The '=' form ('--a=-Infinity') bypasses this and works.
Duplicate JSON keys are last-wins, including duplicate "$schema" — {"$schema":draft-07,"$schema":draft-03} dispatches to Draft3Validator.

$schema: null/false/""/"   "/0 quietly fall back (warning + 2020-12); 1/-1/1.5/true crash with AttributeError 'no attribute decode'; {} or [] crash with TypeError: unhashable type. Three different outcomes for the same 'wrong type' category.

A whole-schema of null or a number crashes inside validator_for; a whole-schema that is a string or array survives validator_for and crashes later in referencing._dollar_id. Both are exit 1 with empty stdout.
Crash tracebacks end with '[PYI-<random>:ERROR] Failed to execute script test13' whose number changes every run — never diff on it.

result.findings:
PROGRAM UNDER TEST (/workspace/dataset/test13_executable, source /workspace/dataset/test13.py): parses --a as the instance JSON and --b as the schema JSON, then `vc = validators.validator_for(schema); v = vc(schema); print(vc.__name__); print(v.is_valid(instance)); print(len(list(v.iter_errors(instance))))`. Three stdout lines, exit 0. Line 2 ("True"/"False") is ALWAYS exactly `errorCount == 0` (verified over all 950 non-crashing vectors — zero inconsistencies). No format_checker is ever installed and check_schema is never called, so invalid schemas are never reported as schema errors. On ANY Python exception stdout is COMPLETELY EMPTY (no partial lines — is_valid runs before the first print) and exit code is 1, with a traceback on stderr ending in `[PYI-xxxx:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13' due to unhandled exception!`.

DIALECT SELECTION (line 1). `validator_for` behaves as: take `schema.get("$schema")`; if the schema is a bool, has no `$schema`, or `$schema` is JSON null -> Draft202012Validator (the latest, the default). Otherwise the id is looked up after STRIPPING TRAILING '#': `http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema` (no '#') -> Draft7Validator and `https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema#` (with '#') -> Draft201909Validator, so both spellings of all six ids work. Lookup is CASE-SENSITIVE: `HTTPS://JSON-SCHEMA.ORG/DRAFT/2020-12/SCHEMA` -> Draft202012Validator (fallback). Any unrecognized string id (`http://example.com/unknown`, `http://json-schema.org/schema#`, `http://json-schema.org/draft-05/schema#`, `""`) silently falls back to Draft202012Validator, exit 0. A NON-STRING, NON-NULL `$schema` (`123`, `["x"]`) CRASHES (exit 1, empty stdout). Recognized ids: draft-03 `http://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema#`, draft-04 `...draft-04/schema#`, draft-06, draft-07, `https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema`, `https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema`.

WHOLE-SCHEMA FORMS. `{}` -> True/0. `true` -> True/0. `false` -> False/1 for every instance type. A schema that is a JSON string, number, array, or null CRASHES (exit 1, empty stdout) — only objects and booleans are usable schemas.

TYPE GATING (all string keywords). minLength, maxLength, pattern, format, content* are no-ops unless the instance is a JSON string. Non-string instances (number, float, bool true/false, null, array, object) always yield 0 errors from these keywords, and the gate happens BEFORE any coercion or regex compilation: `{"pattern":"["}`, `{"pattern":123}`, `{"minLength":"5"}`, `{"maxLength":{}}` against `5`, `1.5`, `true`, `false`, `null`, `[]`, `["x"]`, `{}`, `{"k":"v"}` all return True/0 with exit 0 instead of crashing. Booleans are NOT strings here.

minLength / maxLength — CODE POINT semantics (Python len), never UTF-16 units. "😀"(U+1F600) length 1; "😀😀" 2; "a😀b" 3; flag "🇺🇸" 2; single regional indicator "🇺" 1; ZWJ family "👩‍👩‍👧" 5; U+10FFFF 1; ZWJ U+200D alone 1. This holds identically when the astral char arrives as a JSON surrogate-pair escape `"😀"` (json.loads recombines it) -> length 1. LONE SURROGATES are accepted by json.loads and count as 1 code point: `"\ud800"` maxLength:1 -> True; `"\udfff"` minLength:2 -> False. Embedded NUL `"a�b"` is length 3 and is a perfectly ordinary character. A JS port MUST use `[...s].length` / `Array.from(s).length`, and must tolerate lone surrogates (so `[...s]` is correct — it yields the lone surrogate as one element). NO Unicode normalization anywhere: precomposed "é"(U+00E9)=1 vs decomposed "e"+U+0301=2 (maxLength:1 fails, minLength:2 passes); "Å" decomposed 2 vs precomposed 1; Hangul "가" precomposed 1 vs jamo 2; Devanagari "क्ष" 3; Thai "ก"+U+0E48 = 2; "e"+U+0301+U+0301 = 3 (maxLength:2 fails). Fullwidth "１２" = 2. "\r\n" = 2. A 1000-char ASCII string is 1000.
Comparison is strict: error iff `len(s) < minLength` / `len(s) > maxLength`; equality passes (len 3 with minLength:3 and maxLength:3 -> True/0). minLength:0 / maxLength:0 on "" -> True; maxLength:0 on "abc" -> False; "" with minLength:1 -> 1 error.
The bound is used as a raw Python number, so fractional bounds matter: minLength:3.5 on "abc" -> False; maxLength:2.5 on "abc" -> False; maxLength:2.999999999999999 on "abc" -> False; maxLength:0.5 on "" -> True; minLength:0.5 on "" -> False; minLength:2.0000001 on "ab" -> False; minLength:3e0 and minLength:0.1e1 == 3 and 1. FLOAT PRECISION: minLength:3.0000000000000001 rounds to exactly 3.0 in IEEE754 -> "abc" passes (True/0) — a JS impl using Number gets this right automatically. Negative bounds: minLength:-1 (and -1e400) always True; maxLength:-1 always False. -0.0 behaves as 0: maxLength:-0.0 on "abc" -> False, on "" -> True; minLength:-0.0 on "" -> True. Infinity from `1e400` works: minLength:1e400 -> always False, maxLength:1e400 -> always True. Huge integers (1e20, 3e22 written as integer literals) work. JSON booleans are Python ints: minLength:true == 1, minLength:false == 0 (both pass "abc"); maxLength:true == 1 and maxLength:false == 0 both reject "abc". DUPLICATE JSON KEYS in the schema: last wins (`{"minLength":1,"minLength":5}` behaves as 5); same for the instance object (`{"a":"xxxxx","a":"y"}` -> the value is "y").
CRASH: a non-numeric minLength/maxLength raises TypeError ONLY when the instance is a string — `{"minLength":"5"}`, `{"maxLength":"3"}`, `{"minLength":"0"}` (even against ""), `{"minLength":null}`, `{"minLength":[5]}`, `{"minLength":{}}`, `{"maxLength":[]}`, `{"maxLength":{}}` -> exit 1, empty stdout, `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'str'`.
Each of minLength and maxLength contributes at most ONE error; both failing at once = exactly 2 top-level errors, identical in all six drafts.

pattern — Python `re.search` (SUBSTRING SEARCH, never fullmatch), re.UNICODE implicitly on, no other flags. "abc" vs "b" valid; vs "^b" invalid; vs "c$" valid; vs "^abc$" valid; "abcd" vs "^abc$" invalid. Empty pattern "" matches everything.
Anchors: Python `$` matches at end OR immediately before a SINGLE trailing "\n". "abc\n" vs "^abc$" and vs "abc$" and vs "c$" -> VALID; "abc\n\n" -> invalid; "abc\r" and "abc\r\n" -> INVALID (\r is not special). "" vs "$" -> valid; "\n" vs "^$" -> VALID (empty match at position 0). `\Z` is absolute end: "abc\n" vs "^abc\Z" invalid, but "abc\n" vs "^abc\n\Z" valid. `\A` is absolute start; "\nabc" vs "^abc" -> invalid (no MULTILINE by default). `(?m)` makes ^/$ match around "\n" ONLY: "a\nb" vs "(?m)^b$" valid, but "a\rb" and "a b" vs "(?m)^b$" invalid. `.` excludes \n by default ("a\nb" vs "a.b" invalid, "(?s)a.b" valid).
Regex operates on code points, so `.` consumes a whole astral char: "😀" vs "^.$" valid, "^..$" invalid; "😀😀" vs "^..$" valid; "🇺🇸" vs "^..$" valid; ZWJ family vs "^.....$" valid; a lone surrogate "\ud800" vs "^.$" valid; an emoji object key vs propertyNames `^.$` valid. Character-class ranges are code-point ranges: "😀"/"😁" match `^[😀-😂]$`, "😃" does not, a lone surrogate does not. Decomposed "é" vs "^.$" invalid, "^..$" valid.
Python-specific syntax that WORKS: named groups `(?P<n>...)`, named backrefs `(?P=n)`, numeric backrefs `\1` (also with a preceding named group), comments `(?#...)`, GLOBAL inline flags only at pattern START `(?i)(?m)(?s)(?x)(?a)(?u)` and repeats/combos like `(?i)(?i)a`, scoped flags `(?i:...)`/`(?-i:...)`, `(?:)`, lookahead `(?=)`/`(?!)`, FIXED-WIDTH lookbehind `(?<=ab)`/`(?<!a)`, atomic groups `(?>a*)` and possessive quantifiers `a*+`/`a++` (Python 3.11+; "aaa" vs "^(?>a*)a$" invalid = correctly atomic, "aaa" vs "^a*+a$" invalid, "^a++$" valid), `\N{LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A}`, octal `\141` and `\0`, `\x61`, `a`, `\U0001F600`, `\a`, `\b`, empty alternatives `a|`, `|a`, `(?:a)|`, empty group `()`, lazy quantifiers `a*? a+? a??`, `a{2,}`, `a{,3}` (== `{0,3}`), and a literal unescaped `{`/`}` when not a valid quantifier (`a{` matches the two-char string "a{", `a}` likewise). Non-alphanumeric escapes are literals: `\/ \- \# \<space>` all compile and match the bare character. `(?x)` VERBOSE really strips whitespace and `#` comments: "abc" matches `(?x)a b c` but "a b c" does NOT. Character sets: a `]` immediately after `[` is a literal member, so `[]a]` == the set {']', 'a'} (matches "]" and "abc", not "b") while `[]` and `[^]` are UNTERMINATED and CRASH; `[[]`, `[a-b-c]`, `[]^]` all compile. POSIX classes are NOT special: `[[:alpha:]]+` compiles as an ordinary set and usually fails to match.
Unicode class semantics (`re.UNICODE` default for str): `\d` matches any Nd — Arabic-Indic "١٢٣", Devanagari "१२३", Thai "๑๒", Bengali "১", fullwidth "１２" — but NOT "²" (No), NOT "½" (No), NOT "Ⅰ" (Nl). `[0-9]` matches none of those. `\w` matches accented letters (precomposed "café", "Ünïcödé", "naïve"), CJK "日本語"/"中", Arabic-Indic digits, "²", "①", "µ", and "_", but NOT a bare combining acute U+0301 (Mn), NOT "☃", NOT emoji ("😀" is `\W` and `\S`). Consequence: decomposed "café" fails `^\w{4}$` (5 code points, U+0301 is not \w) but passes `^\w{4}.$`; precomposed "café" passes `^\w{4}$`. `\s` matches: space, \t(09), \v(0B), \f(0C), \r(0D), U+001C, U+001D, U+001F, U+0085(NEL), U+00A0(NBSP), U+1680(OGHAM SPACE), U+2003(EM SPACE), U+2009, U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+205F, U+3000. It does NOT match U+180E, U+200B(ZWSP), or U+FEFF(BOM). `\b` is unicode-aware ("café" vs `\bcafé\b` valid; "xabcx" vs `\babc\b` invalid; "x abc x" valid; "a1b" vs `\b1\b` invalid, "a 1 b" valid). `(?a)` restricts to ASCII: "é" fails `(?a)^\w+$`, "١٢" fails `(?a)^\d+$`, "abc" passes `(?a)^\w+$`.
`(?i)` uses Python's SIMPLE case folding, not full casefold: "ß" vs `(?i)^SS$` -> INVALID; but "K"(KELVIN U+212A) vs `(?i)^k$` and vs `(?i)^[a-z]$` -> VALID; "İ"(U+0130) vs `(?i)^i$` -> VALID; "ı"(dotless i) vs `(?i)^I$` -> VALID; "ς" vs `(?i)^Σ$` -> VALID; "ẞ" vs `(?i)^ß$` -> VALID; "é" vs `(?i)^É$` -> VALID; "abc" vs `(?i)^[A-Z]+$` -> VALID; `(?i)(abc)\1` matches "abcABC".
CRASHES (exit 1, EMPTY stdout, traceback from re/_parser.py or re/__init__.py), reached ONLY when a string actually hits the keyword: `[`, `[]`, `[^]`, `[z-a]`, `[a-\d]`, `[\d-a]`, `(unclosed`, `)`, `(*)`, `*`, `a**`, `{2}`, `a{2,1}`, `a{2,3}{2}`, `\` and `a\` (bad escape at end), `\2`/`\8` (invalid group ref), `\p{L}+`/`\pL` (bad escape \p), `\Q abc \E` (bad escape \Q), `\k<n>` (JS/.NET backref), `(?P<1bad>a)`, `(?<name>a)` and `(?'n'a)` (.NET named groups), `(?P<x>a)(?P<x>b)` (redefinition), `(?P>n)`, `(?R)`, `(?y)a` (unknown flag), `(?L)^\w+$` (LOCALE with str), `(?<=a+)b` (VARIABLE-WIDTH LOOKBEHIND — Python forbids it, JS allows it), `a|*`, `abc(?(1)x)`, and (Python 3.11+) global inline flags NOT at pattern start: `^(?i)x$`, `a(?i)bc`. `a{1000000}` compiles fine and is fast. A NON-STRING pattern value (`123`, `0`, `null`, `true`, `false`, `["a"]`, `{}`) -> `TypeError: first argument must be string or compiled pattern`.
Compilation is LAZY AND INSTANCE-DRIVEN. `{"properties":{"y":{"pattern":"["}}}` is fine for `{"x":1}` and for `{"y":5}` but crashes for `{"y":"s"}`. `{"definitions":{"s":{"pattern":"["}}}` and `{"$defs":{"s":{"pattern":"["}}}` never crash on their own (never reached), but `{"$ref":"#/definitions/s","definitions":{"s":{"pattern":"["}}}` does. `{"contains":{"pattern":"["}}` is fine for the string "s" (not an array) and crashes for `["s"]`. `{"patternProperties":{"[":{...}}}` is fine for 5, "s", and even `{}` (no keys to iterate) but crashes for `{"a":1}`. `{"propertyNames":{"pattern":"["}}` crashes for `{"a":1}` (keys are strings). `{"items":{"pattern":"["}}` crashes for `["x"]`. The exception ESCAPES every error-collecting applicator — anyOf, oneOf, allOf, not, not/not, if/then, $ref, enum siblings — it is never swallowed into `context`.
pattern contributes at most ONE error.

format — NEVER ASSERTED, in any draft, for any name. Zero format checkers are installed. email, idn-email, date-time, date, time, duration, ipv4, ipv6, uuid, uri, uri-reference, iri, hostname, idn-hostname, json-pointer, relative-json-pointer, regex, uri-template, plus the draft-03 names ip-address, host-name, color, style, phone, utc-millisec, plus unknown names and `""`, all return True/0 against "!!!definitely-not-valid!!!" in draft-03/04/06/07/2019-09/2020-12. `{"format":"regex"}` against the string "[" is True/0 (the format value is never compiled). Declaring `$vocabulary: {".../vocab/format-assertion": true}` in a 2020-12 schema does NOT enable assertion. A non-string format value (123, null, {}, true) is silently ignored, no crash. format contributes 0 errors always.

contentEncoding / contentMediaType / contentSchema — NEVER ASSERTED in any draft; pure annotations, 0 errors. "!!!not-base64!!!" with contentEncoding:"base64" -> True/0 in all six drafts; "notjson" with contentMediaType:"application/json" -> True/0; contentSchema is never evaluated, including `contentSchema:false` and `contentSchema:{"type":"integer"}` against a non-JSON string. Python '$' matches at end OR before a SINGLE trailing '
': 'abc

', 'abc', 'abc

Python re is UNICODE by default: \d matches Arabic-Indic ١٢٣, Devanagari, Thai, Bengali and fullwidth digits (Nd) but NOT ² ½ Ⅰ (No/Nl); \w matches accented letters, CJK, µ, ², ① and _; \w does NOT match combining marks (Mn), ☃, or emoji. \s matches \t \v \f \r U+001C U+001D U+001F U+0085 U+00A0 U+1680 U+2003 U+2009 U+200A U+2028 U+2029 U+205F U+3000 but NOT U+180E, U+200B, U+FEFF. JS \d/\w/\s differ — translate them.

Character sets: ']' immediately after '[' is a LITERAL member, so '[]a]' is the set {']','a'} and compiles, while '[]' and '[^]' are UNTERMINATED and CRASH. JS treats '[^]' as 'any character' — opposite behavior.
Python allows a literal unescaped '{' when it is not a valid quantifier ('a{' matches the string 'a{'), and 'a{,3}' means {0,3}. JS with the /u flag throws on both.
Variable-width lookbehind '(?<=a+)b' CRASHES in Python but is legal in JS. Conversely '\k<n>' (JS backref), '(?<name>...)' (JS/.NET named group) and '\p{L}' CRASH in Python but are legal in JS.

Python-only syntax that must be supported: (?P<n>...), (?P=n), (?#comment), global inline flags (?i)(?m)(?s)(?x)(?a)(?u) at pattern START ONLY (mid-pattern global flags CRASH on Python 3.11+), scoped (?i:...)/(?-i:...), \A, \Z, \N{NAME}, octal \141 and \0, \U0001F600, atomic (?>...), possessive a*+ / a++. (?x) VERBOSE genuinely strips whitespace and #-comments.
(?i) is SIMPLE case folding, not full casefold: 'ß' does NOT match (?i)^SS$, but KELVIN SIGN K matches (?i)k and (?i)[a-z], İ matches (?i)i, ı matches (?i)I, ς matches (?i)Σ.
