THE CENTRAL RULE (DESCEND vs COLLAPSE). A keyword either (a) DESCENDs -- yield from validator.descend(...), so every child error is re-yielded and becomes its OWN top-level error -- or (b) COLLAPSEs -- builds exactly one ValidationError whose children go into .context, which does NOT add to the top-level count. Measured classification (each tested with a 2-failing-keyword subschema {"minLength":9,"maxLength":0} against "ab"):
  DESCEND: allOf, then, else, properties, patternProperties, additionalProperties (ONLY when the value is a schema object), items (draft-04..2019-09 single-schema form, and 2020-12 schema form), prefixItems, additionalItems (draft-07 schema form), propertyNames, dependentSchemas, dependencies (schema form), $ref, draft-03 extends.
  COLLAPSE (exactly 1 error when failing, 0 when passing): anyOf, oneOf, not, contains, minContains/maxContains, draft-03 disallow, draft-03 type when given an array.
  NEITHER (fixed per-item counts): required yields ONE error PER missing property ({} vs {"required":["a","b","c"]} => 3; duplicates count separately, {"required":["a","a"]} => 2). dependentRequired and draft<=7 array-form dependencies yield one error per missing dependency ({"a":1} vs {"dependencies":{"a":["b","c"]}} => 2). additionalProperties:false yields exactly ONE aggregate error no matter how many extras (2 extras => 1, 3 extras => 1). 2020-12 items:false yields exactly ONE aggregate error for all extras ([1,2] => 1; [1,2,3] with prefixItems:[{}] => 1). draft-07 additionalItems:false also 1.
  DESCEND multiplies: {"items":{"allOf":[3 failing]}} on ["a","a","a"] => 9. {"items":{"items":{"allOf":[2 failing]}}} on [["a","a"],["a","a"]] => 8. {"propertyNames":{"allOf":[{"maxLength":0},{"pattern":"^z"}]}} on {"a":"x","b":"y"} => 4. Three nested properties levels + allOf of 3 => 3. {"properties":{"a":{allOf 2},"b":{allOf 2}}} => 4.
  A COLLAPSE keyword ANYWHERE on the path caps that subtree at 1: {"anyOf":[{"allOf":[2 failing]}]} => 1; {"items":{"anyOf":[{"allOf":[2]}]}} on ["a"] => 1; {"properties":{"x":{"anyOf":[deep 2-failing tree]}}} => 1; {"contains":{"allOf":[2]}} => 1; {"not":{"anyOf":[...]}} => 1. Above a collapse point counting resumes: {"items":{"oneOf":[{"minLength":9}]}} on ["a","a"] => 2.
  Siblings SUM, no short-circuiting between keywords: {"minLength":9,"maxLength":0,"pattern":"^z","type":"number","allOf":[{"minLength":9}],"anyOf":[{"type":"number"}],"oneOf":[],"not":{},"enum":["q"],"const":"q"} on "ab" => 10. {"type":"array","required":["b","c"],"minProperties":5,"allOf":[{"maxProperties":0}],"not":{}} on {"a":1} => 6. Schema key order never changes counts.

allOf. {"allOf":[{"type":"number"},{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]} on "ab" => False/3. {"allOf":[]} => True/0. {"allOf":[true,true]} => True/0. {"allOf":[true,false,false]} => False/2. {"allOf":[false]} => 1. Nested allOf flattens fully. One branch with several failing keywords contributes one error per keyword. allOf never short-circuits: a malformed later element always crashes.

anyOf. Fails => exactly 1 error regardless of branch count or child error counts. {"anyOf":[]} => False/1 (UNLIKE allOf). {"anyOf":[false,false]} => 1. {"anyOf":[true]} => True/0. Triple-nested anyOf of a failing schema => 1. Two sibling anyOfs each failing => 2. anyOf SHORT-CIRCUITS on the first matching branch: {"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},null]} is True/0 on "a" but CRASHES on 1; {"anyOf":[true,null]} => True/0.

oneOf. Exactly 1 error in BOTH failure modes. Zero matches: 1. Two or more matches: 1 -- even 3 matches ({"oneOf":[{},{},{}]} => 1; {"oneOf":[{"type":"number"},{"type":"string"},{"minLength":1},{"maxLength":9}]} on "a" => 1). {"oneOf":[]} => False/1. {"oneOf":[{}]} => True/0. {"oneOf":[true,false]} => True/0. {"oneOf":[false,false,false]} => 1. Exactly one match anywhere in the list (first, middle, or last) => True/0. oneOf does NOT short-circuit -- after the first match it still evaluates every remaining branch to count extra matches, so {"oneOf":[{"type":"string"},null]} CRASHES on "a" while the anyOf equivalent does not. This is the sharpest anyOf/oneOf behavioural difference.

not. Exactly 1 error when the subschema matches; the negated subschema's own error count is irrelevant. {"not":{"type":"string"}} on "ab" => 1. {"not":{}} => 1. {"not":true} => 1. {"not":false} => True/0. {"not":{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0}]}} => True/0. {"not":{"not":{}}} => True/0; {"not":{"not":{"not":{}}}} => 1. {"allOf":[{"not":{}},{"not":{}}]} => 2. {"oneOf":[{"not":{}},{"not":{}}]} => 1. not does NOT contribute annotations for unevaluatedProperties.

if/then/else. Present ONLY in Draft7, 2019-09, 2020-12. Draft3/4/6 treat if/then/else as unknown keywords and IGNORE them ({"$schema":draft-06,"if":{"type":"string"},"then":false} => True/0; draft-07 => False/1). then and else DESCEND: {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}} on "ab" => 2; {"if":{"type":"number"},"else":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}} => 2; on 5, {"if":{"type":"number"},"then":{"minimum":10,"maximum":1,"multipleOf":7}} => 3; an else branch with 3 failing keywords => 3. if ALONE never produces an error even when it fails -- purely a selector. then/else WITHOUT a sibling if are ignored completely ({"then":false} => True/0, {"else":false} => True/0); the if_ handler is the only path that reaches them. Exactly one branch runs: {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":true,"else":false} => True/0. Boolean if works: {"if":true,"then":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":0}} => 2; {"if":false,"else":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":0}} => 2; {"if":{}} behaves like true. Evaluation is LAZY -- an untaken malformed branch never crashes: {"if":{"type":"number"},"then":null} on "a" => True/0 and {"if":{"type":"string"},"else":null} => True/0, but {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":null} and {"if":{"type":"number"},"else":null} CRASH. Combinators inside if work and their errors are discarded: {"if":{"anyOf":[{"type":"number"}]},"else":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":0}} => 2; {"if":{"not":{}},"then":{"minLength":9},"else":{"maxLength":0,"pattern":"^z"}} => 2. Nesting: if/then inside allOf flattens (2); inside anyOf => 1; inside not => 0/1.

$ref AND SIBLING KEYWORDS -- BIGGEST CROSS-DRAFT COUNT DIFFERENCE (missed entirely by the prior report). In Draft4/6/7, keywords SIBLING to $ref are IGNORED: {"$ref":"#/definitions/a","minLength":9,"maxLength":0,"definitions":{"a":{"pattern":"^z","type":"string"}}} on "ab" => 1 (only the ref's own pattern error). The IDENTICAL schema under 2019-09/2020-12 with $defs => 3. Same inside allOf: {"allOf":[{"$ref":"#/X/a","minLength":9}],"X":{"a":{"maxLength":0}}} => 1 under draft-4/6/7, 2 under 2019-09/2020-12. With no siblings, $ref is transparent to counting in every draft: {"$ref":"#/$defs/a","$defs":{"a":{"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0}]}}} => 2, and a $ref reached through nested properties still flattens => 2. Recursive $ref works. An UNRESOLVABLE pointer CRASHES even inside anyOf ({"anyOf":[{"$ref":"#/$defs/missing"}]} crashes -- anyOf does NOT swallow resolution failures); a remote http $ref crashes (no network resolver). 2020-12 $dynamicRef/$dynamicAnchor resolves normally; a 2019-09 $recursiveRef/$recursiveAnchor schema without $id CRASHES.

unevaluatedProperties / unevaluatedItems (2019-09+; IGNORED in draft-07 and earlier: {"properties":{"a":{}},"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1,"b":2} => True/0 under draft-07, False/1 under 2019-09). unevaluatedProperties yields exactly ONE aggregate error regardless of how many properties are unevaluated (1 extra => 1, 2 extras => 1). Successful if/then, anyOf, oneOf, and allOf branches DO contribute property annotations that satisfy it: {"properties":{"a":{}},"if":{"properties":{"a":{}}},"then":{"properties":{"b":{}}},"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1,"b":2} => True/0; the anyOf and allOf equivalents also => True/0; an if/else pair where else is taken also => True/0. A FAILING anyOf branch does not annotate, but a later matching branch does. not does NOT annotate: {"not":{"properties":{"zz":{"type":"number"}}},"properties":{"a":{}},"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"a":1,"b":2} => 2. unevaluatedItems behaves the same and yields 1 error; note {"anyOf":[{"prefixItems":[{},{},{}]}],"unevaluatedItems":false} on [1,2,3] => False/1 under 2019-09 (prefixItems is not a keyword there, so no annotation) but True/0 under 2020-12.

PER-DRAFT KEYWORD AVAILABILITY (an absent keyword is silently ignored => 0 errors, never a schema error). allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not: draft-04+. if/then/else: draft-07+. dependencies: draft-03 through draft-07 ONLY -- REMOVED in 2019-09/2020-12, where {"dependencies":{"a":["b","c"]}} on {"a":1} => True/0 while draft-03/4/6/7 give 2 (schema form likewise 2 vs 0). dependentSchemas/dependentRequired: 2019-09+ only (2 there, 0 in draft<=7). contains: draft-06+ (draft-03/04 ignore). minContains/maxContains: 2019-09+ (draft-07 ignores, so {"contains":{"type":"number"},"maxContains":1} on [1,2,3] => True/0 in draft-07 but False/1 in 2019-09+). propertyNames: draft-06+ (2 errors for a 2-failing subschema; 0 in draft-03/04). const: draft-06+. prefixItems: 2020-12 ONLY -- unknown elsewhere, so {"prefixItems":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"string"}]} on [1,2] is True/0 for draft-03..2019-09 and False/2 for 2020-12. items as an ARRAY (tuple form) plus additionalItems: draft-04..draft-07. items:false on [1,2]: draft-07 DESCENDS per item => 2 errors; 2020-12 emits ONE aggregate error => 1. Boolean subschemas work inside combinators in EVERY draft including draft-04 ({"allOf":[true,false,false]} => 2 under Draft4Validator). Apart from the availability differences here and the $ref-sibling rule, draft-04 through 2020-12 count identically for allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not.

DRAFT-03 (the big special case). Draft3Validator has NO allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if, then, else, const, contains, propertyNames, prefixItems, dependentSchemas, dependentRequired -- all silently ignored, so a pure-combinator schema is vacuously valid. Analogs: extends DESCENDS and accepts a single schema OR an array of schemas ({"extends":{"minLength":9,"maxLength":1}} => 2; {"extends":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1},{"type":"number"}]} => 3; nested {"extends":{"extends":{2 failing}}} => 2; {"extends":[{"extends":{"minLength":9}},{"maxLength":1}]} => 2; {"extends":[]} => True/0; {"extends":{}} => True/0; {"extends":true} CRASHES). disallow COLLAPSES to exactly 1 ({"disallow":"string"} => 1, {"disallow":"any"} => 1, {"disallow":["string","number"]} => 1, {"disallow":[{"type":"object"}]} on {} => 1) and PASSES when its subschemas fail ({"disallow":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]} on "ab" => True/0); {"disallow":[]} => True/0. Draft-03 type given an array is the anyOf analog and COLLAPSES to 1 ({"type":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":1}]} => 1; {"type":[]} => 1; mixed strings and schemas: {"type":[{"minLength":1},"number"]} => True/0, {"type":["number",{"minLength":9}]} => 1). Draft-03 required is a BOOLEAN inside each property schema, one error per missing required property ({"properties":{"a":{"required":true},"b":{"required":true}}} on {} => 2), and combines with extends ({"properties":{"a":{"required":true}},"extends":{"properties":{"b":{"required":true}}}} => 2). Draft-03 IGNORES draft-04-style {"required":["a","b"]} => True/0. divisibleBy is draft-03's multipleOf => 1. extends is draft-03 ONLY -- draft-04/06/07/2020-12 ignore it => True/0.

JAVASCRIPT-REIMPLEMENTER TRAPS (Python semantics leaking through). (1) STRING LENGTH IS CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 units: U+1D11E has length 1, so {"allOf":[{"maxLength":1}]} => True/0 and {"allOf":[{"minLength":2}]} => 1; two emoji have length 2 so {"maxLength":2} passes; a JS .length implementation gets all of these backwards. But combining marks DO count separately: "e"+U+0301 has length 2, so {"maxLength":1} => 1 error. {"propertyNames":{"allOf":[{"maxLength":1}]}} on an emoji key => True/0. (2) REGEX IS PYTHON re.search, NOT JS RegExp: pattern is a SEARCH not a full match ({"pattern":"b"} on "abc" => valid, {"pattern":"^b"} => 1). Python $ matches BEFORE a trailing newline, so {"pattern":"^a$"} on "a\n" => True/0 (JS would fail) and {"not":{"pattern":"^a$"}} on "a\n" => 1. \d and \w are UNICODE-aware: Arabic-Indic digit U+0663 matches "^\\d$" => True/0; "e"+U+0301 matches "^\\w$" => True/0. Python-only syntax works: inline flags (?i)abc matches "ABC"; \Z is supported; named groups (?P<x>a) are supported -- all three THROW in JS RegExp. "." matches an astral char as one unit: "^.$" matches an emoji => True/0. An INVALID regex like {"pattern":"["} CRASHES (exit 1). Overlapping patternProperties both apply: {"patternProperties":{"^a":{"type":"number"},"X$":{"type":"number"}}} on {"aX":"s","aY":"s"} => 3. (3) BOOLEANS ARE NOT NUMBERS despite Python bool<:int -- jsonschema unbools explicitly: true is neither "integer" nor "number" (1 error each); {"oneOf":[{"type":"integer"},{"type":"boolean"}]} => True/0 for both true and 1; {"enum":[1]} rejects true and {"enum":[true]} rejects 1; {"const":1} rejects true and {"const":true} rejects 1; {"const":[true]} rejects [1]; uniqueItems treats them as DISTINCT ([true,1] unique, [0,false] unique, but [1,1.0,true] => 1 error because 1 and 1.0 collide). (4) 1 vs 1.0: numerically EQUAL for const/enum/uniqueItems ({"oneOf":[{"const":1},{"const":1.0}]} => 1 error from TWO matches, for both instance 1 and instance 1.0; {"oneOf":[{"const":1e2},{"const":100}]} on 100 => 1; [1,1.0] fails uniqueItems; {"const":{"a":1.0}} matches {"a":1}). But type:"integer" DIFFERS BY DRAFT: 1.0 is NOT an integer in draft-03/draft-04 but IS in draft-06+ (so {"oneOf":[{"type":"integer"},{"type":"number"}]} on 1.0 => True/0 in draft-04 and False/1 in draft-06+ -- an actual validity flip). -0.0 and 1e2 are integers in draft-06+. (5) -0: JSON -0 parses to Python int 0, so {"const":-0} matches 0, {"oneOf":[{"const":0},{"const":-0}]} => 1 error (two matches), and [0,-0] FAILS uniqueItems. (6) FLOAT PRECISION: multipleOf uses float division, so {"multipleOf":0.1} on 0.3 FAILS (1 error) while {"multipleOf":0.0001} on 0.0075 and {"multipleOf":1.5} on 4.5 pass; {"multipleOf":1e-308} on 1e308 fails. Arbitrary-precision integers work: 12345678901234567890123 satisfies {"type":"integer"} and {"multipleOf":1}. 1e400 parses to float inf and satisfies {"type":"number"}. (7) OBJECT KEYS: duplicate JSON keys -> LAST wins ({"a":1,"a":2} matches {"properties":{"a":{"const":2}}}). Insertion order never changes error COUNTS. Deep equality is order-insensitive for objects ({"const":{"b":2,"a":1}} matches {"a":1,"b":2}) but order-SENSITIVE for arrays ({"enum":[[2,1],[1,2]]} matches [1,2] only via the second entry). (8) TYPE-INAPPLICABLE KEYWORDS ARE NO-OPS, silently reducing counts: {"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0},{"pattern":"^z"}]} on the NUMBER 1 => True/0; {"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"minItems":9},{"maxItems":0}]} on [1,2,3] => 2 (minLength skipped); {"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"type":"string"}]} on null => 1; {"properties":{"x":{"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"minLength":9}]}}} with x=1 => ONE error, not two. (9) format is NOT asserted by default: {"allOf":[{"format":"email"},{"format":"date"}]} on "zz" => True/0. (10) Unknown keywords and $comment are ignored without error.

contains DETAIL. Collapses to 1. Empty array with any contains => 1. {"contains":false} on [] => 1. {"contains":true} on [1] => True/0. A NON-ARRAY instance makes contains a no-op ({"contains":{"type":"number"}} on "a" => True/0). minContains/maxContains each add their own single error when violated ([1,2,3] with maxContains:1 => 1; minContains:5 => 1; minContains:2,maxContains:2 => 1). {"contains":{"type":"number"},"minContains":0} on [] => True/0. contains and a sibling items both fire: {"contains":{allOf 2 failing},"items":{allOf 2 failing}} on ["a","a"] => 5 (1 + 4).

CRASH MATRIX (exit=1, empty stdout). For allOf/anyOf/oneOf the value is iterated and each element handed to the schema machinery. NON-CRASHING degenerate values are exactly the EMPTY ITERABLES "" and {}: {"allOf":""} and {"allOf":{}} => True/0 (vacuous), while {"anyOf":""}, {"anyOf":{}}, {"oneOf":""}, {"oneOf":{}} => False/1 (nothing matched), mirroring {"allOf":[]} => True/0 vs {"anyOf":[]}/{"oneOf":[]} => False/1. EVERYTHING ELSE CRASHES: non-empty strings ({"allOf":"x"}, {"allOf":"ab"} -- iterating yields chars, AttributeError 'str' has no attribute 'get'), non-empty objects ({"allOf":{"type":"number"}}, {"allOf":{"a":{...}}}, {"allOf":{"":{}}} -- iterating yields keys), and all non-iterables (0, 1.5, null, true, false). Bad ELEMENTS crash too: {"allOf":[null]}, {"allOf":[1]}, {"allOf":[[]]}, {"allOf":[[{...}]]}, {"anyOf":[[]]}. Because anyOf short-circuits, a bad element AFTER a matching branch is never reached (no crash); oneOf always scans the rest, so it always crashes. For not, ONLY a dict or bool is legal: {"not":{}} => 1, {"not":true} => 1, {"not":false} => 0, while {"not":[]}, {"not":""}, {"not":"x"}, {"not":0}, {"not":1.5}, {"not":null}, {"not":[{...}]} ALL CRASH -- note {"not":[]} and {"not":""} crash even though empty. Same for if: {"if":{}}, {"if":true}, {"if":false} are fine; {"if":[]}, {"if":""}, {"if":"x"}, {"if":0}, {"if":null} crash. contains and propertyNames crash on null/1/[]/"" values. Other crashes: {"pattern":"["} (invalid regex), {"$schema":7}, draft-03 {"extends":true}, unresolvable $ref pointers (including inside anyOf), remote http $ref, and 2019-09 $recursiveRef without $id. Malformed JSON in either --a or --b also crashes the same way.
gotchas: The prior report's vector count (193) was wrong (file had 146) and several cited vectors did not exist. Its claim that additionalProperties DESCENDS is WRONG: additionalProperties DESCENDS only when its value is a SCHEMA; additionalProperties:false emits exactly ONE aggregate error no matter how many extra properties (3 extras => 1 error). Same for 2020-12 items:false and draft-07 additionalItems:false.

BIGGEST MISS: $ref SIBLING KEYWORDS. In Draft4/6/7 all keywords sibling to $ref are IGNORED; in 2019-09/2020-12 they are applied. {"$ref":"#/X/a","minLength":9,"maxLength":0} where the ref target also fails => 1 error under draft-4/6/7 but 3 under 2019-09/2020-12. Same inside allOf: 1 vs 2.

anyOf SHORT-CIRCUITS on the first matching branch but oneOf NEVER does (it must scan every branch to count matches). Observable: {"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},null]} on "a" is VALID/0, but {"oneOf":[{"type":"string"},null]} on "a" CRASHES with exit=1. allOf never short-circuits either.

allOf/then/else/properties/patternProperties/items/prefixItems/propertyNames/$ref/dependentSchemas DESCEND (N child errors => N top-level errors, multiplying through chains). anyOf/oneOf/not/contains/minContains/maxContains/draft-03 disallow/draft-03 array-type COLLAPSE to exactly 1. A single COLLAPSE keyword anywhere on the path caps that whole subtree at 1 error.
propertyNames DESCENDS (not collapses) and runs per key: {"propertyNames":{"allOf":[{"maxLength":0},{"pattern":"^z"}]}} on a 2-key object => 4 errors. It is draft-06+; draft-03/04 ignore it entirely.

Empty combinator values diverge: {"allOf":[]} / {"allOf":""} / {"allOf":{}} => VALID/0, but {"anyOf":[]} / {"anyOf":""} / {"anyOf":{}} / {"oneOf":[]} / {"oneOf":{}} => INVALID with exactly 1 error. Any OTHER non-array value (non-empty string, non-empty object, 0, 1.5, null, true, false) CRASHES with exit=1 and empty stdout.
oneOf yields exactly 1 error for BOTH failure modes -- 0 matches and 2+ matches (4 branches with 3 matches => 1). Never emit one error per extra match.

then/else DESCEND: a then-branch with 3 failing keywords produces 3 TOP-LEVEL errors, not 1. And then/else WITHOUT a sibling `if` are completely ignored (0 errors); `if` alone with no then/else never errors even when it fails.
if/then/else are LAZY: {"if":{"type":"number"},"then":null} on a string is VALID/0, but {"if":{"type":"string"},"then":null} CRASHES. Only the taken branch is ever touched.

Keyword availability by draft, each silently ignored (0 errors) when absent: if/then/else draft-07+; dependencies draft-03..07 ONLY (REMOVED in 2019-09+, so {"dependencies":{"a":["b","c"]}} => 2 in draft-03..07 but 0 in 2019-09/2020-12); dependentSchemas/dependentRequired/minContains/maxContains/unevaluated* 2019-09+; contains/propertyNames/const draft-06+; prefixItems 2020-12 ONLY.
{"items":false} on [1,2] => 2 errors under Draft7Validator (descends per item) but 1 error under Draft202012Validator (one aggregate message). Same schema, different count.

STRING LENGTH IS UNICODE CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 units. U+1D11E has minLength/maxLength 1, so {"maxLength":1} PASSES where a JS `.length` implementation fails. Use [...str].length. (Combining marks still count separately: "e"+U+0301 is length 2.)

`pattern` is Python re.search, not JS RegExp: unanchored by default; `$` matches before a trailing newline so "a\n" MATCHES "^a$"; \d and \w are Unicode-aware (Arabic-Indic digits match \d); Python-only syntax (?i), \Z, (?P<name>...) all work and would throw in JS. An invalid regex like "[" CRASHES with exit=1.

Booleans are never numbers: `true` fails type integer AND type number; {"enum":[1]} rejects true, {"const":true} rejects 1, and uniqueItems treats [true,1] and [0,false] as UNIQUE. But 1 and 1.0 ARE equal for const/enum/uniqueItems ([1,1.0] fails uniqueItems; {"oneOf":[{"const":1},{"const":1.0}]} => 1 error from two matches), and -0 equals 0 ([0,-0] fails uniqueItems).

type:"integer" on 1.0 is FALSE in draft-03/draft-04 but TRUE in draft-06+ -- a real validity flip: {"oneOf":[{"type":"integer"},{"type":"number"}]} on 1.0 is VALID in draft-04 and INVALID (1 error) in draft-06+.
multipleOf uses float arithmetic: {"multipleOf":0.1} on 0.3 FAILS. Do not 'fix' it with an epsilon.

Keywords that do not apply to the instance's type are silent no-ops, quietly reducing counts. The assignment's own vector {"properties":{"x":{"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"minLength":9}]}}} with x=1 gives ONE error, not two, because minLength ignores numbers. Likewise {"allOf":[{"minLength":9},{"maxLength":0},{"pattern":"^z"}]} on 1 => 0 errors.

In 2019-09+, successful allOf/anyOf/oneOf/if-then/if-else branches DO contribute property annotations that satisfy unevaluatedProperties (making it pass), but `not` does NOT. unevaluatedProperties/unevaluatedItems emit exactly ONE aggregate error regardless of how many members are unevaluated, and are entirely ignored in draft-07 and earlier.

`not` polarity: {"not":false} is VALID/0 while {"not":true} and {"not":{}} are INVALID/1. And {"not":[]} / {"not":""} CRASH even though they look 'empty' -- unlike allOf/anyOf, `not` requires a dict or bool.

`required` emits one error PER missing property (3 missing => 3; duplicate entries count twice), unlike additionalProperties:false which aggregates. dependentRequired and draft<=7 array-form dependencies likewise emit one per missing dependency.

Crashes print NOTHING on stdout (not even the validator class name) and exit 1, because is_valid() raises before the first print. Unresolvable $ref pointers crash even when wrapped in anyOf -- anyOf swallows validation errors, not resolution errors.

Draft-03 has NONE of allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not/if/then/else/const/contains/propertyNames/prefixItems, so a pure-combinator schema is vacuously valid. Analogs: extends (DESCENDS; schema or array of schemas; {"extends":true} CRASHES), disallow (COLLAPSES to 1 and PASSES when its subschemas fail), array-valued type (COLLAPSES to 1; mixes type-name strings and subschemas), boolean `required` inside each property schema (draft-04-style {"required":[...]} is IGNORED), divisibleBy. extends is ignored in draft-04+.

validator_for strips a trailing '#' and falls back to Draft202012Validator for missing/unknown $schema and for boolean root schemas; {"$schema":7} CRASHES. Root schema `true` => True/0, root `false` => False/1.

result.findings:
ALL statements below are OBSERVED from 1099 black-box runs of /workspace/dataset/test13_executable (528 prior + 571 appended by me). Output line 1 = validator class, line 2 = True/False, line 3 = number of TOP-LEVEL errors from iter_errors. I re-ran 22 randomly sampled pre-existing lines and every one matched the recorded "out"/"exit" — the prior file is trustworthy. One prior claim was WRONG: the crash count is now 65/1099 (it was 44/528, not 40).

=== DRAFT DISPATCH ($schema) ===
"http://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema#" -> Draft3Validator; draft-04 -> Draft4Validator; draft-06 -> Draft6Validator; draft-07 -> Draft7Validator; "https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema" -> Draft201909Validator; "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema" -> Draft202012Validator. The trailing "#" is OPTIONAL and irrelevant ("http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema" -> Draft7Validator; ".../2019-09/schema#" -> Draft201909Validator). NO $schema key at all -> Draft202012Validator. An UNRECOGNIZED $schema URI ("http://example.com/unknown", "http://json-schema.org/schema#") does NOT crash and does NOT warn-out: it falls back to Draft202012Validator and validates normally. A NON-STRING $schema ("$schema":12) CRASHES (exit 1, empty stdout). A whole-schema boolean works: schema `true` on [1,2,3] -> True/0; schema `false` on [1,2,3] or on [] -> False/1. Schema `{}` -> True/0.

=== items AS A SINGLE SCHEMA (object) — identical in every draft ===
Applies to every element (in 2020-12, to every element at index >= len(prefixItems)). Each element yields its OWN top-level error, and each FAILING KEYWORD inside the subschema yields its own top-level error: items:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 3; items:{"type":"string","minimum":10} on [1,2,3] -> 6; items:{"type":"integer","minLength":5} on ["a","b"] -> 4. Descent multiplies: items:{items:{"type":"string"}} on [[1,2],[3,4]] -> 4; items:{items:{"type":"string","minimum":10}} on [[1,2],[3,4]] -> 8; items:{items:{items:{"type":"string"}}} on [[[1]],[[2]]] -> 2; items:{properties:{a,b}} on two bad objects -> 4; items:{items:{"type":"integer"},"minItems":3} on [[1,2],[3,"x"]] -> 3. Counts scale linearly: 100-element array with items:{"type":"string"} -> 100 errors; 50-element array with items:{"type":"string","minimum":1000} -> 100 errors. items:{} -> 0 in all drafts. `items` NEVER fires on a non-array instance (0 errors, all drafts). type:"array" on a non-array short-circuits nothing but items/minItems simply do not fire: {"type":"array","items":{...},"minItems":5} on {"a":1} -> exactly 1 error (the type error) in draft7 and 2020-12.

=== items AS AN ARRAY (tuple form) ===
Tuple validation works in draft3, draft4, draft6, draft7 AND 2019-09 — all five produce identical counts. Only 2020-12 dropped it. items:[str,str,str] on [1,2,3] -> 3; items:[str] on [1,2,3] -> 1 (only index 0 checked); items:[] -> True/0; a tuple LONGER than the instance only checks min(len(items),len(instance)) positions (items:[{},{},{},{}] on [1,2,3] -> 0; four failing schemas on a 3-array -> 3). Multiple failing keywords per tuple position each count: items:[{"type":"string","minimum":10},{"type":"string","minimum":10}] on [1,2] -> 4. Nested: items:[{items:{"type":"string"}},{items:{"type":"string"}}] on [[1],[2]] -> 2. Booleans inside the tuple work: items:[false,false] on [1,2] -> 2; items:[true,true] -> 0.
In 2020-12 array-form items is NOT tuple validation and NOT ignored — it CRASHES with AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' (jsonschema/_keywords.py line 78 -> validators.descend -> referencing/jsonschema.py _dollar_id), exit 1, empty stdout. The crash fires only if at least one element is actually descended into: 2020-12 items:[...] on [], on a non-array instance ("s"), or with prefixItems covering every index (prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + items:[{}] on [1,2,3]) -> True/0 with no crash; but the same schema on [1,2,3,4] -> crash. items:[] on [1,2,3] in 2020-12 -> CRASH; items:[{}]+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> CRASH; allOf:[{items:[{},{},{}]}] on [1,2,3] -> CRASH; items:[{},{},{}]+unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> CRASH.

=== items AS A BOOLEAN ===
draft3/draft4 CRASH unconditionally on items:true and items:false (TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable, _legacy_keywords.py:100), exit 1 — even for the EMPTY array []. Only a non-array instance escapes (True/0).
draft6/draft7/2019-09 treat boolean items as a schema applied to every element: items:false on [1,2,3] -> 3 (one per element), on [] -> 0; items:true -> 0.
2020-12 special-cases false as an aggregate length check: items:false on [1,2,3] -> exactly 1 error; prefixItems:[{"type":"integer"}] + items:false on [1,2,3] -> 1; prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + items:false on a 10-element array -> 1; prefixItems:[{},{},{}] (or 4 entries) + items:false on [1,2,3] -> True/0; items:false on [] -> 0; items:true -> 0. prefixItems:[{"type":"string"}] + items:false on [1,2,3] -> 2 (1 prefixItems + 1 items aggregate).
Non-boolean non-object items values (string, number) crash in any draft that reaches descent (e.g. items:"xyz"), but 2020-12 prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + items:"xyz" on [1,2,3] -> True/0 because nothing is descended.

=== prefixItems ===
Recognized ONLY by 2020-12. Completely ignored (0 errors) in draft3/4/6/7 AND 2019-09. 2020-12: prefixItems:[str,str,str] on [1,2,3] -> 3; prefixItems:[str] on [1,2,3] -> 1; prefixItems:[str,str,str,str] on [1,2] -> 2 (only min(len) positions); prefixItems:[] -> no-op; prefixItems:[true,false,true] on [1,2,3] -> 1. Multiple failing keywords in one entry each count: prefixItems:[{"type":"string","minimum":10}] on [1] -> 2. Nested prefixItems multiply: prefixItems:[{prefixItems:[str,str]},{prefixItems:[str,str]}] on [[1,2],[3,4]] -> 4. prefixItems must be a LIST: prefixItems:{} (empty object) -> True/0 by accident, prefixItems:{"a":{...}} / true / "xyz" -> CRASH. In 2020-12 `items` starts at index len(prefixItems). additionalItems alongside prefixItems is ignored in 2020-12 (prefixItems:[{"type":"string"}]+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 1, only the prefixItems error).

=== additionalItems ===
Honored in draft3, draft4, draft6, draft7, 2019-09; IGNORED entirely in 2020-12. GUARD: additionalItems does nothing unless `items` is present AND is a LIST. items absent -> inert (additionalItems:false or {"type":"string"} or "nonsense" on [1,2,3] -> True/0). items a dict/object -> inert (items:{"type":"integer"}+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> True/0). items a BOOLEAN -> CRASH TypeError: object of type 'bool' has no len() (_legacy_keywords.py:113) in draft6/draft7/2019-09 (draft3/4 crash earlier inside items); a non-array instance escapes.
VALUE SEMANTICS (this is a Python-truthiness dispatch, NOT a boolean/schema dispatch): if the value IS a JSON object -> it is used as a schema and descended into for every extra element; ELSE IF the value is FALSY (false, null, 0, 0.0, "", []) -> exactly ONE aggregate "additional items not allowed" error when extras exist; ELSE (truthy non-object: true, 1, "x", [1]) -> completely INERT, zero errors. Verified with items:[{}] on [1,2,3] in draft7 (and null re-checked in draft4 and 2019-09): null/0/[]/""/0.0/false -> 1 error each; true/1/"x"/[1] -> 0; {} -> 0 (descend into empty schema).
COUNTING: falsy additionalItems yields exactly ONE aggregate error no matter how many extras (items:[{}]+additionalItems:false on a 5-array -> 1; items:[{},{},{}]+additionalItems:false on a 10-array -> 1). Schema additionalItems yields one error PER extra element PER failing keyword (items:[{}]+additionalItems:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 2; on [1..5] -> 4; items:[{"type":"string"}]+additionalItems:{"type":"string","minimum":10} on [1,2,3] -> 5 = 1 tuple + 2 extras x 2 keywords). Tuple errors and additionalItems errors ADD: items:[int]+additionalItems:{int} on ["a","b","c"] -> 3; items:[int,int]+additionalItems:false on ["a","b","c","d"] -> 3; items:[false]+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 2; items:[str,str,str]+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 3; items:[str,str]+additionalItems:{str} on [1,2,3,4] -> 4.
EMPTY TUPLE: items:[] is still a list, so the guard passes and additionalItems applies from index 0: items:[]+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 1; items:[]+additionalItems:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 3; items:[]+additionalItems:true -> 0; items:[]+additionalItems:false on [] -> 0. (In 2020-12 items:[] on a non-empty array crashes first.)

=== contains / minContains / maxContains ===
`contains` is ignored in draft3 and draft4 (always 0 errors, even contains:false). Present in draft6, draft7, 2019-09, 2020-12, and the WHOLE group emits AT MOST 1 top-level error ever (sub-errors go into .context). contains:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 1; on [1,"a",3] -> 0; on [] -> 1; contains:{} on [] -> 1; contains:true on [] -> 1; contains:false on [1] -> 1; contains:{"type":"string","minLength":5} on [1,"a",3] -> 1 (still 1, not 2). Non-array instance ("notarray", {"a":1}) -> 0. contains:"xyz" / 123 / [] -> CRASH.
minContains/maxContains are recognized ONLY in 2019-09 and 2020-12; SILENTLY IGNORED in draft6/draft7 (which still apply plain contains with an implicit minimum of 1). Cross-draft forks: contains:{"type":"string"},minContains:0 on [1,2,3] or on [] -> False/1 in draft6/draft7, True/0 in 2019-09/2020-12. contains:{"type":"integer"},maxContains:2 on [1,2,3] -> True/0 in draft6/draft7 (maxContains unknown, contains matches), False/1 in 2019-09/2020-12. maxContains:0 with matches -> 0 in draft6/7, 1 in 2019-09/2020-12. minContains:2 + contains:{"type":"string"} with 0 matches -> 1 in draft6/draft7 too (plain contains failure).
Without `contains`, minContains/maxContains are inert in EVERY draft (minContains:0 alone, maxContains:0 alone -> 0 errors). Never more than 1 error from the group: minContains:5+maxContains:1 with 0 matches -> 1; minContains:2+maxContains:1 with 3 matches -> 1; minContains:0+maxContains:0 with 1 or 3 matches -> 1; minContains:0+maxContains:0 with 0 matches -> 0; minContains:3+maxContains:3 with 3 matches -> 0; minContains:4 with 3 matches -> 1; contains+minContains:0+maxContains:5 on [] -> 0.
NUMERIC/BOOL VALUES: floats compare numerically (minContains:2.0 ok with 3 matches; minContains:1.5 with 3 matches -> 0; maxContains:2.5 with 3 matches -> 1). Booleans are accepted as 1/0 (minContains:true with 3 matches -> 0; maxContains:false with 3 matches -> 1). Negative values are accepted (minContains:-1 -> ok; minContains:-1+maxContains:-1 with 3 matches -> 1). minContains:"x" / null and maxContains:"2" -> CRASH.

=== uniqueItems ===
Identical in EVERY draft (draft3..2020-12) and always AT MOST ONE error regardless of how many duplicate groups ([1,1,2,2,3,3] -> 1; 200-element array with one dup -> 1; 500 objects with one dup -> 1). Non-array instances (strings with repeated chars, objects with repeated values) -> 0 errors.
VALUE IS PYTHON-TRUTHINESS-TESTED, not boolean-tested. On [1,1]: true, "yes", "false", "0", 1, 0.1, [0], [[]], {"a":1} all ENFORCE uniqueness (-> 1 error); false, 0, 0.0, -0, null, "", [], {} all SKIP the check (-> 0 errors). NOTE the JS trap: empty object {} and empty array [] are FALSY here (skip), while non-empty {"a":1} / [0] and the string "0"/"false" are TRUTHY (enforce).
EQUALITY (recursive, applied at every depth):
- numbers compare by VALUE after Python parsing: 1 == 1.0 == 1e0 (dup), 100 == 1e2 == 1E2 == 100.0, 0 == -0 == -0.0, 1e16 == 10000000000000000, 1e-7 == 0.0000001, 0.1 == 0.10000000000000001 (same IEEE double). Distinct doubles stay distinct: 1.0000000000000002 vs 1.0000000000000004 unique; 3 vs 3.0000000000000004 unique.
- ARBITRARY-PRECISION INTEGERS: Python ints are exact, so 9007199254740993 vs 9007199254740992 are UNIQUE, and 123456789012345678901234567890 vs ...891 are UNIQUE. (A JS implementation using Number would wrongly call these duplicates.) Identical big ints are still dups.
- Overflow: 1e400 parses to inf, so [1e400,1e400] AND [1e400,1e401] are both DUPS (inf == inf).
- BOOLEANS ARE NEVER EQUAL TO NUMBERS at any depth: [1,true], [0,false], [true,1.0], [false,0.0], [false,-0.0], [{"a":false},{"a":0}], [[false],[0]], [[[false]],[[0.0]]], [{"a":[true]},{"a":[1]}], [{"a":[true]},{"a":[1.0]}], [[{"x":true}],[{"x":1}]] are all UNIQUE. [true,true] and [false,false] are dups; [true,false] is unique.
- objects: key ORDER irrelevant ({"a":1,"b":2} == {"b":2,"a":1}); values compared with the same numeric rules ({"a":1} == {"a":1.0}, {"a":1,"b":2} == {"a":1.0,"b":2.0}, {"a":-0} == {"a":0.0}); nested arrays/objects recurse ([1,[2.0]] == [1.0,[2]], {"a":[1,{"b":2}]} dup, {"a":{}} dup).
- cross-type non-equalities: [] vs {}, "" vs 0, null vs false, null vs 0, 1 vs "1", [1] vs ["1"] are all UNIQUE. [null,null], [[null],[null]], [{"a":null},{"a":null}], [[],[]], [{},{}], [[[]],[[]]], ["a","a"], [[1],[1]], [[[1],"a"],[[1],"a"]] are DUPS.
- strings compare by exact code-point sequence with NO Unicode normalization: "é" (NFC) vs "é" (NFD) are UNIQUE; two identical astral strings "😀" are dups.

=== minItems / maxItems ===
Identical in all drafts, one error each, and they ADD (unlike the contains group): {"minItems":5,"maxItems":1} on [1,2,3] -> 2. minItems:3 on [1] -> 1; maxItems:1 on [1,2,3] -> 1; maxItems:0 on [1] -> 1; maxItems:-1 on [1,2,3] -> 1; minItems:0 -> 0; minItems:-1 -> 0; minItems:1e308 on [1,2,3] -> 1. Floats compare numerically: minItems:2.5 on [1,2,3] -> 0, maxItems:2.5 on [1,2,3] -> 1, maxItems:2.999999999999999 on [1,2,3] -> 1, minItems:3.0 on [1,2,3] -> 0. BOOLEANS are accepted as ints: minItems:true == minItems:1 (on [] -> 1 error, on [1] -> 0), maxItems:false == maxItems:0 (on [1] -> 1 error), maxItems:true on [1,2] -> 1, {"minItems":true,"maxItems":true} on [1,2,3] -> 1. Non-array instance -> 0. Non-numeric values CRASH: minItems:"3", minItems:[], minItems:{}, maxItems:null -> TypeError, exit 1.

=== unevaluatedItems ===
Recognized ONLY in 2019-09 and 2020-12; completely ignored (0 errors) in draft3/4/6/7 — even alongside items:true, where draft6/draft7 give True/0. It yields AT MOST ONE top-level error, ever, regardless of how many items are unevaluated or how many keywords in its subschema fail: unevaluatedItems:false on a 10-element array -> 1; unevaluatedItems:{"minLength":5} on ["a","b","c"] -> 1; unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer","minLength":5} on ["a","b","c"] -> 1; unevaluatedItems:{"type":"string","minLength":9} on a 10-element int array -> 1. It is NOT a bare "no unevaluated items allowed" check — the subschema IS applied and the error only appears if some unevaluated item FAILS it: unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer"} on [1,2,3] -> True/0, on [1,"a"] -> 1, on ["a","b"] -> 1; unevaluatedItems:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 1 (both 2019-09 and 2020-12). unevaluatedItems:true / {} -> 0; on [] -> 0; on a non-array instance -> 0. Non-schema values CRASH: "xyz", 0, [] -> exit 1.
EVALUATION TRACKING is computed from the SAME schema object only (an unevaluatedItems inside an allOf branch cannot see the parent's sibling prefixItems: {"allOf":[{"unevaluatedItems":false}],"prefixItems":[{},{},{}]} -> False/1). Contributors:
- `items` as a SCHEMA marks ALL indexes evaluated even when items itself produced errors: items:{"type":"string"}+unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 3 (not 4); items:{"type":"string"}+unevaluatedItems:{"type":"string"} -> 3; items:{}+unevaluatedItems:false -> 0.
- 2020-12 `items:false` also marks everything evaluated: items:false+unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 1, items:false+unevaluatedItems:{"type":"string"} -> 1 (the items error only). 2020-12 items:true+unevaluatedItems:{"type":"string"} -> 0.
- 2019-09 `items` in TUPLE form marks indexes 0..len(items)-1: items:[{},{},{}] -> 0 errors; items:[{},{},{},{}] on [1,2,3] -> 0; items:[{},{}] leaves index 2 -> 1; items:[] leaves everything -> 1.
- 2019-09 `additionalItems` — merely BEING PRESENT (alongside a tuple `items`) marks all remaining indexes evaluated, whatever its value: items:[{},{}]+additionalItems:true+unevaluatedItems:false -> 0; +additionalItems:"x" -> 0; +additionalItems:{} -> 0; +additionalItems:{"type":"string"} -> 1 total (the additionalItems validation error, not an unevaluatedItems error); +additionalItems:false -> 1 total (the additionalItems aggregate). additionalItems WITHOUT items contributes nothing: additionalItems:{}+unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 1.
- **2019-09 CRASHES when a boolean `items` is reachable while unevaluatedItems is present** (the index-tracking walker does len() on a bool): {"items":true,"unevaluatedItems":false} on [1,2,3] -> exit 1; also with unevaluatedItems:true or {}; also on the EMPTY array []; also when the boolean items sits inside allOf ({"allOf":[{"items":true}],...}) or behind a $ref ({"$defs":{"x":{"items":true}},"$ref":"#/$defs/x","unevaluatedItems":false}). Only a non-array instance escapes (True/0). 2020-12 does NOT have this bug: {"allOf":[{"items":true}],"unevaluatedItems":false} -> True/0.
- `prefixItems` marks indexes under 2020-12 ONLY: prefixItems:[{},{},{}]+unevaluatedItems:false -> True/0 in 2020-12 but False/1 in 2019-09 (prefixItems unknown there). prefixItems:[{},{}] on [1,2,3] leaves index 2 -> 1. prefixItems:[{},{},{}]+unevaluatedItems:{"type":"string"} -> 0. prefixItems:[{}]+items:{}+unevaluatedItems:false -> 0. 2020-12 additionalItems contributes nothing (prefixItems:[{},{}]+additionalItems:{}+unevaluatedItems:false -> 1).
- `contains` marks ONLY the MATCHING indexes: contains:{"type":"integer"} on [1,2,3]+unevaluatedItems:false -> 0; on [1,"a",3] index 1 stays unevaluated -> with unevaluatedItems:false -> 1, with unevaluatedItems:{"type":"string"} -> 0, with unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer"} -> 1. Matching indexes are marked even when the contains GROUP fails on count: contains:{"type":"integer"},maxContains:1 on [1,2,3]+unevaluatedItems:false -> 1 (the maxContains error only). contains that matches nothing marks nothing: contains:{"type":"string"}+unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 2 (1 contains + 1 unevaluated); with minContains:0 added -> 1 (contains now passes, still nothing evaluated). prefixItems:[{},{}]+contains:{"const":3}+unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 0.
- It recurses into allOf/anyOf/oneOf/if/then/else/$ref, but ONLY THROUGH SUBSCHEMAS THAT ARE VALID for the instance. A FAILING branch contributes NO annotations: allOf:[{prefixItems:[{},{},{}],"minItems":10}]+unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 2 (minItems error + unevaluated error); allOf:[{prefixItems:[{"type":"string"},{},{}]}]+unevaluatedItems:false -> 2. Valid branches do contribute: allOf:[{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]}] -> 0; allOf:[{prefixItems:[{},{}]}] -> 1; allOf:[{items:{"type":"integer"}}] -> 0; allOf:[{contains:{"type":"integer"}}] on [1,"a"] -> 1, allOf:[{contains:{int}},{contains:{str}}] on [1,"a"] -> 0, allOf:[{contains:{"type":"boolean"}}] on [1,"a"] -> 2. anyOf:[{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]},{"minItems":99}] -> 0; anyOf:[{prefixItems:[{},{},{}],"minItems":10},{"minItems":1}] -> 1 (failing branch's annotations dropped); anyOf:[{"minItems":99}] -> 2 (anyOf + unevaluated). oneOf with BOTH branches matching -> 1 total (the oneOf error; annotations still collected so unevaluatedItems is satisfied); oneOf:[{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]},{"minItems":99}] -> 0. A passing `if` contributes even with no `then`: if:{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]}+unevaluatedItems:false -> 0; if:{"minItems":99} (fails, no else) -> 1; if matches + then:{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]} -> 0; if fails + then:{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]} -> 1; if fails + else:{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]} -> 0; if matches + then:{"minItems":99} -> 2 (then error + unevaluated). $ref works in both drafts: {"$defs":{"x":{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]}},"$ref":"#/$defs/x","unevaluatedItems":false} -> 0 (2020-12); {"definitions":{"x":{items:[{},{},{}]}},"$ref":"#/definitions/x","unevaluatedItems":false} -> 0 (2019-09); $ref to prefixItems:[{},{}] -> 1.
- `not` does NOT contribute evaluated indexes: not:{"minItems":99}+unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 1.
- unevaluatedItems nested inside prefixItems entries works normally: prefixItems:[{prefixItems:[{}],"unevaluatedItems":false}] on [[1,2]] -> 1; prefixItems:[{prefixItems:[{},{}],"unevaluatedItems":false}] -> 0.
- unevaluatedItems errors ADD to sibling errors: prefixItems:[{"type":"string"}]+unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 2; unevaluatedItems:false+minItems:5 (2019-09) -> 2; unevaluatedItems:false+minItems:5+maxItems:1+uniqueItems:true on [1,2,3] -> 3; unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer"}+minItems:9 on [1,2,3] -> 1 (only minItems); 2019-09 contains:{int}+minItems:9+unevaluatedItems:false on [1,"a",3] -> 2. unevaluatedProperties alongside is inert on arrays (unevaluatedItems:false+unevaluatedProperties:false on [1,2,3] -> 1).

=== STRING SUB-KEYWORDS REACHED THROUGH items (Python semantics a JS port will get wrong) ===
maxLength/minLength count Unicode CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 units: ["😀"] (one astral emoji) passes items:{"maxLength":1} and FAILS items:{"minLength":2}; ["😀😀"] passes maxLength:2. Decomposed sequences count their parts: ["é"] passes maxLength:1 but ["é"] FAILS maxLength:1.
`pattern` is Python `re.search` (substring match, not anchored): pattern:"b" matches "abc". Python-only regex behaviour observed: "$" matches BEFORE a trailing newline, so pattern:"^a$" MATCHES "a\n" (True/0) — JS would reject it; "^" is NOT multiline, so pattern:"^b" does NOT match "a\nb"; "\Z" is supported (pattern:"a\\Z" matches "a", "^ab\\Z" matches "ab") — JS treats \Z as literal "Z"; inline flags work (pattern:"(?i)ABC" matches "abc", "(?i)abc" matches "ABC", "(?s)a.b" behaves as a normal dot and does NOT match "ab"); "." matches a whole astral code point (pattern:"^.$" matches "😀") whereas JS without /u would need two units; "\d" is UNICODE-aware and matches Arabic-Indic "٠" (JS \d is ASCII-only); "\w" matches "é"; POSIX classes are NOT supported ("[[:alpha:]]" does not match "x").
`type` distinguishes bool from number in every draft: items:{"type":"integer"} on [true] -> 1 error, on [true,false] -> 2; items:{"type":"number"} on [true] -> 1; items:{"type":"boolean"} on [1] -> 1; items:{"type":"integer"} on [1] -> 0 and on [1.5] -> 1.

=== COMBINED COUNTS ===
items 3-fail + minItems + maxItems + uniqueItems(unique) -> 5; items 3-fail + uniqueItems(dup) -> 4; items:{"type":"string"}+contains:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 4; type:"array"+items:{"type":"string"}+minItems:5 on [1,2,3] -> 4; uniqueItems+contains+minItems:5+maxItems:2+items:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 6 (identical in draft7 and 2020-12); contains-fail+minItems:5+uniqueItems(unique) on [1,2,3] -> 2; contains-fail+uniqueItems(dup)+minItems:5+maxItems:2 on [1,1,1] -> 4.

=== CRASH BEHAVIOUR ===
Every crash prints NOTHING on stdout, prints a Python traceback plus "[PYI-NNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13' due to unhandled exception!" on stderr, and exits 1. 65 of the 1099 vectors crash. Crash triggers seen: non-string $schema; draft3/4 boolean items on an array; boolean items + additionalItems in draft6/7/2019-09; boolean items + unevaluatedItems in 2019-09 (incl. via allOf/$ref, incl. on []); 2020-12 array-form items that actually descends; non-list prefixItems (non-empty object, true, string); non-schema contains (string, number, array); non-numeric minContains/maxContains; non-numeric minItems/maxItems (string, null, array, object); non-schema unevaluatedItems (string, number, array); non-schema items values that get descended into.
gotchas: NEW: 2019-09 CRASHES (exit 1) whenever `unevaluatedItems` is present and a boolean `items` is reachable in the same schema object — {"items":true,"unevaluatedItems":false} on [1,2,3] OR on [] both crash, and so do {"allOf":[{"items":true}],"unevaluatedItems":false} and a $ref to {"items":true}. 2020-12 does NOT crash on the same shapes. Only a non-array instance escapes.

NEW: `additionalItems` is dispatched by Python TRUTHINESS, not by boolean-vs-schema. Object -> used as a schema; FALSY non-object (false, null, 0, 0.0, "", []) -> one aggregate error; TRUTHY non-object (true, 1, "x", [1]) -> completely INERT (zero errors). A JS port that does `typeof v === 'boolean' ? ... : descend` gets 4 of these wrong.

NEW: in 2019-09, merely HAVING an `additionalItems` key next to a tuple `items` marks every remaining index evaluated for unevaluatedItems purposes, regardless of the additionalItems value — even additionalItems:"x" or true. additionalItems WITHOUT items contributes nothing.

NEW: unevaluatedItems only collects annotations from allOf/anyOf/oneOf/if branches that are VALID for the instance. A failing allOf branch carrying prefixItems does NOT mark anything evaluated: allOf:[{prefixItems:[{},{},{}],minItems:10}] + unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 2 errors, not 1.

NEW: `uniqueItems` deep-equality uses Python arbitrary-precision integers, so 9007199254740993 vs 9007199254740992 are UNIQUE and 123456789012345678901234567890 vs ...891 are UNIQUE. A JS Number-based comparison calls both pairs duplicates. Meanwhile 1e400 vs 1e401 ARE duplicates (both parse to inf).
NEW: `uniqueItems` truthiness traps for JS: {} and [] are FALSY (uniqueness NOT enforced), while {"a":1}, [0], [[]], "0", "false", 0.1 are TRUTHY (enforced). In JS {} and [] are truthy.
NEW: minItems/maxItems/minContains/maxContains accept BOOLEANS as 1/0 (minItems:true behaves as 1, maxItems:false as 0, maxContains:false as 0), but crash on strings/null/arrays/objects.

NEW: no $schema at all -> Draft202012Validator, and an UNRECOGNIZED $schema URI also silently falls back to Draft202012Validator (no crash). A non-string $schema (e.g. 12) CRASHES. The trailing '#' on any known URI is optional.

NEW: items:[] is still a LIST, so in draft3-2019-09 additionalItems applies from index 0 (items:[]+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 1; +{"type":"string"} -> 3), while in 2020-12 items:[] on a non-empty array CRASHES.

NEW: string keywords under items use Python semantics — maxLength counts CODE POINTS ("😀" has length 1, NFD "é" has length 2) and `pattern` is re.search where `$` matches before a trailing newline ("^a$" MATCHES "a\n"), `\Z` and inline `(?i)`/`(?s)` flags work, `\d`/`\w` are Unicode-aware, `.` spans an astral code point, and POSIX classes like [[:alpha:]] do NOT work.
NEW: prior report said 40 of 528 vectors crash; the true figure in the original file was 44, and it is 65 of 1099 now.

2020-12 with array-form `items` does NOT ignore it and does NOT do tuple validation — it CRASHES (AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'). But only if at least one element is actually descended into: items:[...] on [], on a non-array instance, or fully covered by prefixItems yields True/0.
2019-09 STILL supports tuple-form `items` + `additionalItems` (identical counts to draft7). Only 2020-12 dropped them.
draft3 and draft4 CRASH on boolean `items` (true OR false) even when the instance is the EMPTY array []. Only a non-array instance avoids the crash.
`additionalItems` CRASHES (object of type 'bool' has no len()) in draft6, draft7 and 2019-09 whenever `items` is a boolean; it is silently inert when items is absent or is an object.

2020-12 `items:false` yields exactly ONE aggregate error, whereas draft6/7/2019-09 `items:false` yields ONE ERROR PER ELEMENT. 2020-12 items:false also marks every index evaluated for unevaluatedItems.
`prefixItems` is ignored in 2019-09 as well as in draft3-7, so prefixItems + unevaluatedItems:false diverges completely between 2019-09 (1 error) and 2020-12 (0).
`unevaluatedItems` NEVER produces more than 1 top-level error, and it DOES apply its subschema (unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer"} on [1,2,3] is VALID).
`items` as a schema marks all indexes evaluated EVEN WHEN items itself fails — items:{"type":"string"} + unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] gives 3, not 4.
`contains` marks only MATCHING indexes evaluated — and it still marks them when the contains group fails on maxContains (contains:{int},maxContains:1,unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 1).

minContains:0 is a real draft fork: VALID in 2019-09/2020-12 with 0 matches, INVALID (1 error) in draft6/draft7. maxContains is likewise ignored in draft6/7 (maxContains:0 with matches -> 0 errors there, 1 error in 2019-09/2020-12).
The whole contains/minContains/maxContains group emits AT MOST 1 top-level error; minItems and maxItems DO both fire (2 errors) when both are violated.

Error counts multiply per element AND per failing keyword inside a subschema (items:{"type":"string","minimum":10} on [1,2,3] -> 6; 50 elements x 2 keywords -> 100), except for the aggregate-style keywords (uniqueItems, contains-group, unevaluatedItems, falsy additionalItems, 2020-12 items:false) which are capped at 1.
