PROGRAM UNDER TEST: /workspace/dataset/test13_executable --a '<instance json>' --b '<schema json>'. It does validator_for(schema) -> cls(schema); prints cls.__name__, is_valid(instance), len(list(iter_errors(instance))). On any exception ALL THREE lines are lost (stdout EMPTY), exit code 1, traceback on stderr plus a PyInstaller "[PYI-NNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13'..." line. Vectors: /workspace/probes/refs.jsonl, 963 lines, {"a","b","out","exit"}; out is stdout only. 648 exit-0, 315 exit-1. 34 duplicate (a,b) pairs (harmless overlap between generators; all consistent). 21 lines re-run by the critic matched exactly — the file is machine-captured, not hand-written. Generators: gen_refs.js, gen_refs_crit.js, gen_refs_crit2.js, gen_refs_crit3.js, gen_refs_crit4.js, gen_refs_crit5.js in /workspace/probes.

=== 1. BASIC POINTER REFS ===
"#/definitions/x" and "#/$defs/x" both resolve as PLAIN JSON POINTERS in EVERY draft (3,4,6,7,2019-09,2020-12). The pointer walk is purely structural and draft-agnostic: it does not care whether the containing key is a known keyword. {"$schema":draft-07,"$ref":"#/$defs/a","$defs":{"a":{"type":"integer"}}} works; so does the same under draft-03. A failing target contributes exactly the errors the target schema itself produces, as TOP-LEVEL errors, no wrapping: $ref -> {"minLength":10,"pattern":"^z"} on "x" = 2 errors in all drafts. Chained refs add nothing: a->b->c with only c failing = 1 error (verified 3-chain and 60-link and 400-link chains: long chains are fine, no recursion limit hit). Two properties both ref-ing the same failing def = 2. allOf:[{$ref: 3-failure target}] = 3. Two allOf branches both ref-ing a 2-failure target = 4. anyOf/oneOf/not wrapping a ref = 1 top-level error (sub-errors go to .context). Empty-object target {} => True/0.

=== 2. $ref SIBLING KEYWORDS (headline cross-draft difference) ===
draft-03/04/06/07: when "$ref" is present in a schema object, ALL other keys of that object are IGNORED — validation keywords, applicators, AND the identifier ($id/id). {"$ref":"#/definitions/a","minLength":10,"definitions":{"a":{"type":"string"}}} on "x" => True/0 in draft3/4/6/7. {"$ref":X,"minLength":10,"pattern":"^z"} on a bad string => 1 error in d3/4/6/7. {"$ref":X,"$defs":{...},"maxLength":0,"type":"integer"} where X yields 2 errors => d7: 2 errors ($ref target's 2 only). {"$ref":X,"required":["q","r"]} on {} => d7: 1.
2019-09/2020-12: siblings ARE applied, $ref is just one more keyword, and each contributes its own top-level errors. Same cases: 1st => False/1; {$ref,minLength,pattern} => 3; +maxLength => 4; the 2-error-target + maxLength + type case => 4 (2 from target + 2 siblings); {$ref, required:["q","r"]} on {} => 3 (required emits ONE error PER missing property, plus the ref error). {"anyOf":[{"type":"integer"}],"$ref":"#/anyOf/0"} on "x" => 1 in d3-7, 2 in 2019/2020. Nested (non-root) refs behave identically: {"properties":{"p":{"$ref":X,"minLength":10,"pattern":"^z"}}} on {"p":"x"} => 3 in 2020-12. Pure-annotation siblings ($comment/title/default/examples/deprecated) add 0 errors in 2019/2020.
KEYWORD EVALUATION ORDER in 2019/2020 follows the schema object's JSON key insertion order, and this is observable: {"$ref":"#/not/0","not":[{...}]} in 2020-12 crashes with AttributeError 'list' object has no attribute 'get' (the $ref runs first), while {"not":[{...}],"$ref":"#/not/0"} crashes with AttributeError 'list' object has no attribute 'items' (the not keyword runs first and is handed the raw list). Error COUNTS are order-independent, only crash identity changes.

=== 3. ROOT/SELF RECURSION ===
{"$ref":"#"} and {"$ref":""} at the TOP LEVEL are unguarded infinite loops => RecursionError, exit 1, in EVERY draft. So are: {"$ref":"#/$defs/a","$defs":{"a":{"$ref":"#"}}}; {"$ref":"#/$defs/a","$defs":{"a":{"$ref":"#/$defs/a"}}}; mutual a<->b ({"$ref":"#/$defs/a","$defs":{"a":{"$ref":"#/$defs/b"},"b":{"$ref":"#/$defs/a"}}}); {"$id":"http://x/root","allOf":[{"$ref":"http://x/root"}],"type":"integer"} in d6/7/2019/2020 (draft-03 gives False/1 there because allOf is unknown to d3); {"$anchor":"root","type":"integer","allOf":[{"$ref":"#root"}]} in 2020-12; {"$dynamicAnchor":"n","$dynamicRef":"#n"} in 2020-12; {"$recursiveAnchor":true,"$recursiveRef":"#"} in 2019-09.
Recursion guarded by instance structure terminates: {"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"$ref":"#"}}} on {"a":{"a":1}} => 1 error, on {"a":{"a":{"a":1}}} => 1 error. There IS a Python recursion ceiling on instance depth when a $ref is in the loop: nesting depth 50/120/150/180/200/220/240 => False/1, depth 260 and 300 => RecursionError. The same depths with a ref-free nested schema do NOT blow up at 240. So budget roughly ~250 nested $ref applications.
Self-ref by absolute $id + pointer ($id:"http://x/root", $ref:"http://x/root#/$defs/a") works in draft-06+; draft-04 fails (uses "id"); draft-03 returns True/0 when the ref sits under allOf (allOf unknown to d3).

=== 4. JSON-POINTER FRAGMENT DECODING (order NOW PROVEN) ===
Order is: percent-decode the WHOLE fragment (UTF-8, single pass) FIRST, then split on "/", then undo ~1/~0 escapes. Evidence: {"$defs":{"~1":...}} + $ref "#/$defs/%7E1" => PointerToNowhere, but {"$defs":{"/":...}} + the same ref RESOLVES (so %7E -> ~, then ~1 -> "/"). {"$defs":{"a/b":...}} + "#/$defs/a%2Fb" => PointerToNowhere, but {"$defs":{"a":{"b":...}}} + "#/$defs/a%2Fb" RESOLVES — i.e. %2F (and lowercase %2f) becomes a real PATH SEPARATOR. Only ONE decode pass: "#/$defs/a%2520b" does NOT find key "a b" (it looks for "a%20b"), and "#/$defs/a%252Fb" finds key "a%2Fb". Confirmed resolving: ~1 -> "/", ~0 -> "~", ~01 -> "~1", ~0~1 -> "~/", %20 -> space, a LITERAL space, a LITERAL tab, %0A -> newline, %C3%A9 -> "é", the literal "é", %F0%9F%98%80 -> "😀" and the literal astral "😀", %25 -> "%", %23 -> "#", literal '"' and '?' and even a literal second '#' inside the key, %24 -> "$", %61 -> "a", "a+b" stays "a+b" (NO plus-to-space). An INVALID escape is left literal: "a%b" finds key "a%b". Pointer matching is byte/char exact and CASE-SENSITIVE ("#/$defs/a" does not find key "A"; "#/$DEFS/a" fails). No trimming: $ref "  #/$defs/a  " looks for key "a  " and fails; "#/$defs/a " finds key "a " if present. "#/$defs/" and "#/$defs/a/" address the empty-string key. "#/$defs/a#" and "#//$defs/a" are PointerToNowhere.
ARRAY INDEX SEGMENTS use Python int(): "#/anyOf/0" fine; "#/anyOf/00" RESOLVES (leading zeros OK); "#/anyOf/-1" RESOLVES (Python negative indexing — last element!); "#/anyOf/1" on a 1-element list => PointerToNowhere; "#/anyOf/-" => raw, UNWRAPPED ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '-'. A numeric segment against an OBJECT looks up the string key: {"$defs":{"a":{"0":{...}}}} + "#/$defs/a/0" resolves.
PLAIN-NAME (anchor) FRAGMENTS ARE **NOT** PERCENT-DECODED: {"$anchor":"a b"} + $ref "#a b" resolves (root -> RecursionError proves resolution), but $ref "#a%20b" => NoSuchAnchor: 'a%20b'.

=== 5. $id / id BASE URI ===
Identifier keyword per draft: draft-03/04 use "id"; draft-06/07/2019-09/2020-12 use "$id". The wrong spelling is completely inert ($id in draft-04 => Unresolvable; id in draft-07 => inert). If BOTH are present the draft's own spelling wins and the other is inert.
SIBLING-$ref SUPPRESSION OF THE IDENTIFIER (draft-03/04/06/07 ONLY): a schema object's id/$id is dropped when "$ref" is a sibling. Consequence for a ROOT of the form {"$id":"http://x/","definitions":{"a":{"$id":"b",...}},"$ref":...}: the base stays "", the subresource registers as bare "b", so $ref:"http://x/b" is Unresolvable (exit 1) while $ref:"b" RESOLVES. Verified for d3(id), d4(id), d6($id), d7($id). Move the $ref off the root (into properties or allOf) and the root id is honored again: both "b" and "http://x/b" resolve. 2019-09/2020-12 never have this quirk — root $id is always honored, both forms resolve. ANCHORS survive the suppression: {"$schema":d7,"$id":"http://x/","definitions":{"a":{"$id":"#foo",...}},"$ref":"#foo"} still resolves (anchor registered against the empty base).
$id VALUE TYPE: a non-string $id crashes the crawl with AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'rstrip'.
$id URI RESOLUTION is plain RFC3986 with NO case normalization: $id "HTTP://X/" does NOT match $ref "http://x/#/$defs/a" (Unresolvable). Relative $ids resolve normally: base "http://x/a/c.json" + sub $id "e.json" => http://x/a/e.json; "/e.json" => http://x/e.json; "../c" against "http://x/a/b" => http://x/c; "./c" => http://x/a/c; base "http://x/a/" + sub $id "sub/" => http://x/a/sub/ (and "sub/#/$defs/t" resolves). Query strings work ($id "http://x/?q=1" + $ref "http://x/?q=1#/$defs/a"). URNs work: $id "urn:example:root" + $ref "urn:example:root#/$defs/a"; sub $id "urn:example:a" + $ref "urn:example:a"; even a RELATIVE sub $id "sub" against a urn base resolves via $ref "sub". Duplicate $id registrations do not error (last/first wins silently — one of them resolves, 1 error). $id "" and $id "http://x/#" are accepted with no ill effect. A nested $id creates a new base: inner "#/$defs/b" resolves WITHIN the inner resource (and PointerToNowhere if the target only exists in the outer one), while "http://y/#/$defs/b" reaches it from outside and "http://x/#/$defs/b" from inside reaches back out.

=== 6. WHICH CONTAINERS ARE CRAWLED FOR $id/$anchor (full matrix, measured) ===
Crawling is per-draft and only covers slots that draft knows. Using {<container>:{a:{$id:"http://y/b","type":"integer"}}, allOf/properties:[{$ref:"http://y/b"}]}:
- draft-03 (key "id"): CRAWLS definitions, properties, patternProperties, dependencies, additionalProperties, items(single), items(array). DOES NOT crawl $defs or unknown keywords (=> Unresolvable). "extends" is treated as an ARRAY-of-schemas slot: an object-valued extends makes any crawl crash (see §9).
- draft-04: CRAWLS definitions, properties, patternProperties, items(single), items(array), anyOf, not, additionalProperties. NOT $defs, NOT prefixItems, NOT dependentSchemas, NOT contains, NOT then, NOT unknown keywords.
- draft-06: as draft-04 PLUS contains. Still NOT $defs / prefixItems / dependentSchemas / then / unknown.
- draft-07: as draft-06 PLUS then (if/then/else). Still NOT $defs / prefixItems / dependentSchemas / unknown.
- 2019-09: CRAWLS $defs AND definitions, properties, patternProperties, items(single), items(array), anyOf, not, additionalProperties, dependentSchemas, contains, then. NOT prefixItems, NOT unknown keywords.
- 2020-12: CRAWLS $defs AND definitions, properties, patternProperties, items(single), prefixItems, anyOf, not, additionalProperties, dependentSchemas, contains, then. NOT unknown keywords. items-as-ARRAY is a hard crash (§9).
Hence {"$schema":d7,"$defs":{"a":{"$id":"http://y/b",...}},"$ref":"http://y/b"} => Unresolvable, while the same with "definitions" resolves; both resolve under 2019-09/2020-12. Plain JSON-pointer refs like "#/$defs/a" still work in every draft regardless.
WHEN THE CRAWL RUNS: a same-document JSON-pointer fragment ("#", "#/...") does NOT trigger a whole-document id/anchor crawl. Any URI lookup or plain-name anchor lookup DOES force a full crawl of the root resource — which is why merely HAVING a badly-shaped slot is harmless until you use a non-pointer $ref (see §9).

=== 7. ANCHORS / PLAIN-NAME FRAGMENTS ===
Anchor spelling per draft: draft-03/04 => id:"#foo"; draft-06/07 => $id:"#foo"; 2019-09/2020-12 => $anchor:"foo" (an $id:"#foo" in 2019/2020 is NOT an anchor => NoSuchAnchor). Wrong flavor => _WrappedReferencingError: NoSuchAnchor: 'foo' does not exist within {<repr of the whole root schema>}, exit 1. Anchor names are CASE-SENSITIVE ($id:"#FOO" is not found by "#foo"). Anchor names are NOT VALIDATED: "$anchor":"1bad", "a-b", "a.b", "a/b", "a b", "" all register and resolve (each of those probes hit RecursionError precisely because the ref resolved back to the root). A NON-STRING $anchor (e.g. 5) does not register => NoSuchAnchor: '5'. Anchors are scoped to their containing resource: {"$defs":{"a":{"$id":"b","$anchor":"c",...}},"allOf":[{"$ref":"#c"}]} => NoSuchAnchor, while $ref:"b#c" resolves. http://x/#foo works with root $id:"http://x/". Anchor discovery obeys the §6 crawl matrix exactly (draft-07 does not crawl $defs, so a $defs-nested $id:"#foo" is NoSuchAnchor in draft-07 but $anchor in $defs works in 2019-09/2020-12; $anchor in "definitions" also works in 2019-09). In 2020-12 declaring both $anchor and $dynamicAnchor with the same name is fine.

=== 8. $recursiveRef/$recursiveAnchor (2019-09 only) and $dynamicRef/$dynamicAnchor (2020-12 only) ===
$recursiveRef/$recursiveAnchor are keywords ONLY in 2019-09; in draft-07 and 2020-12 they are unknown and silently ignored. {"$recursiveAnchor":true,"type":"object","properties":{"p":{"$recursiveRef":"#"}}} on {"p":1} => draft-07 True/0, 2020-12 True/0, 2019-09 False/1. $recursiveAnchor:false behaves like true for the simple root case, and OMITTING $recursiveAnchor entirely still gives False/1 — jsonschema falls back to the base resource root. In 2019-09 the $recursiveRef FRAGMENT IS IGNORED: "$recursiveRef":"#/$defs/a" and "$recursiveRef":"#nope" both behave like "#" (both => RecursionError at root, they do not do pointer/anchor lookup). REAL DYNAMIC SCOPE IS IMPLEMENTED: the classic strict-tree test ({"$id":"http://y/strict","$recursiveAnchor":true,"$ref":"http://y/tree","unevaluatedProperties":false,...} where tree recurses via $recursiveRef "#") CATCHES a typo'd child property (False/1).
$dynamicRef/$dynamicAnchor are keywords ONLY in 2020-12; ignored in draft-07 and 2019-09. {"$dynamicAnchor":"n","type":"object","properties":{"p":{"$dynamicRef":"#n"}}} on {"p":1} => d7 True/0, 2019 True/0, 2020-12 False/1. Real dynamic scope: the 2020-12 strict-tree (http://x/strict with $dynamicAnchor "node" + $ref to http://x/tree + unevaluatedProperties:false) gives False/1 on {"children":[{"daat":1}]} and True/0 on {"children":[{"data":1}]}, while the plain tree without the strict wrapper gives True/0. A $dynamicAnchor ALSO registers as a plain anchor ($ref:"#n" finds it), and $dynamicRef will bind to a plain $anchor (including one inside $defs). $dynamicRef accepts an absolute form "http://x/r#n". $dynamicRef with a JSON-POINTER fragment works as an ordinary pointer ("#/$defs/a" resolves; "#/$defs/nope" => PointerToNowhere). $dynamicRef WITHOUT a leading '#' ("n", "nope") => Unresolvable. Bare {"$dynamicRef":"#nope"} at root => NoSuchAnchor in 2020-12, True/0 in d7/2019.

=== 9. LIST/OBJECT SHAPE MISMATCHES IN SCHEMA SLOTS => AttributeError CRASHES ===
Two distinct triggers, same exception text: AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' (raised in referencing/jsonschema.py _dollar_id while computing a sub-resource id).
(a) A JSON POINTER that WALKS THROUGH a slot the draft treats as a SINGLE schema while that slot holds an array.
(b) A URI or ANCHOR lookup anywhere in the document, which forces a full crawl and hits the bad slot even if the pointer never touches it. Verified: {"$schema":2020-12,"items":[{...}],"allOf":[{"$ref":"http://nope/"}]} and the same with "#anchornope" both crash, whereas the identical schema with a plain pointer ref does not crash unless the pointer walks items. And {"$defs":{"a":[{...}]},"type":"integer"} with no ref at all is completely fine.
MEASURED CRASH MATRIX for $ref "#/<slot>/.../0" (all 6 drafts probed):
- "#/definitions/a/0": CRASHES in ALL SIX drafts (definitions is a crawled schema-map everywhere, including draft-03/04).
- "#/properties/p/0": CRASHES in all six.
- "#/patternProperties/^p/0": CRASHES in all six.
- "#/additionalProperties/0": CRASHES in all six.
- "#/$defs/a/0": WORKS in draft-03/04/06/07 ($defs unknown => no id() call), CRASHES in 2019-09/2020-12.
- "#/items/0": WORKS in draft-03/04/06/07 and 2019-09 (array-of-schemas slot), CRASHES in 2020-12 (single-schema slot). Nested "#/$defs/a/items/0" likewise only crashes in 2020-12.
- "#/contains/0": WORKS in draft-03/04 (contains unknown), CRASHES in draft-06/07/2019/2020.
- "#/not/0": WORKS in draft-03 (not unknown), CRASHES 'get' in draft-04/06/07 and in 2019/2020 when $ref precedes the not key; in 2019/2020 with the not key FIRST you instead get AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'items' (the not keyword itself receives the list).
- "#/prefixItems/0": WORKS in all six (unknown pre-2020; array-of-schemas in 2020-12).
- "#/anyOf/0", "#/allOf/0": always work (array-of-schemas everywhere they exist). Note {"allOf":[{"type":"integer"}],"$ref":"#/allOf/0"} on "x" = 1 error in d3-7 but 2 in 2019/2020 (sibling allOf also runs).
- "#/dependencies/q/0": WORKS in all six (dependencies values may legitimately be arrays of names).
- draft-03 "extends" is treated as an ARRAY-of-schemas slot, so an OBJECT-valued extends crashes any crawl with AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get' (it iterates the dict's string keys). Validation itself is unaffected until a URI/anchor lookup happens; a pointer "#/extends" or "#/extends/0" works.

=== 10. OTHER FAILURE MODES (all exit 1, EMPTY stdout) ===
All resolution failures are hard crashes, never validation errors. Exception classes seen (last traceback line):
- jsonschema.exceptions._WrappedReferencingError: PointerToNowhere: '<ptr>' does not exist within {<repr of the resource the pointer was resolved against>}.
- _WrappedReferencingError: Unresolvable: <uri> — http://example.com/x, https://example.com/x#/foo, urn:uuid:..., file:///etc/passwd, "nope", "other.json", "/$defs/a" (a ref with a leading slash but no '#'), "//example.com/x", "?q", ".", and any $id-relative miss. NO network I/O is ever attempted (an unresolvable http ref fails in ~0.37 s).
- _WrappedReferencingError: NoSuchAnchor: '<name>' does not exist within {<root schema repr>}.
- _WrappedReferencingError: InvalidAnchor: '<ref>' is not a valid anchor, neither as a plain name anchor nor as a JSON Pointer. You may have forgotten... — NEW: raised for "#$defs/a" and "##/$defs/a" (a fragment that is neither empty, nor starting with '/', nor a syntactically valid plain name).
- RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded (see §3).
- ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '-' for "#/anyOf/-" (unwrapped).
- AttributeError: 'int'/'NoneType'/'bool'/'list'/'dict' object has no attribute 'startswith' when $ref is not a string (raised before any resolution).
- AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'rstrip' when $id is not a string.
- AttributeError: 'list'/'str' object has no attribute 'get' — see §9.
- Ref target that is not a schema: a STRING or LIST target reached outside a crawled slot => AttributeError: 'str'/'list' object has no attribute 'items' (raised by iter_errors), e.g. {"$ref":"#/title","title":"t"}, {"$ref":"#/enum","enum":[1,2]}, {"$ref":"#/$defs/a/$ref",...}. A NUMBER target => TypeError: argument of type 'int' is not iterable (raised by the "$ref" in schema membership test), e.g. {"$ref":"#/minLength","minLength":5}. A NULL target inside a CRAWLED slot ({"$defs":{"a":null},"$ref":"#/$defs/a"} in 2020-12) => AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'; a null reached outside a crawled slot gives TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable. So which of the three exceptions you get depends on whether the final pointer segment lands in a slot the draft crawls.
- BOOLEAN targets: {"definitions":{"a":false},"$ref":"#/definitions/a"} => draft-06/07/2019/2020 False/1 and true => True/0, but draft-03 and draft-04 CRASH with TypeError: argument of type 'bool' is not iterable (no boolean-schema support). A boolean ROOT schema is fine in the default (2020-12) dialect: schema true => True/0, schema false => False/1.
- Object-but-not-schema target is fine: {"definitions":{"a":{"type":"integer"}},"$ref":"#/definitions"} resolves to {"a":{...}}, only unknown keywords => True/0.

=== 11. SUBRESOURCE $schema SWITCHES DIALECT (major, previously unprobed) ===
A subschema that carries its OWN "$schema" is processed under THAT dialect, for both identification and validation, even though the printed validator class is the ROOT's. {"$schema":draft-07,"definitions":{"a":{"$id":"http://x/a","$schema":2020-12,"prefixItems":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"string"}]}},"properties":{"p":{"$ref":"http://x/a"}}} on {"p":[1,"x"]} prints Draft7Validator / False / 1 — prefixItems WAS applied; drop the inner $schema and the same schema prints True/0 (prefixItems ignored under draft-07). The $ref-sibling suppression rule also follows the SUBRESOURCE dialect: a subresource {"$id":"http://x/a","$schema":draft-07,"$ref":...,"minLength":99} inside a 2020-12 root becomes Unresolvable: http://x/a, because draft-07 semantics suppress that subresource's own $id. Likewise a subresource with "$schema":draft-04 but an "$id" key is Unresolvable (draft-04 wants "id"). A "$schema" in a subschema WITHOUT an $id is harmless. Key order inside the subresource ($schema before or after $id) does not matter.

=== 12. unevaluatedProperties / unevaluatedItems ACROSS $ref (2019-09 & 2020-12 only) ===
Unknown/ignored in draft-03/04/06/07 (always True/0 there). In 2019-09 and 2020-12 annotations DO propagate across a $ref, both as a direct sibling and through allOf: {"$ref":"#/$defs/a","$defs":{"a":{"properties":{"x":true}}},"unevaluatedProperties":false} on {"x":1} => True/0 (x was evaluated by the ref target), and on {"x":1,"y":2} => False/1. COUNTING: unevaluatedProperties emits exactly ONE top-level error no matter how many properties are unevaluated ({"x":1,"y":2,"z":3} with unevaluatedProperties:false => 1; with unevaluatedProperties:{"type":"string"} => 1). unevaluatedItems likewise emits exactly 1.

=== 13. META-SCHEMA REFS ARE FULLY OFFLINE — EXACT RESOLVABLE SET ===
No network is ever attempted. RESOLVE: http://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema#, draft-04/schema#, draft-06/schema#, draft-07/schema# (trailing '#' optional), https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema, https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema (trailing '#' also fine), and the vocabulary metas https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/meta/{core,applicator,validation,unevaluated,format-annotation,content,meta-data} and https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/meta/{core,applicator,validation,format}. UNRESOLVABLE (exit 1): the unversioned http://json-schema.org/schema# and https://json-schema.org/schema#; ANY scheme/host swap — https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#, https://json-schema.org/draft-06/schema#, http://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema; http://json-schema.org/draft-05/schema#; every hyper-schema (draft-07/hyper-schema#, 2019-09/meta/hyper-schema, 2020-12/hyper-schema).
ERROR COUNTS against metas (independent of the outer document's $schema — "x" vs the 2019-09 meta gives 7 whether the root declares draft-03 or 2020-12): instance "x" vs draft-03/04/06/07 meta => 1 each; vs 2019-09 meta => 7; vs 2020-12 meta => 8 (each allOf $ref to a meta/* vocabulary yields one top-level error, plus the type error). Instance 5 vs 2020-12 meta => 8. Instance {} vs 2020-12 meta => True/0; {} vs 2020-12 meta/applicator => True/0. {"type":"string"} vs draft-07 meta => True/0; {"type":"bogus"} => 1; {"type":"bogus","minLength":"x"} => 2; {"minimum":"x","maxLength":-1,"type":1} => 3. {"type":"bogus"} vs draft-04 meta => 1.
POINTERS INTO METAS work where the target exists: draft-07/schema#/definitions/nonNegativeInteger (-5 => 1, 5 => 0), draft-07/schema#/definitions/simpleTypes ("x" => 1), draft-07/schema#/properties/type, draft-04/schema#/definitions/positiveInteger, draft-03/schema#/properties/type ("x" => True/0), 2020-12/meta/validation#/$defs/nonNegativeInteger, 2020-12/meta/core#/$defs/anchorString ("x" => True/0, "#abc" => 1 error since anchorString forbids the '#'). But 2020-12/schema#/$defs/nonNegativeInteger and 2019-09/meta/core#/$defs/anchorString are PointerToNowhere, and the exception message dumps the whole meta-schema dict.

=== 14. REFS IN APPLICATOR POSITIONS (counting) ===
Refs under properties, items (single and array form), prefixItems, additionalProperties, patternProperties, propertyNames, contains, dependencies (draft-04..draft-07 only), dependentSchemas, allOf all bubble their target's errors to top level one-for-one. Measured: 2 properties each failing = 2; array with 2 bad elements = 2; items:[ref,ref] on 2 bad elements = 2 (d4/d6/d7/2019); prefixItems:[ref,ref] = 2 (2020-12); allOf with a 3-failure target = 3; contains whose ref fails for every element = 1; 2020-12 prefixItems + sibling $ref-to-items = 2. "dependencies" with a SCHEMA value is silently IGNORED in 2019-09/2020-12 (True/0) — use dependentSchemas there. if/then/else with refs: an if-failure is never an error, so {"if":{$ref fails},"then":{$ref},"else":{$ref}} = 1 error total.

=== 15. JS-REIMPLEMENTER TRAPS observed through refs ===
Numbers: JSON 1.0 and 1 are EQUAL for const/enum and 1.0 satisfies "type":"integer" (Python float-is-integral rule); 1e2 == 100; -0 == 0 for const in both directions. Booleans are NOT numbers: true fails const 1, true fails enum [1,"x"], 1 fails enum [true], true fails "type":"integer". Strings: length is in Unicode CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 units — "😀" fails minLength 2 and passes maxLength 1 (a naive JS .length gives 2). Regex is PYTHON re, applied with re.search (unanchored): pattern "^a" does NOT match "xa" (^ is string-start), "." does NOT match "\n" (no DOTALL), and "$" matches BEFORE a trailing newline so "a\n" MATCHES "^a$" (JS would reject). Object keys: duplicate JSON keys are resolved by Python json.loads with LAST-WINS ({"$ref":A,"$ref":B} uses B; a duplicated "$defs" uses the second). Keyword iteration order = JSON key insertion order (§2). Keyword names are case-sensitive: "$Ref" is an unknown keyword (True/0). "$vocabulary" is completely IGNORED — declaring the validation vocabulary false in 2019-09 does not disable minLength/type (still 2 errors).
gotchas: Percent-decoding of a pointer fragment happens BEFORE splitting on '/' and BEFORE ~1/~0 unescaping, and only ONCE. So %2F/%2f becomes a real path SEPARATOR (#/$defs/a%2Fb navigates $defs->a->b, it does not find the key 'a/b'), and %7E1 becomes ~1 which then becomes '/'. %2520 is not double-decoded. Plain-name anchor fragments are NOT percent-decoded at all: $anchor 'a b' is found by '#a b' but NOT by '#a%20b'.

draft-03/04/06/07: ANY sibling of $ref is ignored — validation keywords AND $id/id. 2019-09/2020-12: siblings are applied and each yields its own top-level errors, and they are evaluated in JSON key insertion order (so {"$ref":X,"not":[...]} and {"not":[...],"$ref":X} crash with two DIFFERENT AttributeErrors, 'get' vs 'items'). {"$ref":X,"required":["q","r"]} on {} = 1 error in draft-7 but 3 in 2020-12 (required emits one error per missing key).

Because $id is suppressed by a sibling $ref in draft 3/4/6/7, a ROOT of the form {"$id":"http://x/","$ref":...} loses its base URI: $ref "http://x/b" is Unresolvable while relative $ref "b" resolves. Moving the $ref into properties/allOf restores it. 2019-09/2020-12 never do this. Anchors registered under the empty base still resolve either way.

A subschema carrying its own "$schema" is processed under THAT dialect for both id resolution and validation, while the printed validator class stays the root's. prefixItems inside a 2020-12-tagged subresource IS applied under a Draft7Validator root; a draft-04-tagged subresource with "$id" becomes Unresolvable; a draft-07-tagged subresource with a sibling $ref loses its own $id.

$id/$anchor discovery only crawls slots the draft knows, and the matrix is not what you'd guess: 'definitions' is crawled in ALL SIX drafts (including draft-03/04 and 2019/2020); '$defs' is crawled ONLY in 2019-09/2020-12; 'prefixItems' only in 2020-12; 'dependentSchemas' only in 2019/2020; 'contains' in draft-06+; 'then' in draft-07+; unknown keywords never. Plain pointer refs like '#/$defs/a' still work in every draft — pointer resolution is purely structural.

A pointer that walks through an ARRAY sitting in a slot the draft treats as a single schema crashes with AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'. #/definitions/a/0, #/properties/p/0, #/patternProperties/^p/0 and #/additionalProperties/0 crash in ALL SIX drafts; #/$defs/a/0 crashes only in 2019/2020; #/items/0 crashes only in 2020-12; #/contains/0 crashes in draft-06+; #/not/0 crashes in draft-04+; #/prefixItems/0, #/anyOf/0, #/allOf/0 and #/dependencies/q/0 never crash. Worse, ANY non-pointer ref (a URI or an anchor, even one that will fail) forces a full document crawl and hits the bad slot even if the pointer never touches it — {"items":[...],"allOf":[{"$ref":"http://nope/"}]} crashes in 2020-12 instead of reporting Unresolvable.

Array index segments go through Python int(): '#/anyOf/00' resolves, '#/anyOf/-1' resolves to the LAST element (negative indexing!), '#/anyOf/1' on a 1-element list is PointerToNowhere, and '#/anyOf/-' raises a bare ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '-'.

Every resolution failure is a hard crash (exit 1, EMPTY stdout, traceback) rather than a validation error: PointerToNowhere, Unresolvable, NoSuchAnchor and InvalidAnchor (all wrapped as jsonschema.exceptions._WrappedReferencingError), plus RecursionError for loops. InvalidAnchor is the one for a fragment that is neither empty, nor pointer-shaped, nor a valid plain name — e.g. '#$defs/a' or '##/$defs/a'.

{"$ref":"#"} or {"$ref":""} at the ROOT loops forever => RecursionError in every draft, as do self/mutual $defs loops and {"$id":"http://x/root","allOf":[{"$ref":"http://x/root"}]}. Instance-guarded recursion terminates but has a ceiling: depth 240 nested objects through a $ref is fine, depth 260 is a RecursionError. Long non-recursive ref CHAINS (400 links) are fine.

No network is ever attempted and the resolvable meta-schema set is exact: draft-03/04/06/07 http URIs, 2019-09 and 2020-12 https URIs, plus 2020-12 meta/{core,applicator,validation,unevaluated,format-annotation,content,meta-data} and 2019-09 meta/{core,applicator,validation,format}. Every scheme swap (https draft-07, http 2020-12), draft-05, the unversioned .../schema#, and every hyper-schema are Unresolvable.

Error counts against metas are large, specific, and independent of the outer $schema: instance "x" vs draft-03/04/06/07 meta = 1 each, vs 2019-09 meta = 7, vs 2020-12 meta = 8. Instance 5 vs 2020-12 meta = 8. Instance {} vs 2020-12 meta = 0.

$recursiveRef/$recursiveAnchor exist ONLY in 2019-09; $dynamicRef/$dynamicAnchor ONLY in 2020-12; elsewhere they are unknown keywords silently ignored (True/0). Real dynamic-scope resolution IS implemented (the strict-tree test catches a typo'd grandchild property). In 2019-09 the $recursiveRef fragment is IGNORED — '#/$defs/a' and '#nope' both behave like '#'. Omitting $recursiveAnchor still resolves to the base root. $dynamicRef without a leading '#' is Unresolvable; with a pointer fragment it acts as an ordinary pointer.

In 2020-12 a $dynamicAnchor also registers as a plain anchor ($ref '#n' finds it) and $dynamicRef will bind to a plain $anchor, including one nested in $defs. Anchor NAMES are never validated: '1bad', 'a-b', 'a.b', 'a/b', 'a b' and '' all register fine; only a non-string $anchor fails to register.

Ref targets that are not schemas crash in three different ways depending on whether the target sits in a crawled slot: str/list target => AttributeError ... has no attribute 'items'; int target => TypeError: argument of type 'int' is not iterable; null inside a crawled slot ($defs in 2020-12) => AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'. A non-string $ref => AttributeError ... has no attribute 'startswith'; a non-string $id => AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'rstrip'.

Boolean ref targets work in draft-06+ (false => 1 error, true => 0) but crash draft-03/draft-04 with TypeError: argument of type 'bool' is not iterable. A boolean ROOT schema is fine (true => True/0, false => False/1).

unevaluatedProperties/unevaluatedItems annotations DO cross a $ref boundary in 2019-09/2020-12 (both as a direct sibling and via allOf), and each emits exactly ONE top-level error no matter how many members are unevaluated. Both keywords are unknown and ignored in draft-03/04/06/07.

'dependencies' with a SCHEMA value is silently ignored in 2019-09/2020-12 (True/0) but applies in draft-04/06/07. '$vocabulary' is completely ignored — setting the validation vocabulary to false does not disable minLength/type.

URI comparison has NO case normalization: $id "HTTP://X/" is not matched by $ref "http://x/". Duplicate $id registrations are silently accepted. URNs work as bases, including relative sub-$ids resolved against them.

draft-03 'extends' is treated as an ARRAY-of-schemas slot by the resolver, so an object-valued extends makes any URI/anchor lookup crash with AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get' (it iterates the dict's string keys); pointers into it still work.

Python json.loads semantics leak through: duplicate JSON keys resolve LAST-WINS (a schema literally containing two "$ref" keys uses the second). Keyword names are case-sensitive ($Ref is unknown). $ref strings are never trimmed: "  #/$defs/a  " looks for key "a  ".
